- **14 unit tests** (`integrationRequests.test.ts`) — TOML CRUD operations against real filesystem

title: refactor: migrate deployment record TOML handling from Go API to TypeScript
description:
## Intent

Migrate deployment/content record TOML file operations (read, create, patch, list) from the Go HTTP API to direct TypeScript file operations in the extension. This follows the same pattern established by the prior configuration TOML migration and is part of the broader effort to reduce dependency on the Go backend for file-based operations.

Publishing, canceling deployments, and fetching environment variables remain in Go.

Fixes #3702 

## Type of Change

- - [x] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->

## Approach

**Phase 1: Rename config-specific files** — Renamed existing `src/toml/` files (e.g., `loader.ts` → `configLoader.ts`) to make room for deployment equivalents.

**Phase 2: Extract shared utilities** — Moved `readLeadingComments`, `stripEmpty`, `isRecord`, `relativeProjectDir`, and `formatValidationErrors` into `tomlHelpers.ts` for use by both config and deployment modules.

**Phase 3: Type reconciliation** — Added `logsUrl` to `PreContentRecord`, added `RenvLockfile`/`RenvPackage`/`RenvRepository` types, and `requirements`/`renv` fields to `ContentRecord` so the TypeScript types match what the Go backend writes to TOML.

**Phase 4: Deployment TOML loader** (`deploymentLoader.ts`) — Reads TOML, validates against the JSON schema (with `$ref` resolution for the embedded config schema), converts keys to camelCase, computes `logsUrl` default, determines state (`NEW` vs `DEPLOYED`) based on `deployedAt`.

**Phase 5: Deployment TOML writer** (`deploymentWriter.ts`) — `createDeploymentRecord` creates new deployment files; `patchDeploymentRecord` patches existing ones (config name or content ID). Both validate config existence and compute Connect URLs.

**Phase 6: Deployment discovery** (`deploymentDiscovery.ts`) — `loadDeployment`, `loadAllDeployments`, `loadAllDeploymentsRecursive` for finding and loading deployments from disk. `loadAllDeploymentsRecursive` takes `(startDir, rootDir)` to support scoped walks.

**Phase 7-8: Update callers** — Replaced all `api.contentRecords.get/getAll/createNew/patch` calls with the new TypeScript functions in `state.ts`, `homeView.ts`, `showAssociateGUID.ts`, and `newDeployment.ts`. Updated `state.test.ts` to mock the new TOML functions instead of the API client. Only `api.contentRecords.getEnv` remains on the Go API.

**Phase 9-10: Remove Go APIs** — Deleted 9 Go handler/test files (GET/POST /deployments, GET/PATCH /deployments/{name}) and their route registrations. Removed corresponding `getAll`, `get`, `createNew`, `patch` methods from the TypeScript API client. Only `publish`, `cancelDeployment`, and `getEnv` remain on the Go API.

**Trade-offs:**
- `patchDeploymentRecord` uses a denylist to strip computed fields before writing back to TOML (since TypeScript types mix TOML data with location metadata). This is fragile to new field additions but matches the pragmatic approach used elsewhere.
- Type assertions (`as ContentRecord`) are used in the loader after schema validation, consistent with the config loader pattern.

## User Impact

No user-visible changes. Deployment TOML operations now happen directly in the extension process instead of going through the Go HTTP API, which should be slightly faster and removes a class of potential HTTP communication failures.

## Automated Tests

- **`deploymentLoader.test.ts`** — 13 tests: pre-deployment, full deployment, Connect Cloud, logsUrl computation, error handling, renv, embedded config, minimal records
- **`deploymentWriter.test.ts`** — 11 tests: create, cloud, content ID, conflict detection, config validation, clientVersion, patch operations
- **`deploymentDiscovery.test.ts`** — 14 tests: path helpers, listing, loading, recursive walk, skip rules
- **`state.test.ts`** — Updated to mock `loadDeployment` instead of `api.contentRecords.get`, with ENOENT/error handling tests

All 434 unit tests pass. Lint clean. Full `just` build passes.

## Directions for Reviewers

1. Start with `src/toml/index.ts` for the public API surface

title: Fix flaky open-connect-content e2e test
description:
## Summary

Fixes the flaky `open-connect-content` e2e test that was failing across multiple Connect versions (preview, release, 2023.03.0, 2025.03.0).

### Root cause

The `ConnectContentFileSystemProvider` was **blocking VS Code's workspace validation** during the workspace switch. When `updateWorkspaceFolders` is called, code-server validates the new folder by calling `stat()` and `readDirectory()` on the root URI. Our implementation awaited the full bundle fetch pipeline (Go backend startup → credential refresh → Connect API call → tar extraction) before responding. This caused code-server to silently reject the workspace change because the validation timed out.

Additionally, in code-server, `updateWorkspaceFolders` creates a **multi-root workspace** where the content folder appears at `aria-level="2"` instead of `aria-level="1"`, so the test's CSS selector was missing the GUID entirely.

### Extension fixes (`connect_content_fs.ts`)

- **Non-blocking `stat()` for root URIs**: Returns an immediate directory entry without waiting for the bundle fetch. The bundle is kicked off in the background.
- **Non-blocking `readDirectory()` for root URIs**: Returns whatever is cached (or `[]` if nothing yet), then fires a `FileChangeType.Changed` event when the bundle fetch completes to trigger VS Code to refresh the explorer tree.
- **Non-blocking error handling**: `showErrorMessage` and the credential dialog are fire-and-forget (`void`) instead of `await`ed, so they don't stall the filesystem provider.

### Test fixes (`open-connect-content.cy.js`)

- Removed `aria-level='1'` restriction from the GUID selector — matches the folder at any tree depth to handle both single-folder and multi-root workspace modes.
- Added notification toast dismissal during polling.
- Increased `waitUntil` timeout to 120s.
- Added explorer DOM diagnostics to the error message for easier debugging of future failures.

## Test plan

- [x] All 4 e2e matrix variants pass (preview, release, 2023.03.0, 2025.03.0)
- [x] Unit tests pass (18/18) including new error-handling coverage
- [x] Lint and formatting clean

## Intent

## Approach

Created a standalone `packages/connect-api/` package with a `ConnectAPI` class that wraps the Posit Connect REST API. All 15 API methods are implemented:

- **Auth & User**: `testAuthentication`, `getCurrentUser`
- **Content CRUD**: `contentDetails`, `createDeployment`, `updateDeployment`
- **Environment**: `getEnvVars`, `setEnvVars`
- **Bundles**: `uploadBundle`, `latestBundleId`, `downloadBundle`

- **axios** for HTTP — uses `axios.create()` with a pre-configured `baseURL` and default `Authorization` header. Each method calls `this.client.request<T>()` directly with response generics for strong typing.
- **Default axios error handling** — non-2xx responses throw `AxiosError` automatically. No custom error classes. Two methods use per-request `validateStatus` overrides: `testAuthentication` (inspects error response bodies for messages) and `validateDeployment` (accepts non-5xx status codes).
- **Raw API responses** — every method returns the exact JSON the Connect API sends back (full DTOs), rather than constructing new objects or extracting single fields. The contract test adapter handles any field extraction needed.
- **Branded ID types** (`ContentID`, `BundleID`, `TaskID`) for type safety on parameters

title: Migrate /api/interpreters endpoint from Go to TypeScript
description:
## Summary

Move interpreter detection (Python/R version, lockfiles, package managers) from the Go backend API into a new TypeScript module in the VSCode extension. This eliminates the HTTP round-trip to the Go process for logic that can run directly in TypeScript using `child_process`.

- Add `src/interpreters/` module with Python and R detection, version constraint parsing, and project metadata reading (`.python-version`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`)
- Replace `api.interpreters.get()` calls in `state.ts` with `getInterpreterDefaults()`
- Remove `GET /api/interpreters` Go endpoint and route registration
- Remove `Interpreters` API resource class from TypeScript client
- Add 74 unit tests covering all new modules

## How requiresPython / requiresR worked in the Go implementation

In the Go backend, the `Python` and `R` config structs in `internal/config/types.go` each had a `FillDefaults()` method that was called with an interpreter instance. The flow was:

1. **`Python.FillDefaults(pythonInterpreter)`** — if `RequiresPythonVersion` was empty, called `python.GetPythonRequires()`, which searched `.python-version` → `pyproject.toml` → `setup.cfg` in order.
2. **`R.FillDefaults(rInterpreter)`** — if `RequiresRVersion` was empty, called `rLang.GetRRequires()`, which searched `DESCRIPTION` → `renv.lock` in order.

The key difference is that in Go, `FillDefaults` was called on the config struct itself — it mutated the config in place. The interpreters were Go objects already constructed with the project directory and executable path, and `GetPythonRequires()` / `GetRRequires()` were methods on those interpreter objects.

In the TypeScript migration, this is now handled in two places:

- **`detectPythonInterpreter` / `detectRInterpreter`** — call `getPythonRequires()` / `getRRequires()` and include the result in the returned config.
- **`UpdateConfigWithDefaults`** in `configurations.ts` — fills in empty fields on the config, same as `FillDefaults` did in Go.

## Go components intentionally retained

The following Go interpreter code is **not removed** by this PR because it is still used by other backend endpoints:

| Component | Used by |
|-----------|---------|
| `InterpretersFromRequest()` in `api_helpers.go` | `POST /api/deployment` (post_deployment.go), `POST /api/inspect` (post_inspect.go), `POST /api/packages/r/scan` (post_packages_r_scan.go) |
| `internal/interpreters/` package (Python/R interpreter structs, version detection, requires parsing) | `InterpretersFromRequest`, `config.Python.FillDefaults()`, `config.R.FillDefaults()`, bundle manifest generation |
| `config.Python.FillDefaults()` / `config.R.FillDefaults()` in `internal/config/types.go` | Server-side config population during deployment and inspection |

These can be migrated in follow-up work as their consuming endpoints are moved to TypeScript.

## Type of Change

- [x] Refactor

## Approach

Ported the interpreter detection logic from Go to TypeScript, matching the existing behavior:
- Python version via `python -E -c "import sys; ..."` with pyenv shim cache bypass
- R version via `R --version` with combined stdout/stderr parsing
- renv lockfile resolution via `renv::paths$lockfile()` with fallback to default `renv.lock`
- Version constraint adaptation (PEP 440 operators, compatible release `~=`)
- Project metadata parsing for Python requires (`.python-version`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`) and R requires (`DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`)

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior change. Interpreter detection now runs in-process in the extension instead of making an HTTP call to the Go backend.

## Automated Tests

74 new Vitest unit tests across 6 test files covering:
- Version constraint adaptation (28 tests)
- Python requires parsing (10 tests)
- R requires parsing (10 tests)
- Python interpreter detection (9 tests)
- R interpreter detection (11 tests)
- `getInterpreterDefaults()` public API (6 tests)

32 integration tests in `integration.test.ts` that run against:
- A real temporary filesystem (created with `mkdtemp`, cleaned up after)
- Real Python and R executables when available on PATH

Tests are organized in layers from low-level to high-level:
1. `fsUtils` — filesystem helpers
2. `getPythonRequires` / `getRRequires` — version constraint extraction from project files
3. `detectPythonInterpreter` / `detectRInterpreter` — full detection with real executables
4. End-to-end tests — detection + project files combined
5. `getInterpreterDefaults` — top-level orchestrator for both interpreters

Tests that require a specific interpreter use `test.skipIf(!available)` so the suite runs in any environment. In CI, `interpreter-integration.yaml` installs known Python and R versions across a 12-configuration matrix (Python 3.9–3.13, R 4.1–4.4, combined, cross-platform).

### E2E coverage

No new E2E tests are needed. The existing deployment E2E tests (`deployments.cy.js`, `embedded-deployments.cy.js`) implicitly validate this migration — they open real Python and R projects, wait for interpreter detection via `waitForInterpreterReady()`, and deploy to Connect. If interpreter detection regressed (wrong version, missing lockfile, bad package manager), those deployments would fail.

This migration changes internal plumbing (HTTP call to Go → direct `child_process` execution), not the inputs or outputs. The sidebar displays the same data and configurations receive the same defaults, so the existing E2E suite covers the end-to-end behavior without modification.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have updated the _root_ [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

title: refactor: read and write config toml in TypeScript
description:
## Intent

Migrate configuration reading and writing from Go API calls to a pure TypeScript toml module in the VSCode extension. This removes three HTTP round-trips to the Go backend for operations that only need local file I/O, and moves us toward reducing the extension's dependency on the Go subprocess.

Fixes #3651 
Fixes #3652 
Fixes #3653 

## Type of Change

- [x] Refactor
- [x] Bug fix (schema misspelling) 

## Approach

Updated type definitions and the schema to match current behavior:

- Consolidated TS types to match Go and schema (remove dead types/fields, add missing ones)
- Removed dead Go types (Schedule, AccessType, ConnectAccessControl) and unreachable code in content.go
- Fixed schema: auth_type in integration_requests (was camelCase), add additionalProperties: false to integration_requests items

Added a new `src/toml/` module with seven files:

- **errors.ts** — `ConfigurationLoadError` class and error factory functions
- **convertKeys.ts** — Bidirectional snake_case ↔ camelCase key conversion, preserving user-defined keys in `environment` and `integration_requests[].config`
- **compliance.ts** — Port of Go's `ForceProductTypeCompliance()` for Connect Cloud
- **loader.ts** — Reads TOML, validates against the JSON schema (using ajv), applies defaults
- **writer.ts** — Validates, converts to snake_case, strips empty leaf values, writes TOML
- **discovery.ts** — File discovery (`listConfigFiles`), single/batch/recursive loading, path resolution
- **validate.ts** — Shared setup for TOML validator function

The public API surface is five exports: `loadConfiguration`, `loadAllConfigurations`, `loadAllConfigurationsRecursive`, `writeConfigToFile`, and `ConfigurationLoadError`. Internal helpers stay exported on their source files for intra-module use and tests, but are not re-exported from the barrel.

All functions that produce `Configuration` objects accept `(projectDir, rootDir)` where `projectDir` is relative (e.g., `"."` or `"subdir"`) and `rootDir` is the absolute workspace root. Path resolution to absolute paths for file I/O happens inside the module. This matches the Go convention where `ProjectDirFromRequest` resolves relative `dir` parameters against the workspace base.

After replacing all callsites, the three Go API handlers (`GET /configurations`, `GET /configurations/{name}`, `PUT /configurations/{name}`) and their tests were deleted. The shared `configDTO`/`configLocation` types remain as they're used by other endpoints.

A copy of the JSON schema is bundled at `src/toml/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json`, identical to the Go source of truth. A comment in the schema test notes the need to keep them in sync.

**Key design decisions:**
- No intermediate store — callsites call toml functions directly
- Writer returns the written `Configuration` — no write-then-read round-trip
- Loader throws on error; discovery functions catch and collect errors for the UI
- `src/toml/` has no vscode imports — it's pure Node.js
- `stripEmpty` only removes leaf values (undefined, null, empty strings), never parent objects, because the schema conditionally requires section headers like `[r]` even when all fields are empty

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior change. Configuration reading and writing now happens directly in the extension process instead of through HTTP calls to the Go backend.

## Automated Tests

[ed: there's probably more now, I've made some improvements since ]

a bunch of new tests in `src/toml/`:
- Key conversion (19 tests) — snake/camel round-trip, preservation of user-defined keys
- Schema validation (32 tests) — validates the bundled JSON schema against known valid/invalid configs
- Loader (19 tests) — happy path, TOML parse errors, schema errors, defaults, comments, business rules
- Writer (14 tests) — round-trip fidelity, snake_case output, comments, stripEmpty, compliance, unknown type handling, empty section preservation
- Discovery (22 tests) — file listing, single/batch/recursive loading, relative projectDir, error collection, skip rules
- Compliance (13 tests) — cleanup and field modifications based on target product (connect or cloud)
- Errors (13 tests) — error factories and formatting of validation error messages

Existing `state.test.ts` tests were rewritten to mock the toml module instead of the API client.

## Directions for Reviewers

I recommend reading through the new `toml/` directory first and then reviewing the updates to the extension code.

I am working my way through these manual tests:

- [x] Open workspace with existing config — sidebar loads, no errors
- [x] Open workspace with configs in a subdirectory — configs discovered and selectable
- [x] Open workspace with no configs — loads cleanly
- [x] Open workspace with malformed .toml — config shows error state, no crash
- [x] Select a deployment — config loads, files/packages/secrets populate (no 404s)
- [x] Open config dropdown — shows configs matching current entrypoint
- [x] New deployment for Python app — config created with `[python]` section, snake_case keys
- [x] New deployment for R Shiny app — config created with `[r]` section, no schema error
- [x] Re-associate: select existing config — config list loads
- [x] Re-associate: create new config — file written, deployment uses it
- [x] Subdirectory project — all above work, no absolute paths in debug console

## Checklist

- [x] I have updated the _root_ [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

yes, only for the auth_type schema fix. The rest should not be user-facing.

title: fix: derive expected extension version from VSIX filename instead of git tags
description:
## Summary

- Fixes a race condition causing E2E CI failures on main when a release PR merges
- The install-positron-extension script was using `git describe --tags` to determine the expected installed version, but this races with the `tag-on-release-merge` workflow that creates the version tag concurrently
- Now derives the expected version from the actual VSIX filename, which always reflects what `set-version.py` produced during the build

## Root cause

When a release PR merges to main, two workflows trigger simultaneously:
1. `main.yaml` — builds the VSIX (before the tag exists, so version is e.g. `1.35.6-4-g16bde683`, and `set-version.py` leaves package.json at `99.0.0`)
2. `tag-on-release-merge.yaml` — creates the `v1.35.7` tag

By the time the E2E install script runs (with `fetch-depth: 0`), it picks up the newly-created tag and expects version `1.35.7`, but the extension was installed as `99.0.0`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify the E2E `install-positron-extension` step passes on this PR's CI run
- [ ] Confirm no regression on non-release builds (version should resolve to `99.0.0`)

title: feat: sync credentials to SecretStorage
description:
Migrates credentials from the Go keyring storage to VS Code's `SecretStorage`.

It does this on every credential refresh which occurs when viewing the Publisher sidebar for the first time, on creation, and deletion.

When we swap to `SecretStorage` only this will prevent any users who used Publisher during the time when this syncing / migration occurred from needing to recreate their credentials.

## Intent

Resolves #3635

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

All create, delete, and load paths go through `refreshCredentials()` so that is where the `SecretStorage` sync was setup - `syncAllCredentials()`.

Similar to the Go backend each credential is wrapping in a versioning envelope like `{ version: 1, credential: {...} }` so it is easy for us to change them in the future.

The credentials are stored with the `credential:{guid}` key.

The credentials are not used yet, the Go backend is still handling the actual credentials used to make API calls to Connect and Connect Cloud.

## User Impact

No changes yet.

This prepares us for a future release where the Go code is removed.

## Automated Tests

New unit tests were added covering the new functionality.

## Directions for Reviewers

I tested manually in Workbench by installing the `vsix` file created in CI.

I was able to confirm that credentials were synced to `SecretStorage` via the Posit Publisher output:

> 2026-03-04 19:28:17.165 [info] Synced 1 credentials to SecretStorage

Positron and VS Code use Electron's [`safeStorage`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/safe-storage) which has fallbacks for different OS cryptography systems falling back if there is no secret store for the OS.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have updated the _root_ [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

I didn't update the CHANGELOG since this is not user facing yet.

title: simplify e2e tests to static-only content and single Connect version
description:
## Summary

Reduce CI matrix from 4 Connect versions to 1 (release), switch all deployments to static HTML only, and remove unused content types (FastAPI, Shiny Python, Quarto, R) and their associated test specs. Backfill removed E2E coverage with targeted unit tests.

## Intent

The E2E test suite tested multiple content types against 4 Connect Server versions, creating a large CI matrix and slow runs. Content-type testing arguably belongs in Connect's own test suite rather than Publisher's. This PR simplifies to static HTML only against one Connect version, while preserving PCC, Workbench, and Positron coverage.

## Type of Change

- [x] Refactor
- [x] Tooling

## Approach

### E2E Simplification

- Remove 3 spec files: `embedded-deployments`, `error-err-config`, `open-connect-content`
- Remove 5 content directories and root-level Python files, keeping only `static/`
- Switch PCC deployment test from Shiny Python to static HTML
- Remove Playwright publish verification (`publish-success-task.js`)
- Remove conditional `@pcc` tag filtering in CI (always run all tests)
- Clean up skipped ShinyApp tests in deployments and positron specs
- Reduce CI matrix from 4 Connect versions to 1 (`release`)

### Unit Test Backfill

Added unit tests to cover the key gaps left by removed E2E specs:

**Go: Subdirectory path handling** (`internal/bundles/bundle_test.go`, `internal/config/config_test.go`, `internal/initialize/initialize_test.go`)
- Bundle from subdirectory only includes that directory's files with correct relative paths; workspace root files are excluded
- File-targeted bundling in a subdirectory resolves baseDir to the file's parent
- `GetConfigPath`, `WriteFile`/`FromFile`, and `ListConfigFiles` all scope correctly to a subdirectory project
- `GetPossibleConfigs` detects content type in a subdirectory, sets correct entrypoint/files, and defaults title to subdirectory name

**Vue: Config error state detection** (`extensions/vscode/webviews/homeView/src/stores/home.test.ts`)
- `isMissing`: config file not found (deleted)
- `isTOMLError`: `invalidTOML` and `unknownTOMLKey` errors (the exact scenario from the deleted `error-err-config` E2E)
- `isUnknownError`: non-TOML agent errors
- `isUnknownType`: config with `type = "unknown"`
- `isEntryMissing`: content record with no config name
- Happy path: all error states false for a valid configuration

## Net Result

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| 9 E2E spec files | 6 E2E spec files |
| 6 content directories + root files | 1 directory (`static/`) |
| 4 Connect versions in CI | 1 (`release`) |
| Playwright for OAuth + app verification | Playwright for OAuth only |
| PCC deploys Shiny Python | PCC deploys static HTML |
| ~36 test runs (9 specs × 4 versions) | ~6 test runs (6 specs × 1 version) |
| No subdirectory path unit tests | 7 new Go unit tests |
| 1 Vue store test | 9 Vue store tests (+8 for error states) |

## What's Preserved

- PCC credential creation (OAuth Device Code via Playwright)
- PCC deployment workflow (now with static HTML)
- PCC content cleanup (`deletePCCContent`)
- Workbench/Positron deployment (static HTML, unchanged)
- PCS credential CRUD
- PCS static deployment
- OAuth cancellation scenarios
- Integration Requests PCS vs PCC conditional UI

## Automated Tests

- 7 new Go unit tests across `bundles`, `config`, and `initialize` packages
- 8 new Vue store tests for config error state detection
- All existing Go and Vue tests pass

title: chore(deps): bump actions/download-artifact from 7 to 8
description:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to false.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

## Summary

- Inventory the Go API surface (46 REST endpoints + SSE) grouped by domain concept
- Map all extension API call sites — confirmed they're centralized in `src/api/resources/`
- Identify all external resources (Connect API, file system, credentials, interpreters, etc.)
- Assess the existing test suite for both Go and TypeScript
- Propose candidate domain groupings, port interfaces, and migration order
- Document open questions for team discussion before proceeding to Phase 3 (port interface design)

This is the Phase 1 output of a planned migration from the Go REST API backend to an in-process TypeScript core package using hexagonal architecture.

Reference implementation: https://github.com/christierney/hexatype

## Open questions (looking for feedback)

1. **SSE replacement** — How should the core report deployment progress?
2. **Credential storage** — VSCode SecretStorage vs. driven port with multiple adapters?
3. **Migration approach** — Option A (port interface boundary) vs. Option B (feature flag routing)?
4. **TOML handling** — Port concern or direct core dependency?
5. **Accounts vs. Credentials** — Distinct domain concept or derived view?

See `TS_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` for full details.

title: Migrate httputil.ReverseProxy from Director to Rewrite
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes a go deprecation that was introduced by go 1.26. Interestingly, it looks like there was never any test coverage for the proxy package, so this PR also adds test coverage we were missing. 


---

- Migrates from the deprecated `Director` field to the newer `Rewrite` function in `httputil.ReverseProxy`
- `Director` was deprecated in Go 1.26
- The `Rewrite` function provides cleaner separation between inbound and outbound requests via the `ProxyRequest` type
- Adds comprehensive test coverage for the proxy package (previously had none)

## Changes

- Replace `Director` field with `Rewrite` function
- Remove `baseProxy` intermediate proxy (no longer needed)
- Store `targetURL` as `*url.URL` instead of `string`
- Use `pr.SetURL()` for URL rewriting instead of calling base Director
- Inline `stripSourcePrefix` logic into `rewrite()` and `proxyURL()`

## Key Differences

| Aspect | Director (old) | Rewrite (new) |
|--------|----------------|---------------|
| Signature | `func(req *http.Request)` | `func(pr *httputil.ProxyRequest)` |
| Request access | Single `req` (clone) | `pr.In` (original), `pr.Out` (to modify) |
| URL rewriting | Call base `Director` | Use `pr.SetURL(targetURL)` |

## Test Coverage Added

Added 17 tests covering all proxy functionality:

| Test | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `TestBasicProxy` | Verifies requests are forwarded and responses returned |
| `TestPathStripping` | Verifies `sourcePath` is removed from request paths |
| `TestPathStrippingToRoot` | Verifies empty path becomes "/" |
| `TestQueryStringPreserved` | Verifies query parameters pass through |
| `TestCookiesStripped` | Verifies cookies are not forwarded (security) |
| `TestHostHeaderSet` | Verifies Host header is set to target |
| `TestRefererRewritten` | Verifies Referer header is rewritten |
| `TestRefererEmpty` | Handles missing Referer gracefully |
| `TestLocationHeaderRewritten` | Verifies redirect locations are rewritten |
| `TestLocationHeaderRelativeUnchanged` | Relative redirects pass through unchanged |
| `TestErrorHandler` | Verifies 502 on backend errors |
| `TestPostRequestBody` | Verifies POST bodies are forwarded |
| `TestProxyURL` | Tests the `proxyURL()` helper |
| `TestProxyURLWithQueryString` | Tests query string handling in helper |
| `TestProxyURLToRoot` | Tests root path mapping |
| `TestProxyURLInvalidURL` | Tests error handling for invalid URLs |
| `TestOtherHeadersPreserved` | Verifies non-cookie headers pass through |

## Test Plan

- [x] Code compiles successfully
- [x] Full test suite passes
- [x] New proxy tests pass (17/17)
- [ ] Manual testing of proxy functionality

Closes #3572

title: fix: resolve nightly test failures
description:
## Summary

Fixes two issues causing nightly test failures since Feb 20.

## Fixes

### 1. E2E: Fix `check-positron-extension.sh` version detection

PR #3577 fixed `install-positron-extension.sh` to use git-based version detection, but forgot to update `check-positron-extension.sh`. 

**Before:** Check script looked for `posit.publisher-99.0.0` (from package.json)
**After:** Check script now correctly looks for `posit.publisher-1.35.0` (from git tag)

The logic now matches the install script:
- Exact semver tags (e.g., `1.35.0`) → use tag version
- Non-release versions (e.g., `1.34.0-7-gabcdef`) → use `99.0.0`

### 2. Unit test: Fix flaky SSE log test race condition

`TestWatchLogsWithSSEServer` was failing intermittently with:
```
FAIL: 3 out of 4 expectation(s) were met.
```

**Root cause:** The test closed the `processed` channel on the 3rd mock call (Debug), but the 4th call (runtime Info) hadn't executed yet when `AssertExpectations` ran.

**Fix:** Moved `close(processed)` to the last expected call.

## Test plan

title: ci: add GitHub Actions security audit script
description:
## Summary

This is the result of working through a suggestion proposed by @dotNomad to capture some of the improvements we made to tidy up our github actions. Those best practices are things we want to continue to maintain moving forward, so this script helps us to mitigate drift over time. It also is something that we could probably apply to other repositories, if we can figure out the right set of validations here. 

I don't have any ideas on how often we want to run this, or where the results should live, or anything like that. But it does capture the work in a set of repeatable checks that we can kick off via a github action manually, which is nice. 


---

Adds a Python script to audit GitHub Actions workflows for common security best practices. This script captures the security hardening improvements that have been applied to this repository, making them repeatable and auditable.

## Security Checks

The script checks for 8 categories of security issues:

| Check | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1. Explicit permissions | All workflows should declare minimum required permissions |
| 2. No secrets: inherit | Pass secrets explicitly to limit exposure |
| 3. Fork PR protection | Jobs using secrets should skip fork PRs |
| 4. Tag ancestry verification | Tag-triggered releases should verify tag is on main |
| 5. workflow_dispatch protection | Publish/release workflows need environment protection |
| 6. Overly permissive | No `write-all` or unnecessary `contents: write` |
| 7. Pinned actions | Don't use `@main` or `@master` for external actions |
| 8. Dangerous patterns | No untrusted input injection, no risky `pull_request_target` |

## Usage

```bash
# Run the audit
python scripts/audit_gha_security.py

# Run tests
cd scripts && python -m unittest test_audit_gha_security -v
```

## Current Results

Running against this repo's workflows shows 3 warnings (no errors):
- `nightly-prerelease.yaml`: Missing tag ancestry verification
- `nightly-prerelease.yaml`: Has `workflow_dispatch` without environment protection
- `e2e.yaml`: Uses `posit-dev/with-connect@main` (unpinned action)

## Test plan

- [x] All 28 unit tests pass
- [x] Script runs successfully against current workflows
- [ ] Can be used to audit other repositories

title: security: replace secrets: inherit with explicit secret passing
description:
## Summary

Replace `secrets: inherit` with explicit secret declarations across all workflows that were using it.

## Why

`secrets: inherit` passes **all** repository secrets to called workflows. This violates the principle of least privilege - if a called workflow is compromised, it would have access to every secret in the repository.

By explicitly declaring which secrets each workflow needs, we limit the blast radius of any potential compromise.

## Changes

| Workflow | Called Workflow | Secrets Now Passed |
|----------|-----------------|-------------------|
| `main.yaml` | `e2e.yaml` | CONNECT_LICENSE, CONNECT_LICENSE_FILE, WORKBENCH_LICENSE, GH_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN, PCC_USER_CCQA3 |
| `main.yaml` | `upload.yaml` | AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME |
| `main.yaml` | `generate-licenses.yaml` | POSIT_CONNECT_PROJECTS_APP_ID, POSIT_CONNECT_PROJECTS_PEM |
| `nightly.yaml` | `e2e.yaml` | CONNECT_LICENSE, CONNECT_LICENSE_FILE, WORKBENCH_LICENSE, GH_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN, PCC_USER_CCQA3 |
| `release.yaml` | `upload.yaml` | AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME |

## Verification

```bash
$ grep -l "secrets: inherit" .github/workflows/*.yaml
# No output - all instances removed
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify main branch CI still passes (e2e, upload, license generation)
- [ ] Verify nightly workflow still runs successfully
- [ ] Verify release workflow still works on next tag push

title: security: add tag ancestry verification to release workflows
description:
## Summary

- Add `verify-tag` job to `release.yaml` and `publish.yaml`
- Ensures tagged commits are on the `main` branch before proceeding with build/release

## Why

Without this check, someone with write access could:
1. Create a branch with unauthorized changes
2. Push a tag (e.g., `v99.0.0`) pointing to that branch
3. Trigger a release of code that was never merged to main

## How It Works

The verification step runs:
```bash
git merge-base --is-ancestor ${{ github.sha }} origin/main
```

This checks if the tagged commit is reachable from main's history:
- ✅ Tag on HEAD of main → passes
- ✅ Tag on older commit on main → passes  
- ✅ Tag on commit from merged PR → passes
- ❌ Tag on unmerged branch → fails
- ❌ Tag on arbitrary commit → fails

## Changes

| Workflow | Change |
|----------|--------|
| `release.yaml` | Added `verify-tag` job, `build` now depends on it |
| `publish.yaml` | Added `verify-tag` job, `build` now depends on it |

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify normal releases still work (tag on main)
- [ ] Verify workflow fails if tag points to non-main commit (can test manually)

title: security: add fork PR checks to e2e and upload jobs
description:
## Summary

Note: this is a pretty minimal add in terms of security, but it does avoid generating OIDC tokens (which we would expect to be rejected in AWS, to be clear - but why not just avoid creating them in the first place)

- Add explicit fork PR checks to `e2e` and `upload` jobs in `pull-request.yaml`
- Fork PRs (from external contributors) will now skip these jobs entirely

## Why

Fork PRs don't have access to repository secrets, so these jobs would fail anyway. This change:

- **Prevents wasted CI resources** on jobs that will fail without secrets
- **Avoids OIDC token generation** for untrusted code paths
- **Makes the security boundary explicit** in the workflow definition

## Details

Added this condition to both jobs:
```yaml
github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
```

This evaluates to `true` only for PRs from branches within `posit-dev/publisher`, not from forks.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify internal PRs still run e2e and upload jobs
- [ ] Verify fork PRs skip these jobs (can test by temporarily forking)

title: security: pin critical GitHub Actions to commit SHAs
description:
## Summary

Pin the most security-critical actions to specific commit SHAs to prevent supply chain attacks.

## Pinned Actions

| Action | Version | SHA |
|--------|---------|-----|
| actions/checkout | v6 | `de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd` |
| actions/upload-artifact | v6 | `b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f` |
| actions/download-artifact | v7 | `37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131` |

## Why These Actions

These are prioritized because they're high-risk:
- **checkout**: Runs arbitrary code from the repository - a compromised checkout action could inject malicious code
- **upload/download-artifact**: Handle build artifacts that get released - a compromised action could swap artifacts

## Why SHA Pinning

Version tags (like `@v6`) can be moved to point at different commits. If an action's repository is compromised, attackers could push malicious code and move the tag to include it. SHA pinning ensures you always get the exact code you reviewed.

Version comments are preserved (e.g., `# v6`) for maintainability.

## Future Work

Consider pinning remaining third-party actions in follow-up PRs, prioritizing by risk.

description:
## Summary

- Replace `secrets: inherit` with explicit secret passing in pull-request.yaml
- Add fork detection to prevent upload job from running on fork PRs
- Update upload.yaml to explicitly declare its required secret

|-----|--------|-------|
| e2e | `secrets: inherit` | Pass only `CONNECT_LICENSE`, `WORKBENCH_LICENSE` |
| upload | `secrets: inherit` | Pass only `AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME` + fork check |

## Why

Using `secrets: inherit` exposes all repository secrets to the called workflow. While GitHub doesn't pass secrets to fork PRs by default, PRs from branches within the same repo (from maintainers) do receive secrets. This change:

1. Reduces attack surface for potential secret exfiltration
2. Makes secret dependencies explicit and auditable
3. Prevents accidental secret exposure if new secrets are added to the repo

This is part of security hardening in preparation for adding package signing.

title: fix: align e2e Workbench version check with build process
description:
## Summary

Fixes intermittent nightly e2e test failures in the Workbench extension installation verification step.

- Aligns `install-positron-extension.sh` version detection with the build process logic
- Tests now correctly predict the installed extension version for both release and non-release builds

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Problem

The nightly e2e tests were failing intermittently with:
```
ERROR: Failed to verify extension installation with version 99.0.0
```

Investigation of [run #22213855528](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/actions/runs/22213855528) showed:
- VSIX installed: `publisher-1.32.0-linux-amd64.vsix`
- Extension installed as: `posit.publisher-1.32.0`
- Script expected: `posit.publisher-99.0.0`

### Why It Was Intermittent

The failure pattern depended on whether the build ran exactly on a git tag:

| Recent Run | Git Describe | Extension Version | Expected | Result |
|------------|--------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| 2026-02-20 | `1.32.0` | `1.32.0` | `99.0.0` | **FAIL** |
| 2026-02-19 | `1.31.7-7-g8f732392` | `99.0.0` | `99.0.0` | PASS |
| 2026-02-17 | `1.31.6` | `1.31.6` | `99.0.0` | **FAIL** |
| 2026-02-17 | `1.31.6-4-ga73b5287` | `99.0.0` | `99.0.0` | PASS |

### The Version Flow

There are two version systems at play:

1. **VSIX filename version**: Derived from `git describe --tags` (e.g., `1.32.0` or `1.31.7-7-gabcdef`)

2. **Internal package.json version**: What the extension actually installs as

The build process in `extensions/vscode/scripts/set-version.py` only updates `package.json` for exact semver versions:

```python
version_re = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$")

if not version_re.match(version):
    print(f"Version {version} is not a release version; skipping version update.")
    sys.exit(0)
```

This means:
- **Exact tag** (e.g., `1.32.0`): `set-version.py` updates package.json → extension installs as `1.32.0`
- **Post-tag commits** (e.g., `1.31.7-7-gabcdef`): `set-version.py` skips → package.json stays at `99.0.0` → extension installs as `99.0.0`

### The Bug

The `install-positron-extension.sh` script was reading the expected version directly from `package.json` in the source checkout:

```bash
EXPECTED_VERSION=$(grep -o '"version": *"[^"]*"' "$PACKAGE_JSON" | cut -d'"' -f4)
```

Since `package.json` in the repo always has `99.0.0`, this only matched when the build happened to skip version updates (post-tag commits).

### The Fix

The script now replicates the same semver-checking logic as `set-version.py`:

```bash
GIT_VERSION=$(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && git describe --tags 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^v//')

if [[ "$GIT_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    # Exact semver - set-version.py will update package.json
    EXPECTED_VERSION="$GIT_VERSION"
else
    # Non-release version - set-version.py skips, stays at 99.0.0
    EXPECTED_VERSION="99.0.0"
fi
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Re-run nightly workflow to verify fix
- [ ] Verify logic matches for both exact tags and post-tag commits

title: ci: fix docs-only detection by inverting to has-code filter
description:
## Summary

Fixes docs-only detection which was completely broken due to issues with `dorny/paths-filter`'s `predicate-quantifier` feature.

### Problems Found

1. **Missing input definition**: The `predicate-quantifier` input isn't declared in `action.yml` for v3, causing "Unexpected input" warnings
   - Original feature PR: [dorny/paths-filter#224](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/pull/224) - added code but missed `action.yml`
   - Fix PR merged but not released: [dorny/paths-filter#279](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/pull/279)
   - Open issues about this: [#226](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/pull/226), [#236](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/pull/236), [#259](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/pull/259)

2. **Broken implementation**: Even when the input is accepted, [the implementation](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/blob/de90cc6fb38fc0963ad72b210f1f284cd68cea36/src/filter.ts#L105-L114) is wrong:
   - **Expected**: "Return true if ALL changed files match at least one pattern"
   - **Actual**: "A file matches only if it matches ALL patterns" ([L110-111](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter/blob/de90cc6fb38fc0963ad72b210f1f284cd68cea36/src/filter.ts#L110-L111): `patterns.every(aPredicate)` checks if a single file matches every pattern)
   
   This meant `CHANGELOG.md` was rejected because it doesn't match `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, etc.

### Solution

Invert the logic from detecting "docs-only" to detecting "has-code":

```yaml
# Old (broken): docs-only is true if ALL files are docs
docs-only:
  - '**/*.md'
  - 'LICENSE'
  # predicate-quantifier: every  # broken!

# New (works): has-code is true if ANY file is NOT a doc
code:
  - '**'
  - '!**/*.md'
  - '!LICENSE'
  - '!.gitignore'
  - '!.gitattributes'
```

With the default `some` quantifier:
- `has-code = true` if any file matches (i.e., any non-doc file exists)
- CI runs when `has-code == 'true'`
- CI skips when only doc files changed

## Test plan

- [ ] PRs with only `.md` file changes skip tests
- [ ] PRs with code changes run tests
- [ ] No more "Unexpected input" warnings

title: ci: enable containerd image store for consistent Docker cache support
description:
## Summary

Fixes intermittent e2e test failures caused by inconsistent Docker cache support across GitHub Actions runners.

### Problem

Some `ubuntu-latest` runners have the containerd image store enabled while others don't. When a job lands on a runner without containerd, the Docker build fails with:

```
ERROR: failed to build: Cache export is not supported for the docker driver.
```

This explains why some matrix jobs (e.g., `preview`) pass while others (e.g., `release`) fail in the same workflow run - they got different runners.

### Solution

Explicitly enable the containerd snapshotter before setting up Docker Buildx:

```yaml
- name: Enable containerd image store
  run: |
    echo '{"features":{"containerd-snapshotter":true}}' | sudo tee /etc/docker/daemon.json
    sudo systemctl restart docker
```

This ensures consistent behavior across all runners while keeping the Docker layer caching benefits.

## Test plan

- [ ] E2E tests pass consistently across all matrix jobs

title: fix(e2e): fix race condition in open-connect-content test
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

I asked Claude to take a look at why open-connect-content continues to periodically flake out. This is what it came up with. The diagnosis and fix seems reasonable - obviously its hard to prove a race condition like this, but the fix itself is pretty non-invasive and reasonable regardless of a race condition existing. It doesn't change anything about what the tests are asserting, so seems pretty safe to try.

-----

The test was flaky because it started looking for the content GUID in the explorer immediately after the quick input closed, but before VS Code had actually started reloading the workspace.

Fix: Wait for the URL to change after submitting the command, which indicates the workspace reload has actually started, before searching for the GUID in the explorer.

title: chore: update to Go 1.25
description:
## Summary
- Update Go version from 1.24.0 to 1.25.0
- Unpin staticcheck to use latest version (v0.7.0 requires Go >= 1.25)
- Fix Windows test failure

## Changes

### Go 1.25 upgrade
- `go.mod`: 1.24.0 → 1.25.0
- Release notes: https://go.dev/doc/go1.25

### Staticcheck unpin
- `justfile`: `staticcheck@v0.6.0` → `staticcheck@latest`
- staticcheck v0.7.0 requires Go >= 1.25.0

### Windows compatibility fix
- `internal/services/api/paths/services.go`: Add `GetFileAttributesEx` to handled error operations

Go 1.25 on Windows changed the error operation returned when checking non-existent paths from `CreateFile` to `GetFileAttributesEx`. This is an internal implementation change not explicitly documented in the release notes, but was observed in CI when `TestPathsService_isSymlink_False_FileMissing` began failing on Windows runners.


Here is the relevant commit: https://github.com/golang/go/commit/bb0c14b895d90bb5941e0463ba6c3564fc504e4f

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...` succeeds
- [x] `go test -short ./...` passes locally
- [x] `staticcheck ./...` passes with v0.7.0
- [x] CI passes (including Windows)

Closes #3520

Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

Version 28.1.0

  • Added blob.text(), blob.arrayBuffer(), and blob.bytes() methods.
  • Improved getComputedStyle() to account for CSS specificity when multiple rules apply. (asamuzaK)
  • Improved synchronous XMLHttpRequest performance by using a persistent worker thread, avoiding ~400ms of setup overhead on every synchronous request after the first one.
  • Improved performance of node.getRootNode(), node.isConnected, and event.dispatchEvent() by caching the root node of document-connected trees.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to correctly handle !important priority. (asamuzaK)
  • Fixed document.getElementById() to return the first element in tree order when multiple elements share the same ID.
  • Fixed <svg> elements to no longer incorrectly proxy event handlers to the Window.
  • Fixed FileReader event timing and fileReader.result state to more closely follow the spec.
  • Fixed a potential hang when synchronous XMLHttpRequest encountered dispatch errors.
  • Fixed compatibility with environments where Node.js's built-in fetch() has been used before importing jsdom, by working around undici v6/v7 incompatibilities.

description:

description:

   - Skips Workbench container setup (~30-60s saved per job)
   - Uses --spec "tests/*.cy.js" to exclude workbench directory
   - Runs against all 4 Connect versions

2. `cypress-workbench` job (new):
   - Runs only Workbench/Positron tests
   - Sets up Workbench container
   - Runs against "release" version only (sufficient coverage)
   - Has dedicated artifact uploads and log extraction

This saves ~30-60 seconds per main test job by not pulling/starting the Workbench container when it's not needed.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.27.2 to 0.27.3
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.27.3

  • Preserve URL fragments in data URLs (#4370)

    Consider the following HTML, CSS, and SVG:

    • index.html:

      <!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head><link rel="stylesheet" href="icons.css"></head>
  <body><div class="triangle"></div></body>
</html>

    • icons.css:

      .triangle {
  width: 10px;
  height: 10px;
  background: currentColor;
  clip-path: url(./triangle.svg#x);
}

    • triangle.svg:

      <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <defs>
    <clipPath id="x">
      <path d="M0 0H10V10Z"/>
    </clipPath>
  </defs>
</svg>

    The CSS uses a URL fragment (the #x) to reference the clipPath element in the SVG file. Previously esbuild's CSS bundler didn't preserve the URL fragment when bundling the SVG using the dataurl loader, which broke the bundled CSS. With this release, esbuild will now preserve the URL fragment in the bundled CSS:

    /* icons.css */
.triangle {
  width: 10px;
  height: 10px;
  background: currentColor;
  clip-path: url('data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><clipPath id="x"><path d="M0 0H10V10Z"/></clipPath></defs></svg>#x');
}

The Connect server in the e2e environment has Python 3.11.11 installed, not 3.11.3. When the test specified the exact version `3.11.3`, the deployment would fail during environment restore with a `ModuleNotFound` error because Connect couldn't find a matching Python installation.

## Solution

Use the minor version (`3.11`) instead of the patch version (`3.11.3`), which allows Connect to match with the available Python 3.11.11 installation.

title: fix: suppress unknown error popup for backend connection errors
description:
## Summary

I'm fairly certain this is being caused by us hitting some type of race condition where the publisher frontend is trying to perform operations against the go api before it has finished startup (for whatever reason). Alternatively, there's something that is causing the go backend to "blip" - it should be immediately restarting if anything takes it down, but perhaps the frontend is making requests during that blip. 

I still want to do more investigation into if there's an underlying fix we need to make to improve the stability of the go backend, and/or make the frontend client more resilient and defensive against random blips in service availability. 

I'll track that work in a separate ticket - for now, this fix should significantly improve the user experience, primarily by logging this transient connection issue to the console rather than via a toast popup. 

If the toast popup were to appear still in some unforeseen way, this PR also improves the error message so that it says something more informative ("Publisher backend available"). 

This also adds a minor usability improvement by calling `showErrorMessage` instead of `showInformationMessage` when showing a true error condition.

## Problem

Users were seeing frequent "Unknown Error" popups with no useful information, especially during extension startup/shutdown when the backend isn't available yet. This is confusing behavior and not actionable for users.

## Changes

- `src/utils/errors.ts`: Added `isConnectionRefusedError()` helper and updated `getMessageFromError()` to handle ECONNREFUSED
- `src/entrypointTracker.ts`: Suppress popup for connection refused errors (just log to console), use proper error message type for real errors
- `src/utils/errors.test.ts`: Added test coverage

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (`npm run test-unit`)
- [x] Lint passes (`npm run lint`)
- [x] Manual test: prevent `bin/publisher` from running, open/save files, verify no popup appears
- [x] Manual test: verify real errors still show with `showErrorMessage`

Fixes #3452

title: fix: do not restart server process when shutting down
description:
## Intent

The server process auto-restart (#2961) should not trigger if we are intentionally stopping the process, as at shutdown.

Resolves #3195

## Type of Change

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

I used Claude to help diagnose the problem and implement the fix.

I was able to observe the buggy behavior sporadically by starting VS Code or Positron, publishing content, and then closing the editor. Sometimes, though not usually, a `publisher` process would linger after the editor was gone.

### things I fixed

The core of the problem seems to be that we have a restart handler that unconditionally restarts the process when it closes, regardless of why it closed. The targeted fix for this was to introduce a `stopping` flag that prevents restart.

I also added error handling around the status bar message setting, because it seems like the behavior of that API might be unpredictable at shutdown time. It might be better to just remove that code---do we really need to send a message when the editor is closing anyway?

### tests

There were no unit tests of Server. I got Claude to write some, which rely on a lot of mocking. We could refactor Server in the future to make it more testable (e.g. inject a ConnectionChecker that would be more easily mocked.)

I used `Run Extension` to manually test a deployment to Dogfood, and verified that the `publisher` process closed when I closed the editor.

### things that seem off but I didn't change

The `dispose` function seems redundant. We might want to consider either embracing the use of `Disposable` (add our server to `context.subscriptions` and let VS Code dispose of it), or removing this function as it might confuse people.

The call to `isDown` is kind of useless as we don't check the return value but I opted to keep this change small and leave that alone.

I'll attach `PLAN.md` with all the notes from the session, including some potential future improvements.

## User Impact

The user should not notice any changes in behavior, but they should no longer have orphaned `publisher` processes running after they exit the editor.

## Automated Tests

Added `servers.test.ts`.

## Directions for Reviewers

Please do review. 🙏🏻  I relied a lot of Claude here although I have read and understood everything in the PR.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.27.2 to 0.27.3
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.27.3

  • Preserve URL fragments in data URLs (#4370)

    Consider the following HTML, CSS, and SVG:

    • index.html:

      <!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head><link rel="stylesheet" href="icons.css"></head>
  <body><div class="triangle"></div></body>
</html>

    • icons.css:

      .triangle {
  width: 10px;
  height: 10px;
  background: currentColor;
  clip-path: url(./triangle.svg#x);
}

    • triangle.svg:

      <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <defs>
    <clipPath id="x">
      <path d="M0 0H10V10Z"/>
    </clipPath>
  </defs>
</svg>

    The CSS uses a URL fragment (the #x) to reference the clipPath element in the SVG file. Previously esbuild's CSS bundler didn't preserve the URL fragment when bundling the SVG using the dataurl loader, which broke the bundled CSS. With this release, esbuild will now preserve the URL fragment in the bundled CSS:

    /* icons.css */
.triangle {
  width: 10px;
  height: 10px;
  background: currentColor;
  clip-path: url('data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><clipPath id="x"><path d="M0 0H10V10Z"/></clipPath></defs></svg>#x');
}

title: feat: use installed R packages for renv snapshot if possible to improve deploy performance
description:
## Intent

Speed up deploys by allowing renv to reuse existing packages in the library.

Fixes #3442 

## Type of Change

performance improvement

## Approach

We create the renv lockfile by generating a new snapshot in a temporary directory. Then we were installing all packages fresh, even if the user already had them on their system. I've replace the `install()` with `hydrate()` which should copy over existing packages, making deploys much faster.

I also removed the `try()` to better surface errors.

## User Impact

Should improve the speed with which packages deploy 

## Automated Tests

Existing tests should continue to pass

title: fix: detect rpy2 dependency to include R section in configuration
description:
## Summary

When a Python file imports `rpy2` (which allows Python to call R code), the generated configuration should include an `[r]` section since R is required at runtime.

This change:
- Adds `HasRpy2Dependency()` function in `pydeps` package to check if `rpy2` is in `requirements.txt`
- Updates `RequiresR()` in the R inspector to check for rpy2 usage when the content type is Python
- Adds unit tests for the new functionality

Fixes #3425

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added for `HasRpy2Dependency()` function
- [x] Unit tests added for `RequiresR()` with rpy2 detection
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Manual test: Create a Python project with `rpy2` in `requirements.txt`, verify that the generated configuration includes an `[r]` section

### Test with samperman/rpy2 example
1. Clone https://github.com/samperman/rpy2
2. Select `app.py` as the entrypoint
3. Verify the configuration now includes `[r]` section

title: fix: improve changelog sync to preserve VSCode extension header
description:
## Summary

- Updates the `sync-changelog` script in `extensions/vscode/justfile` to be more selective when syncing from the root changelog
- Preserves the VSCode extension-specific header ("All notable changes to the Posit Publisher extension are documented...")
- Strips the `[Unreleased]` section

- Excludes pre-extension releases (1.1.2 and earlier, including all alpha/beta versions)
- Updates CONTRIBUTING.md to document the changelog sync behavior in the release process

1. Replaced the extension-specific header text

title: fix: failing server settings fetch
description:
This PR fixes and issue where the server settings `GET` endpoint was always failing.

Previously it would create an empty `unknown` type configuration prior to fetching the server settings, but because of the change in #3267 this _always_ failed. It did this because the endpoint would be incorrectly constructed using the unknown type like so: `/__api__/server_settings/scheduler/unknown-type`.

The fix here is two-fold:
- the API now expects the extension to supply the current deployment's content type
- the API now only uses the content type if the `appMode` `isKnown` meaning its a valid Connect `appMode` type in the `contentTypeConnectMap` we have

## Intent

Fixes #3444

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## User Impact

The "Add Integration Request" action is now visible again.

Previously, `refreshConnectServerSettings` was failing because the server settings API constructed invalid scheduler paths like `/__api__/server_settings/scheduler/unknown` for `unknown` content types.

## Automated Tests

Tests were added for the following:
- `TestAppModeIsKnown` - verifies the new IsKnown() method correctly identifies mapped vs unmapped content types
- `TestGetServerSettingsWithContentType` - verifies the selected deployment's content type is passed through the API handler
- `TestGetServerSettingsWithoutContentType` - verifies default behavior when no content type is provided, which no longer fails the fetch to grab server settings

## Directions for Reviewers

1. Build the extension with `just` at the root, and run the extension using the Extension Development Host
2. Select a deployment or create one
3. Verify the "Add Integration Request" action appears in the UI and that there are no console errors for fetching the server settings in the dev tools
4. Test with different content types like `python-fastapi` and `unknown`

title: Fix empty responses from agent for credentials fetching
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

Improves error handling for credential operations and removes unused performance profiling code from the VSCode extension.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

- **Handle missing responses from Publisher agent** (`8c74f966e`)
  - Add defensive null checks when querying credentials from the Publisher API
  - Properly handle cases where the agent doesn't return a response during:
    - Credential list queries (`multiStepInputs/common.ts:223-229`)
    - Server URL validation (`multiStepInputs/newConnectCredential.ts:251-256`)
    - API key validation (`multiStepInputs/newConnectCredential.ts:454-459`)
  - Show warning messages to users when the agent is unreachable
  - Fix optional chaining in axios error interceptor (`api/client.ts:49`)

### Refactoring
- **Remove performance profiling** (`99001a215`)
  - Remove request timestamp tracking and duration logging from axios interceptors
  - Clean up unused `logDuration()` method
  - Simplify response interceptor logic

## User Impact

These changes make the extension more resilient to network errors or cases where the Publisher agent subprocess fails to respond, preventing silent failures during credential operations. In some cases, performance profiling dropping requests silently.

- [ ] Test credential creation when Publisher agent is running normally

description:
Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 27.4.0 to 28.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

Version 28.0.0

  • Overhauled resource loading customization. See the new README for details on the new API.
  • Added MIME type sniffing to <iframe> and <frame> loads.
  • Regression: WebSockets are no longer correctly throttled to one connection per origin. This is a result of the bug at nodejs/undici#4743.
  • Fixed decoding of the query components of <a> and <area> elements in non-UTF-8 documents.
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest fetches and WebSocket upgrade requests to be interceptable by the new customizable resource loading. (Except synchronous XMLHttpRequests.)
  • Fixed the referrer of a document to be set correctly when redirects are involved; it is now the initiating page, not the last hop in the redirect chain.
  • Fixed correctness bugs when passing ArrayBuffers or typed arrays to various APIs, where they would not correctly snapshot the data.
  • Fixed require("url").parse() deprecation warning when using WebSockets.
  • Fixed <iframe>, <frame>, and <img> (when canvas is installed) to fire load events, not error events, on non-OK HTTP responses.
  • Fixed many small issues in XMLHttpRequest.

Updates `shiny` from 1.5.0 to 1.5.1
Release notes

Sourced from shiny's releases.

shiny 1.5.1

New features

  • Added toast notification system with ui.toast(), ui.toast_header(), ui.show_toast(), and ui.hide_toast(). Toast notifications are temporary, non-intrusive messages that support multiple semantic types (success, warning, error, etc.), flexible positioning (9 positions: top/middle/bottom × left/center/right), auto-hide with configurable duration, optional headers with icons, and programmatic control. (#2111)

  • Added a new input_submit_textarea() input element, which is similar to input_text_area(), but includes a submit button to only submit the text changes to the server on click. This is especially useful when the input text change triggers a long-running operation and/or the user wants to type longer-form input and review it before submitting it. (#2099)

Bug fixes

  • Fixed ui.tooltip()'s options parameter to properly pass Bootstrap tooltip options to the underlying web component. (#2101)

  • Fixed an issue where session.bookmark() would error when non-existent input values are read. (#2117)

  • Revised accordion()'s open logic to close all panels when an empty list is passed. (#2109)

Release notes

pandas 3.0.0

We are pleased to announce the release of pandas 3.0.0, a major release from the pandas 2.x series. This release includes various new features, bug fixes, and performance improvements, as well as possible breaking changes.

The pandas 3.0 release removed a functionality that was deprecated in previous releases. It is recommended to first upgrade to pandas 2.3 and to ensure your code is working without warnings, before upgrading to pandas 3.0.

Highlights include:

  • Dedicated string data type by default
  • Consistent copy/view behaviour with Copy-on-Write (CoW) (a.k.a. getting rid of the SettingWithCopyWarning)
  • New default resolution for datetime-like data
  • Initial support for the new pd.col syntax

See the announcement blog post and the detailed release notes for a list of all the changes.

Pandas 3.0.0 supports Python 3.11 and higher. The release can be installed from PyPI

python -m pip install --upgrade pandas==3.0.*

Or from conda-forge

conda install -c conda-forge pandas=3.0

Please report any issues with the release on the pandas issue tracker.

Thanks to all the contributors who made this release possible.

Updates `scipy` from 1.16.3 to 1.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from scipy's releases.

SciPy 1.17.0 Release Notes

SciPy 1.17.0 is the culmination of 6 months of hard work. It contains many new features, numerous bug-fixes, improved test coverage and better documentation. There have been a number of deprecations and API changes in this release, which are documented below. All users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, as there are a large number of bug-fixes and optimizations. Before upgrading, we recommend that users check that their own code does not use deprecated SciPy functionality (to do so, run your code with python -Wd and check for DeprecationWarning s). Our development attention will now shift to bug-fix releases on the 1.17.x branch, and on adding new features on the main branch.

This release requires Python 3.11-3.14 and NumPy 1.26.4 or greater.

Highlights of this release

  • Many SciPy functions have gained native support for batching of N-dimensional array input and additional support for the array API standard. An overall summary of the latter is now available in a set of tables.
  • In scipy.sparse, coo_array now supports indexing. This includes integers, slices, arrays, np.newaxis, Ellipsis, in 1D, 2D and the relatively new nD. In scipy.sparse.linalg, ARPACK and PROPACK rewrites from Fortran77 to C now empower the use of external pseudorandom number generators, e.g. from numpy.
  • In scipy.spatial, transform.Rotation and transform.RigidTransform have been extended to support N-D arrays. geometric_slerp now has support for extrapolation.
  • scipy.stats has gained the matrix t and logistic distributions and many performance and accuracy improvements.
  • Initial support for 64-bit integer (ILP64) BLAS and LAPACK libraries has been added, including for MKL and Apple Accelerate. Please report any issues with ILP64 you encounter.

New features

scipy.integrate improvements

  • The integration routines dopri5, dopri853, LSODA, vode, and zvode have been ported from Fortran77 to C.
  • scipy.integrate.quad now has a fast path for returning 0 when the integration interval is empty.
  • The BDF, DOP853, RK23, RK45, OdeSolver, DenseOutput, ode, and complex_ode classes now support subscription, making them generic types, for compatibility with scipy-stubs.

Release notes

Sourced from shiny's releases.

shiny 1.5.1

New features

  • Added toast notification system with ui.toast(), ui.toast_header(), ui.show_toast(), and ui.hide_toast(). Toast notifications are temporary, non-intrusive messages that support multiple semantic types (success, warning, error, etc.), flexible positioning (9 positions: top/middle/bottom × left/center/right), auto-hide with configurable duration, optional headers with icons, and programmatic control. (#2111)

  • Added a new input_submit_textarea() input element, which is similar to input_text_area(), but includes a submit button to only submit the text changes to the server on click. This is especially useful when the input text change triggers a long-running operation and/or the user wants to type longer-form input and review it before submitting it. (#2099)

Bug fixes

  • Fixed ui.tooltip()'s options parameter to properly pass Bootstrap tooltip options to the underlying web component. (#2101)

  • Fixed an issue where session.bookmark() would error when non-existent input values are read. (#2117)

  • Revised accordion()'s open logic to close all panels when an empty list is passed. (#2109)

Updates `pandas` from 2.3.3 to 3.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from pandas's releases.

pandas 3.0.0

We are pleased to announce the release of pandas 3.0.0, a major release from the pandas 2.x series. This release includes various new features, bug fixes, and performance improvements, as well as possible breaking changes.

The pandas 3.0 release removed a functionality that was deprecated in previous releases. It is recommended to first upgrade to pandas 2.3 and to ensure your code is working without warnings, before upgrading to pandas 3.0.

Highlights include:

  • Dedicated string data type by default
  • Consistent copy/view behaviour with Copy-on-Write (CoW) (a.k.a. getting rid of the SettingWithCopyWarning)
  • New default resolution for datetime-like data
  • Initial support for the new pd.col syntax

See the announcement blog post and the detailed release notes for a list of all the changes.

Pandas 3.0.0 supports Python 3.11 and higher. The release can be installed from PyPI

python -m pip install --upgrade pandas==3.0.*

Or from conda-forge

conda install -c conda-forge pandas=3.0

Please report any issues with the release on the pandas issue tracker.

Thanks to all the contributors who made this release possible.

Pandas 3.0.0rc2

No release notes provided.

Pandas 3.0.0rc1

No release notes provided.

Pandas 3.0.0rc0

We are pleased to announce a first release candidate for pandas 3.0.0. If all goes well, we'll release pandas 3.0.0 in a few weeks.

See the [whatsnew][0] for a list of all the changes.

The release is available on conda-forge and PyPI.

The release can be installed from PyPI

python -m pip install --upgrade --pre pandas==3.0.0rc0

Or from conda-forge

conda install -c conda-forge/label/pandas_rc pandas==3.0.0rc0

Please report any issues with the release candidate on the pandas issue tracker.

Updates `scipy` from 1.16.3 to 1.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from scipy's releases.

SciPy 1.17.0 Release Notes

SciPy 1.17.0 is the culmination of 6 months of hard work. It contains many new features, numerous bug-fixes, improved test coverage and better documentation. There have been a number of deprecations and API changes in this release, which are documented below. All users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, as there are a large number of bug-fixes and optimizations. Before upgrading, we recommend that users check that their own code does not use deprecated SciPy functionality (to do so, run your code with python -Wd and check for DeprecationWarning s). Our development attention will now shift to bug-fix releases on the 1.17.x branch, and on adding new features on the main branch.

This release requires Python 3.11-3.14 and NumPy 1.26.4 or greater.

Highlights of this release

  • Many SciPy functions have gained native support for batching of N-dimensional array input and additional support for the array API standard. An overall summary of the latter is now available in a set of tables.
  • In scipy.sparse, coo_array now supports indexing. This includes integers, slices, arrays, np.newaxis, Ellipsis, in 1D, 2D and the relatively new nD. In scipy.sparse.linalg, ARPACK and PROPACK rewrites from Fortran77 to C now empower the use of external pseudorandom number generators, e.g. from numpy.
  • In scipy.spatial, transform.Rotation and transform.RigidTransform have been extended to support N-D arrays. geometric_slerp now has support for extrapolation.
  • scipy.stats has gained the matrix t and logistic distributions and many performance and accuracy improvements.
  • Initial support for 64-bit integer (ILP64) BLAS and LAPACK libraries has been added, including for MKL and Apple Accelerate. Please report any issues with ILP64 you encounter.

New features

scipy.integrate improvements

  • The integration routines dopri5, dopri853, LSODA, vode, and zvode have been ported from Fortran77 to C.
  • scipy.integrate.quad now has a fast path for returning 0 when the integration interval is empty.
  • The BDF, DOP853, RK23, RK45, OdeSolver, DenseOutput, ode, and complex_ode classes now support subscription, making them generic types, for compatibility with scipy-stubs.

Updates `playwright` from 1.56.1 to 1.58.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.58.0

📣 Playwright CLI+SKILLs 📣

We are adding a new token-efficient CLI mode of operation to Playwright with the skills located at playwright-cli. This brings the long-awaited official SKILL-focused CLI mode to our story and makes it more coding agent-friendly.

It is the first snapshot with the essential command set (which is already larger than the original MCP!), but we expect it to grow rapidly. Unlike the token use, that one we expect to go down since snapshots are no longer forced into the LLM!

Timeline

If you're using merged reports, the HTML report Speedboard tab now shows the Timeline:

UI Mode and Trace Viewer Improvements

  • New 'system' theme option follows your OS dark/light mode preference
  • Search functionality (Cmd/Ctrl+F) is now available in code editors
  • Network details panel has been reorganized for better usability
  • JSON responses are now automatically formatted for readability

Thanks to @​cpAdm for contributing these improvements!

Miscellaneous

browserType.connectOverCDP() now accepts an isLocal option. When set to true, it tells Playwright that it runs on the same host as the CDP server, enabling file system optimizations.

Breaking Changes ⚠️

  • Removed _react and _vue selectors. See locators guide for alternatives.
  • Removed :light selector engine suffix. Use standard CSS selectors instead.
  • Option devtools from browserType.launch() has been removed. Use args: ['--auto-open-devtools-for-tabs'] instead.
  • Removed macOS 13 support for WebKit. We recommend to upgrade your macOS version, or keep using an older Playwright version.

Browser Versions

  • Chromium 145.0.7632.6
  • Mozilla Firefox 146.0.1
  • WebKit 26.0

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:

  • Google Chrome 144
  • Microsoft Edge 144

v1.57.0

Speedboard

In HTML reporter, there's a new tab we call "Speedboard":

It shows you all your executed tests sorted by slowness, and can help you understand where your test suite is taking longer than expected. Take a look at yours - maybe you'll find some tests that are spending a longer time waiting than they should!
