title: feat: add "set up renv" button
description:
## Intent

Add a button, "Set Up renv", that sets up an renv environment, installs dependencies, and creates an renv lockfile. Exposes functionality added in #3000.

<details>
  <summary>Screen recording of the button in action</summary>

  [video](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32423526-9922-4999-aecd-cf69ba0a5dfc)
</details>

Resolves #2986

## Type of Change

- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->

## Approach

- Adds a button to the R packages section, which is hidden when an R lockfile is detected.
- The button is disabled when clicked. The button will not re-enable till the extension restarts, to avoid problems like a race condition in the case of lengthy installed.

## User Impact

- Allows users with an R project without `renv` to set up renv in that directory.

## Automated Tests

Back-end tests were added in #3000. Adding the button is a front-end component-level change, and those aren't tested right now. I don't see a place to hook in for e2e tests -- perhaps in `test/e2e/tests/deployments.cy.js`, where tests are currently skipped.

## Directions for Reviewers

- Front-end changes are unremarkable.
- The back end code uses `InterpretersFromRequest` to get the R interpreter path. I don't know enough about how this works to feel _certain_ that it will always pick the correct R interpreter for a user's project. It's used like this elsewhere, but those cases might already have an `renv` environment to specify the R version, and I'm not sure how it falls back.

title: fix: bundle autogenerated renv.lock
description:
## Intent

When the renv.lock file doesn't exist the publisher sets it by default anyway and tries to include it in the bundle,
this fails as there is no renv.lock to include. As in that case we scan dependencies and generate the manifest without
any renv.lock, we should include in the bundle the `renv.lock` that was generated instead of looking for one from the user.

## Type of Change

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

## Approach

Bundle creation has been shifted to rely on `Manifest.X` configuration to create the bundle instead of relying on `Config.X`. This makes so that the bundle always respects what was written in the manifest independently from the original configuration.

## User Impact

Deploying without any lockfile should work

## Automated Tests

Added a few tests for the possible combination of cases.

## Directions for Reviewers

This should be tested by deploying R projects that has an ` renv.lock` and R projects that don't have any ` renv.lock`

title: fix: Avoid trying to include n bundles the default renv.lock when it doesn't exist.
description:
## Intent

When the `renv.lock` file doesn't exist the publisher sets it by default anyway and tries to include it in the bundle,
this fails as there is no renv.lock to include. As in that case we scan dependencies and generate the manifest without
any renv.lock, we should just avoid including in the bundle any lockfile.

## Type of Change

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

## Approach

When the lockfile isn't found, keep `Config.R.PackageFile` empty to signal that there is no lockfile at all.
Previously it was set to the default value in all cases.
Then the code can use `PackageFile == ""` as a guard to know if the renv.lock must be included in the bundle or not.

## User Impact

Deploying without any lockfile should work

## Automated Tests

Added tests to confirm that the lock is included when it exists and that is not used when it does not exist.

title: Implementation of Publisher raw logs toggle
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Resolves #2875 

The intent is to introduce a toggle view on the Publisher logs where the user can easily toggle between log summary view (tree view) and the log raw view (text view) so they can easily copy the logs for more in-depth investigations. The are also a couple of handy buttons "Copy Logs" and "Save & Open Logs", which respectively either copies all the logs to the clipboard or saves all the logs to a file and opens it. The "Save & Open Logs" button, which generates the log file and opens it in the editor will provide the capability for searching and sharing that file with other extensions such as the Positron Assistant, which can be used to help analyze errors and provide potential solutions.

<details>
  <summary>VS Code screen video</summary>

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cde32f23-e25d-484f-b866-f846f0c85a14
</details> 

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The approach was to use a container panel and have a couple of views that belong to that panel but only one view is visible at any given point using a view mode that gets persisted in the context global state. There are also a couple of commands for the toggling. The reason for this is to be able to change the icon when we toggle so the list icon changes to the tree icon and so on. The other thing to notice is since we have a couple of views now for the logs panel and any of them can be hidden or visible at any given time, we have to then focus on both views whenever we want to focus on the logs panel view. Whichever view is visible at the moment will work as expected and it will be a no-op for whichever view is currently hidden. This could have been done is a more complex way where we figure out which view is currently visible and only focus on that one view but that felt like unnecessary extra work.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

User will now be able to toggle between the summary logs view (tree) and the raw logs view (text). They will also be able to copy and save the raw logs.

## Automated Tests

<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

My branch passes E2E tests in CI

## Directions for Reviewers

- [ ] Verify that you are able to copy and save the raw logs for both Connect and Connect Cloud deployments in either the tree view or the plain view of the logs panel.

description:
The PR uses the same URL discover logic we have for creating a Publisher Credential via an API key and utilizes it for token authentication.

If additional URL paths are provided like the below the create server URL can will be discovered for easier Credential creation.

- `.../connect`
- `.../connect/#/content/listing`

## Approach

The approach was to extract the URL discovery logic from `post_test_credentials.go` that walked the URL paths backward into a utility function that both credential creation APIs could utilize. Both APIs have their own URL test logic that are passed to the utility to keep things as easy to use as possible.

## User Impact

Users that provide a Connect server URL when creating a credential now have a much easier time copying and pasting.

title: feat: Allow user to explicitly pick python package manager or server default
description:
## Intent

At the moment, if package_manager is not specified, the publisher will default to enforcing "pip".
Instead we want:
1. If not specified -> server default
2. if pip -> enforce pip
3. If uv -> enforce uv

closes #2985
closes #2638

## Type of Change

- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->

## Approach

If `python.package_manager` option is not specified, it will now default to an `"auto"` value.
This value gets then translated to `"pip"`+`"allow_uv=null"` when generating the manifest.
That means the server will be able to choose what to do based on its `DefaultPackageManager` option.

The `allow_uv=null` is because older servers didn't understand or accept the
`allow_uv` option. By setting it at null it gets omitted from the `manifest.json`
and thus retains backward compatibility.

If instead the user specified a value, that value is used and the server can accept
or refuse the deploy based on its `AllowUv` server side option.

## User Impact

When deploying against a server that defaults to `uv`, the user can now
switch back to `pip` by specifying `package_manager=pip`, previously
doing so, would have yet deployed with `uv` if that was the default server
package manager.

## Automated Tests

A test confirms that the json generated given the 3 cases is the expected one.

## Directions for Reviewers

`TestNewManifestFromConfig_PythonPackageManagerVariants_JSON`  more or less explains the expectations

title: Add Cypress e2e test for Posit Workbench
description:
## Intent

Add initial e2e support and test for Publisher deployments on Posit Workbench using Positron.

Fixes #2911

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [x] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

- Leverage previous work that implemented manual Workbench testings in https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2909
- Leverage existing VS Code commands and workflows as much as possible
- Enabled the following plugins:
    - [cypress-wait-until](https://github.com/NoriSte/cypress-wait-until) this was already in the package.json but not enabled
    - [cypress-network-idle](https://github.com/bahmutov/cypress-network-idle) extremely handy tool for pacing tests by waiting for specific network traffic to idle/stop
- Add new Workbench-specific commands to a new workbench support file and name them as clearly as possible to reduce potential confusion
- Added some new commands to CI to save Workbench related logs as artifacts which deviates from the current method of printing them to the CLI
- Also deviated from the existing method of post-test DEBUG where we print out the installed extensions, etc. as most of that is captured during the Workbench extensions install command
- In order to ensure a clean Workbench environment for each test leverage our justfile commands to stop, remove, and start a fresh Workbench container. This adds approximately 25 seconds to each test but is the only way I could find that would ensure a completely clean environment
    - Will create a ticket for future work that can try maintaining test isolation by creating new users for each test, though this may be challenging since we're using the public Workbench container
- Implement the following tests leveraged directly from `test/e2e/tests/deployments.cy.js`:
    - static deployment test that I used to get us started and prove that all of this works locally and in CI
- Updated CONTRIBUTING for all of the Workbench related changes in this and the previous PR

## KNOWN ISSUES

- The first test that runs, does the first visit to Workbench, then silently errors and restarts, then works fine after.
    -  I've chased this down to overriding the baseUrl in the spec, which is a valid thing to do. But when the baseUrl in Cypress config does not match when we do our first visit() Cypress silently restarts the whole spec again. If they do match this restart is not observed. Publisher is currently using an older Cypress version so maybe a version upgrade would correct this behavior, though I see nothing obvious mentioned in [the Cypress changelog](https://docs.cypress.io/app/references/changelog). We do have a paid contract with Cypress and they are responsive if we can provide a reproducible issue.
- Positron session is successfully started though it takes ~60s. This seems related to running Workbench in Cypress as the Positron sessions start quickly in my local browser from the same Workbench container. This occurs when running via Cypress locally or in CI.


## User Impact

None

## Automated Tests

New Workbench-specific Cypress e2e spec.

## Directions for Reviewers

- Follow the existing local `just dev` workflow and ensure you can run the Workbench spec
- Verify the Workbench spec ran and passed in CI
- Verify the new Workbench-specific command names make sense and are clear without having to dive deeply into the code

title: feat: Prevent users to have unknown content configurations for Quarto projects
description:
## Intent

Resolves #2890 

Getting a configuration with `type= "unknown"` is painful. Users that do not have a Quarto binary on the system but that the project can be easily identified as a Quarto project by `.qmd` files are landing in this state.

This PR aims to fix that.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

If there is no Quarto binary on the system, pay attention to the files so that for `.qmd` files or if there is a `_quarto.yml` present we determine the project is a Quarto project.

The resulting configuration will add the adjacent `.qmd` files, we cannot do more than that since `quarto inspect` won;t work. Even so, it is a much better state that can be fixed with the files picker, rather than having `type= "unknown"`.

## User Impact

Users with no Quarto binary on the system can get Quarto type configurations.

## Automated Tests

Expanded unit tests to cover the described scenario.

## Directions for Reviewers

This one is a bit cumbersome to verify manually because quarto should not be available on the system. Options are:
- Get rid (hide, rename, move temporarily from `/usr/local/bin`) of your quarto installation.
- Modify the code, on `/inspect/detectors/quarto.go L51` change `RunCommand("quarto"` to not be `"quarto"` and use an unavailable command name. Then package and install.

Try publishing a Quarto project, even if there is no quarto binary available, you should be able to get a Quarto type configuration.

title: fix: Set config defaults when missing from config
description:
This PR fixes the Python Packages and R Packages views from incorrectly stating that the package files were missing by ensuring that the defaults are loaded into the active configuration state in the extension. They were not loaded in making the `homeView` think that there was no `packageFile` for both Python and R.
Preview
Note: If the `package_file` was set in the `[r]` or `[python]` sections this bug didn't occur since we didn't need to load defaults. The configuration API would include that data. ## Intent Resolves #2882, #2884 ## Type of Change - - [x] Bug Fix - - [ ] New Feature - - [ ] Breaking Change - - [ ] Documentation - - [ ] Refactor - - [ ] Tooling ## Approach Initially, I saw that the state in the `homeView` pinia store `home` did not have the `packageFile` set. I did this by just showing the state in the view to confirm. Next, I looked into where `updatePythonPackages` was being called since that is where we set the Python data for the store. https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/cf31dae294f5226915b8feb66561f48a47b44e2e/extensions/vscode/webviews/homeView/src/stores/home.ts#L271 The API difference looked fishy - the configuration response differed between `v1.18.1` and `main`. Before #2787 we returned empty strings: ``` ... "python": { "packageFile": "", "packageManager": "", "requiresPython": "", "version": "" }, ``` after we didn't. Empty values were omitted ``` ... python: {} ``` But why did it work in `v1.18.1`? https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/ec937e2cd6472fb6e43e62b36e7e16a716632a62/extensions/vscode/src/state.ts#L237 When we load in the selected configuration we get the configuration, but we also call the interpreters API endpoint to get defaults and fill them in the configuration so the state reflects what Publisher will do and not just what is in the configuration file. `UpdateConfigWithDefaults` was expecting those empty strings rather than just checking for `falsey` values. ## User Impact The views now show packages as expected and do not incorrectly communicate that a package file is missing. ## Directions for Reviewers Check that `requirements.txt` and `renv.lock` defaults work. Check that when setting the `package_file` manually the view updates as expected. ## Checklist - [x] I have updated [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

description:
## Intent

Add a button so that users without `renv` infrastructure can create it.

Resolves #2928

## Type of Change

- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->

## Approach

This PR is incomplete, but I'm adding this draft PR because I have some open questions about approach.

So far, the approach has been:

- Add an alternative code path in `defaultRInterpreter.CreateLockfile` that uses a modified version of the R script from `ScanDependencies` (added in #2840).  There are some minor differences (it doesn't run in a temporary directory — aside, writing this I'm now wondering though if the R interpreter's working directory at startup is the correct directory).
  - That path is gated by a boolean, similar to #2840.
- A "Scan" button is added to `RPackages.vue` to initiate the scan. Before this PR, I don't think the old `renv::snapshot()`-only behavior was ever exposed.

Current issues / "new to this project" / other questions I have:

- Concretely and immediately: Currently when the code is dispatched, in `post_packages_r_scan.go`, there is a null pointer dereference that occurs on line 65 when `h.rInterpreterFactory()` is called to instantiate the R interpreter. Need to figure out why that isn't working. I'll dig into that in the morning.
- Thinking about our discussion today and what @amol- was saying — I think it would probably be ideal to not touch the front end with this, to decompose this only into an implementation on the back-end side with tests, and then worry about calling it and adding the front end from a different PR. I added the button to make it easier to test in a real environment, but perhaps this is too early for that! Thinking this through out loud. Perhaps I'll narrow scope tomorrow.
- There is a bunch of logic in the interpreter in `r.go` for finding the current lockfile for an interpreter, but it isn't used very much in this path — the filename for the lockfile is passed back from the front end. To my gut, this feels like a bad way to share division of responsibilities, but perhaps it isn't. 🤔

title: Refreshing the credentials when creating a new deployment failed but creating a new credential succeeded
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->

<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Resolves #2939 

The intent of this PR is to refresh the credential list in the homeView when creating a new deployment failed but creating a new credential succeeded.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

To avoid forcing a credential refresh regardless of having created a new credential or not while creating a new deployment, I have changed the return type of `newDeployment()` to always return an object that may contain undefined properties for all things needed for creating a new deployment. The approach was to declare a new deployment creation successful only when all properties are present, otherwise, check the credential property to trigger a credential refresh only if necessary.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

The user will see newly created credentials while creating a new deployment even if creating that new deployment ends up failing.

description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Resolves #2873 

The intent of this PR is to tweak the wording on the cancel deploy info message and button labeling so it is more obvious that:
- Clicking the button will just open the publisher logs panel (if it isn't already opened) in your editor.
- The deployment "may" or "may not" continue in the server when cancelled depending on how fast the cancel button was clicked. At least this is the case for Connect Cloud where if you click the button fast enough, the publish won't happen in the server at all.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The approach to the wording and labeling changes were simple enough. However, while trying out the deployment cancelling I did find a case where the "Deploy Your Project" button stays disabled when the R environment is broken and the users cancels the deployment right away. I added a new message type to handle this scenario: `PUBLISH_CANCEL`, which will clear the decks for the "Deploy Your Project" button to become enabled again as expected upon deployment cancellation.

Separately, I did a minor tweak to the logs panel so it will auto select and focus on the last error line when there is a failure to deploy in the logs panel. I also included this behavior for cancelled deployments, so the last cancelled line will be auto selected and focused on the logs panel.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

- Better messaging and button labeling for the user when cancelling a deployment.
- Targeted log line selecting and focusing on the logs panel for errors and deployment cancellations.
- Re-enablement of the "Deploy Your Project" button after deployment cancellation with a broken R environment.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

E2E tests pass on CI for this branch.

<!-- Provide steps for reviewers to validate this change manually. -->

- Verify there is better messaging and button labeling for the user when cancelling a deployment for both Connect Cloud and Connect deployments.
- Verify there is targeted log line selecting and focusing on the logs panel for errors and deployment cancellations for both Connect Cloud and Connect deployments.

title: display runtime logs and keep fetching for 5 seconds after publish completes
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

Resolves https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2878.

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

We can show runtime logs just fine in addition to build logs... But since the logs in question happen at the very end of the publishing process, and our logs stream is independent of our publishing status updates, they can get cut off if the status updates before the logs can come through. Here I introduce a 5 second delay before stopping the logs client.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

Users will see the runtime error that caused their app to fail, or if their app starts, the first few seconds of app logs.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

Not sure how to test this... I'm guessing it's not worth the effort to figure out.

## Directions for Reviewers

title: feat: Revealing first failing stage in Publisher logs
description:
This PR introduces a new feature: when the "posit-publisher-logs" panel `TreeView` is revealed the first failing deployment stage (if one exists) will be revealed.

Revealing it:
- scrolls it into view
- expands other `TreeViewItems` if necessary
- expands the `LogsTreeStageItem` itself

## Intent

Resolves #2857 #2858

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

The approach was to use the [TreeView `reveal()` method](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#TreeView.reveal) alongside an [`onDidChangeVisibility` listener](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#TreeView.onDidChangeVisibility) on the TreeView.

When the TreeView is shown we try to grab the first `LogsTreeStageItem` has the `LogStateStatus.failed` status.

If one exists we `reveal()` it.

To accomplish this the two `TreeItem` types (`LogsTreeItemLogItem` and `LogsTreeStageItem`) needed to track their `parent` `TreeItem`s to implement `TreeDataProvider`'s optional `getParent` method which is necessary for the `reveal()` method to function.

With all of this in place the Publisher Logs reveal the first failing stage.

## User Impact

When opening the Publisher Logs the first stage is shown quickly getting users to the most relevant bit of the logs (a failure) as quickly as possible

## Directions for Reviewers

Deploy a project without an error and check that the logs view behaves normally.

Deploy a project that causes a failure in the logs and open the Publisher logs using any method you'd like. The failing stage should be in view even if the logs are very small.

title: Fixing the events for Connect Cloud publishing
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->

<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Resolves #2853 

The intent of this PR is to make the new events for publishing to Connect Cloud visible in the event progress pop-up in the bottom right corner of the editor as the publishing happens.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The actual root cause of the bug was a legitimate change in the order of events for publishing. What was happening was:
- Event A starts - displays active event label for event A
- Event B starts - displays active event label for event B (hides active label for event A)
- Event B ends - displays inactive event label for event B
- Event A continues to happen sending log events while displaying the inactive event label for event B 
- ...
- Event A ends - event progress box is hidden because this was the last event and the active event label for event A was visible for like 1 millisecond or less at the very beginning

The fix was to expose the `localId` for the `log` events from the agent as it is done for all the `start` events so the progress label for the event that is currently logging will override what is being displayed in the progress event popup. It also looks like this was the intent from the beginning and then there was some conversion of `snake-case` to `camelCase` where this must have been missed because the code was present in the codebase to expose the `local-id` just using the wrong case. 

Since this PR exposes the `localId` for ALL the `log` events, I checked that there were no adverse effects for publishing to Connect and I did not see anything outside of what happens currently without this code change.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

None.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

This branch passes all E2E tests in CI.

title: feat: Prefer logs URLs for failure events in logs
description:
This PR updates the Publisher logs view to prefer using passed `logsUrl`s for the `publish/failure` and `publish/validateDeployment/failure` events. This means that when a publish fails you are much more likely to be linked directly to the logs on Connect or in Connect Cloud. In the below preview both the errors: - "Deployed content does not seem to be running. See the logs in Connect for details" - "Deployment failed, click to view Posit Connect logs" now both link to the `/apps/${content-guid}/logs` URL which shows the logs immediately. Since Connect Cloud was already using the `logsUrl` as a preference the behavior stays the same there.
Preview

title: fix keyring ForceSet implementation to not create duplicate creds
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->

<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

The new ForceSet method on the credential service turned out to actually be adding a new credential instead of overwriting as intended.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The file and keychain credential services differ in that the file is a mapping keyed by credential name, and the keychain is a mapping keyed by credential GUID. Since we're creating a new GUID when we interpret the credential, a "new" credential with a different GUID was getting added.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

Stops users from seeing unintended duplicate credentials after credentials are refreshed (due to cloud access token expiring).

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

Updated keychain cred service test to verify the intended behavior.

title: make creating deployment config file work for connect cloud
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Creating a config follows this process:
1. In the extension, call POST /inspect to get the config data
1. Add the product type to the config data
1. In the extension, call PUT /configurations/{name} with the config data
    1. In the agent, validate the config data against the schema
    3. In the agent, write the config to the TOML file

Since we currently use the same Config struct to represent both Connect and Connect Cloud configurations, some fields are only valid for one of the product types. The config returned by `POST /inspect` populates some of those fields, so the validation in 3.i fails. This pull request updates `PUT /configurations/{name}` to unset those fields so that the validation can pass and we can write a valid TOML file.

This pull request also fixes setting the product type in the config data.

Resolves https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2788.

title: Large refactor for creating a new deployment and creating a new credential
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Resolves #2805

The intent of this PR is to refactor common multi-step code to create a new credential into sharable code to eliminate large amounts code duplication between the `newDeployment.ts` file and the `newCredential.ts` file. Some other by-product refactors/enhancements were needed in this endeavor and others were done for efficiency/simplicity, such as:
- Refactoring the way we handled skipping a step in the backward history navigation with the `skipStepHistory` prop to make it simpler, less error prone and more intuitive.
- Keeping track of the local step history stack in parent flows with `stepHistory` and passing it down to children sub-flows as `previousSteps` to keep the backward navigation fully working in all the multi-steps.
- Removing the recursion from the API polling and replacing it with a simple loop to avoid requests overlapping and lessen the call stack depth to make it easier to debug potential issues.
- Splitting the credential `create` API call into: `connectCreate` and `connectCloudCreate` so the multi-step code would not have to handle defaulting of unnecessary params.
- Refactoring the steps in the `newDeployment.ts` file to use simple if/else logic for skipping steps rather than fall through logic so the backward history navigation works as expected with children sub-flows.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [x] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

Almost all the multi-steps in the `newCredential.ts` file have been extracted into either `newConnectCredential.ts` or `newConnectCloudCredential.ts`. The only step(s) left in the `newCredential.ts` file are the ones common to creating a new Connect credential or a new Connect Cloud credential.

Now the `newConnectCredential.ts` file is responsible for encapsulating all the Connect specific steps and validation for creating a new Connect credential. The `newConnectCloudCredential.ts` file is responsible for encapsulating all the Connect Cloud specific steps and validation for creating a new Connect Cloud credential. Therefore making the `newCredential` flow very slim and a parent to the `newConnectCredential` flow and the `newConnectCloudCredential` flow.

All steps for creating a new credential have been removed from the `newDeployment.ts` file and now the `newDeployment` flow is a parent flow to the `newCredential` flow.

The big benefit here is that we have removed all the multi-step code duplication for creating a new credential between the `newCredential.ts` file and the `newDeployment.ts` tile.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

None.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

Existing E2E tests succeeded locally for this branch.

## Directions for Reviewers

<!-- Provide steps for reviewers to validate this change manually. -->

Everything for creating new deployments and creating new credentials should be manually tested.
- [ ] Create a new Connect credential with:
  - [ ] An API key
  - [ ] A Token
  - [ ] A Snowflake connection
- [ ] Create a new Connect Cloud credential with a user having:
  - [ ] A single account
  - [ ] Multiple accounts
  - [ ] No accounts at all
  - [ ] A read-only account (viewer/guest role)
- [ ] Create a new deployment:
  - [ ] When there are zero credentials available and the user is obligated to create their very first credential
  - [ ] Using an existing Connect credential
  - [ ] With a new Connect credential (when there are other credentials available)
  - [ ] With a pre-selected entry point file
  - [ ] With multiple matching content types, so the user is forced to select a content type

if you want to try this yourself locally, I have a couple scripts on my local that you can use to do that:

*deploy.sh* - do the initial deployment
```
#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -e

echo 'removing previous deployments'
rm -rf test/sample-content/quarto-proj-py/.posit/publish/deployments

echo 'creating deployment record'
 curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/deployments \
 -d '{"account": "cloudy", "config": "publisher-test-RFPN.toml", "saveName": "the_save_name"}'

echo 'doing deploy'
 curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/deployments/the_save_name \
 -d '{"account": "cloudy", "config": "publisher-test-RFPN.toml"}'
```

*deploy2.sh* - republish to existing content
```
#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -e

content_id=$(cat test/sample-content/quarto-proj-py/.posit/publish/deployments/the_save_name.toml | dasel -r toml .id)
# strip leading and trailing single quotes
content_id=$(echo $content_id | sed "s/'//g")


echo 'creating deployment record'
 curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/deployments \
 -d "{\"account\": \"cloudy\", \"config\": \"publisher-test-RFPN.toml\", \"saveName\": \"republish\", \"id\": \"$content_id\"}"

echo 'doing deploy'
 curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/deployments/republish \
 -d '{"account": "cloudy", "config": "publisher-test-RFPN.toml"}'
```

title: Introducing the new credential user flows for Connect Cloud
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->

Resolves #2672
Resolves #2674
Resolves #2714
Resolves #2715
Resolves #2716
Resolves #2675

Introducing the new Connect Cloud create new credential user flows:
- **Flow 1**: There is only one publishable account for the user, auto select it to create the credential.
- **Flow 2**: There are multiple publishable accounts for the user, display the account selector so the user may select the account to create the credential.
- **Flow 3**: There are no publishable accounts for the user, but they have at least one read-only account (guest/viewer). Ask if they want to sign up for another Connect Cloud account. If they do, open a browser so they may create another user profile and finish setting up the account in Connect Cloud and use the new account to create the credential.
- **Flow 4**: There are zero accounts for the user (they must be going through the sign up process), open a browser to finish setting up the account in Connect Cloud and use the new account to create the credential.

The intent here was to introduce all the fully working user flows for creating a Connect Cloud credential isolated from other major building blocks or code refactors in the multi-stepper code. These user flows were introduced for creating a new credential (stand-alone) and for creating a new credential while creating a new deployment. 

A few other smaller and needed changes were also introduced: 
- Added the new Connect Cloud data to the credentials object and create API call.
- Introduced a new generic api polling info message input object for the multi-stepper to display while polling and API.
- Custom error types for the known device auth errors.

Introducing environment variables and APIs for Connect Cloud credential support. The intent here is to introduce building blocks needed for adding the Connect Cloud credential support. This PR does not make use of the new api calls introduced, it just introduces them into the code base. PR #2754 will use these new API calls.

A new environment variable has been introduced for Connect Cloud (`CONNECT_CLOUD_ENV `) and if present, it can have any of the following valid values:
- `development`
- `staging` 
- `production`

In the future, the new `CONNECT_CLOUD_ENV ` variable should default to `production` when missing from the environment. For now it defaults to `staging` since the integrating code changes are not yet available in the Connect Cloud `production` environment. The current default for running the extension in development mode is `staging`.

This Connect Cloud environment variable is needed for development and will aid the E2E tests automation via CI so the environment can be set correctly for testing purposes. 

The new `CONNECT_CLOUD_ENV ` variable is also used in the new API functions. It's value is set in the request header so the agent code will use the correct Connect Cloud URLs for the chosen environment. 

The other environment variables introduced (localized to `json` environment files) are:
- `cloudURL`: To be used to open a browser window from the extension to register a new user.

title: check for existing credential by combination of URL and account name
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Currently we have checks in place to prevent users from creating new credentials for the same server URL. However, we want users to be able to create multiple credentials for Connect Cloud (but not with the same account). That means we have to compare both the credential URL and account instead of just the URL.

We'll also have to make changes in the extension code, which performs a similar validation.

## Type of Change

none.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->

Added assertions for:
- When a user creates a duplicate cloud credential
- When a user creates a non-duplicate cloud credential with the same URL

## Directions for Reviewers

Run the following curls:
```
curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/credentials -d '{"name": "foo", "serverType": "connect_cloud", "url": "https://api.connect.posit.cloud", "accountId": "123", "accountName": "my account", "refreshToken": "blah", "accessToken": "blah"}'

^ should succeed

curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/credentials -d '{"name": "foo", "serverType": "connect_cloud", "url": "https://api.connect.posit.cloud", "accountId": "123", "accountName": "my account", "refreshToken": "blah", "accessToken": "blah"}'

^ should fail

curl -X POST localhost:9001/api/credentials -d '{"name": "foo 2", "serverType": "connect_cloud", "url": "https://api.connect.posit.cloud", "accountId": "456", "accountName": "my account 2", "refreshToken": "blah", "accessToken": "blah"}'

^ should succeed

```

      },
      {
        "id": "account2",
        "name": "Account 2",
        "permissionToPublish": true
      },
      {
        "id": "account3",
        "name": "Account 3",

title: Fix issue with account list initialization not using the keychain setting
description:
## Intent

Resolves #2697 

## Type of Change

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

An account list was being created before the keychain setting was resolved, which could lead to incorrect behavior if the keychain was not enabled. The account list should be created after the keychain setting is determined.

This PR ensures the account list is initialized only after the keychain setting is resolved.

- Removed the obsolete Accounts field from CLIContext and its constructor signature.
- Moved accounts.NewAccountList call from main.go into UICmd.Run after UseKeychain is set.
- Updated changelogs in both root and VSCode extension to document the fix.

## User Impact

<!-- Describe how this change will affect users. -->
<!-- Specifically changes to the flow and trade-offs we are making. -->

This change fixes a bug, that would mostly affect developers as they test the different credential services.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

Github review recommended additional unit tests, so I asked CoPilot to write them, using the information provided within the CoPilot review comment. Here was my Prompt:

And here is the summary of the test updates (new file: `cmd/publisher/commands/ui_test.go`)  from CoPilot, using a Claude 4 LLM:

<details> 
<summary> CoPilot generated: UICmd.Run Unit Tests - Testing UseKeychain Initialization Logic</summary>

### Overview

This test suite provides comprehensive coverage for the `UICmd.Run` method, specifically focusing on the critical bug where the account list was being initialized before the `UseKeychain` setting was properly resolved.

### Test Coverage

#### Core Tests for UseKeychain Behavior

1. **TestUICmd_Run_UseKeychainEnabled** - Verifies that when `UseKeychain` is set to `true`, the global `credentials.UseKeychain` variable is correctly set before account list creation.

2. **TestUICmd_Run_UseKeychainDisabled** - Verifies that when `UseKeychain` is set to `false`, the global `credentials.UseKeychain` variable is correctly set before account list creation.

#### Edge Cases and Error Handling

3. **TestUICmd_Run_InvalidPath** - Tests path resolution with invalid paths to ensure error handling works correctly.

4. **TestUICmd_Run_KeychainToggling** - Tests that the `UseKeychain` setting is properly applied regardless of the initial state of the global variable.

5. **TestUICmd_Run_ConcurrentAccess** - Tests that multiple `UICmd` instances don't interfere with each other's `UseKeychain` settings.

#### Integration and Comprehensive Tests

6. **TestUICmd_Run_ActualAccountListCreation** - Comprehensive test that verifies account list creation works correctly with different `UseKeychain` settings, including all four combinations of initial and final states.

7. **TestUICmd_Run_IntegrationFlow** - Tests the complete initialization flow for both keychain enabled and disabled scenarios.

8. **TestUICmd_Run_RaceConditionPrevention** - Demonstrates that the fix prevents race conditions where multiple commands could interfere with each other.

9. **TestUICmd_Run_OperationOrder** - Verifies that operations happen in the correct order: path resolution, `UseKeychain` setting, then account list creation.

10. **TestUICmd_Run_AccountListInitializationOrder** - Specifically tests the bug that was fixed, ensuring account list is created after `UseKeychain` is resolved.

#### Edge Case Tests

11. **TestUICmd_Run_DefaultValues** - Tests that struct field default values are properly handled.

12. **TestUICmd_Run_MockServerIntegration** - Integration test with mock HTTP server to test the full flow.

### Key Testing Scenarios

The tests cover these critical scenarios:

#### UseKeychain State Transitions
- `true` → `true` (no change)
- `true` → `false` (disable keychain)
- `false` → `true` (enable keychain)
- `false` → `false` (no change)

#### Bug Prevention
- **Before Fix**: Account list was created before `UseKeychain` was set, causing it to use the wrong credential provider
- **After Fix**: Account list is created after `UseKeychain` is properly set, ensuring correct credential provider selection

#### Race Condition Prevention
- Multiple `UICmd` instances with different `UseKeychain` values
- Concurrent access to the global `credentials.UseKeychain` variable
- Proper isolation between different command executions

### Test Structure

All tests use the `testify/suite` framework and follow these patterns:

- **Setup**: Mock filesystem, restore original `UseKeychain` state
- **Execution**: Simulate the critical parts of `UICmd.Run`
- **Verification**: Assert that `UseKeychain` is set correctly before account list creation
- **Cleanup**: Restore original state to prevent test interference

### Mock Strategy

The tests use mocking strategically:

- **Filesystem**: Uses `utiltest.NewMockFs()` for file system operations
- **HTTP Server**: Uses `httptest.NewServer()` for integration tests
- **Account List**: Uses mock functions to simulate account list creation without dependencies
- **Keyring**: Uses `keyring.MockInit()` for credential storage testing

### Benefits

1. **Comprehensive Coverage**: Tests all aspects of the `UseKeychain` initialization logic
2. **Bug Prevention**: Specifically tests the bug that was fixed
3. **Regression Testing**: Ensures the fix doesn't break in future changes
4. **Documentation**: Tests serve as documentation for the expected behavior
5. **Maintainability**: Well-structured tests that are easy to understand and maintain

### Usage

Run the tests with:
```bash
cd /Users/billsager/dev/publisher && go test ./cmd/publisher/commands/... -v
```

The tests are designed to be fast, reliable, and independent, making them suitable for CI/CD pipelines and development workflows.

</details>

<details><summary>Refactored after Github review suggested optimization of new unit tests</summary>

### UICmd Test Suite Refactoring Summary

#### Overview

The original test suite contained **12 individual test methods** with **600+ lines of repetitive code**. The refactored version consolidates this into **6 focused test methods** with **~330 lines** using table-driven tests and shared helper functions.

#### Key Improvements

##### 1. **Eliminated Code Duplication**

- **After**: Shared helper functions handle common operations

##### 2. **Table-Driven Tests**

##### 4. **Better Organization**

#### Test Coverage Comparison

3. `TestUICmd_Run_InvalidPath`
4. `TestUICmd_Run_KeychainToggling`

#### Benefits of Refactoring

##### **Maintainability**

- **Less code to maintain** (600+ lines → ~330 lines)

##### **Extensibility**

- **Easy to add new scenarios** by extending test tables
- **Reusable components** for future tests
- **Modular design** allows selective testing
- **Future-proof** structure for additional test cases

#### Test Execution Results

All refactored tests pass successfully:

- **Total test scenarios**: 17 (expanded from 12)
- **Test execution time**: ~0.6 seconds
- **Code coverage**: Maintains same coverage as original
- **All edge cases preserved**: No functionality lost in refactoring

#### Code Quality Metrics

##### **Lines of Code**

#### Conclusion

The refactored test suite maintains **100% of the original functionality** while being significantly more maintainable, readable, and extensible. The table-driven approach makes it easy to add new test scenarios, and the shared helper functions ensure consistency across all tests.

The core functionality being tested - the UseKeychain initialization bug fix - is now more clearly demonstrated and thoroughly tested across all relevant scenarios.

title: schema changes for posit connect cloud
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

Resolves https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2677.

The changes to the schema in v4 are:
- publishing schema:
  - Add `.server_type` field, defaulting to `connect`
  - Rename draft field `.connect.access` to `.connect.access_control`
  - Add `.connect_cloud` field
    - Contains the following fields:
      - `.vanity_name`
      - `.access_control`
        - `public_access`: boolean
        - `organization_access`: `disabled` | `viewer` | `editor`
    - Contains a subset of of the fields previously allowed for Connect. The following fields are not settable for PCC: 
      - `.has_parameters`
      - `.python.package_file`
      - `.python.package_manager`
      - `.python.requires_python`
      - `.r.package_file`
      - `.r.package_manager`
      - `.r.requires_r`
      - `.jupyter.hide_all_input`
      - `.jupyter.hide_tagged_input`
      - `.quarto.version`
      - `.quarto.engines`
      - `.connect`
- Publishing record schema:

title: add device auth and token endpoints
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Resolves https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2670.
Resolves https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2671.

Adds two endpoints which will be used to authenticate through the OAuth device flow for Connect Cloud. The steps to use these will be as follows:

1. Extension calls the device auth endpoint
1. Extension starts polling the token exchange endpoint in the background
1. Extension opens the verification URI in the browser
1. User logs in and confirm the auth request
1. Token exchange succeeds, returning the access and refresh tokens to be saved later in the keyring/creds file

API requests and responses are as follows:

```
POST /connect-cloud/device-auth
Cloud-Auth-Base-Url: https://login.staging.posit.cloud

// response body
{
  "deviceCode": "abc",
  "userCode": "abc",
  "verificationURIComplete": "https://login.staging.posit.cloud/wherever-this-page-will-be",
  "interval": 5
}
```
```
POST /connect-cloud/oauth/token
Cloud-Auth-Base-Url: https://api.login.staging.posit.cloud

// request body
{
  "deviceCode": "abc"
}

// response body
{
  "accessToken": "abc",
  "refreshToken": "abc",
  "expiresIn": 1800
}

// response body - HTTP 400
{
  "code": "deviceAuthPending" // values: deviceAuthPending, deviceAuthSlowDown, deviceAuthAccessDenied, deviceAuthExpiredToken, unknown
}
```

title: support snowflake config.toml and environment variable overrides
description:
[note: this is layered on top of #2687 which should land first]

## Intent

Support more snowflake connection configs:

- `config.toml` (if this and `connections.toml` both exist, `connections.toml` wins)
- per-connection field env var overrides

Fixes posit-dev/connect#31773

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

Followed the behavior in https://github.com/posit-dev/snowflakeauth/, except for the "default connection" support, which doesn't make a ton of sense in the publisher paradigm (we present the user with a list of connection options to choose from, rather than the user entering a connection name or falling back on a default connection name.)

Also ignoring unnamed connection env vars (e.g. `SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`) because which connection would it apply to? All of them? I think this would be a confusing behavior for the publisher flow, especially as we are not handling default connection options either.

- Look for `config.toml` in the same set of directories as `connections.toml`, but only if we have not found a `connections.toml`.
- Handle parsing the different file formats.
- For each connection, check the environment for named overrides and apply if found.

## User Impact

Snowflake users will have better automatic support for more varieties of snowflake configuration.

## Automated Tests

Added new tests to `connection_test.go`.

## Directions for Reviewers

I tested by launching publisher and adding a new credential, with https://bf2oiaib-duloftf-posit-software-pbc-dev.snowflakecomputing.app as the server URL. Publisher loads the connections and tests them and presents a list of valid connections, so I looked for the expected list of connection names.

### Config.toml support 

Tested with a `config.toml` in my snowflake config home. Verified I saw the right connection names.

Added a `connections.toml` alongside with different connections. Verified that I saw the connections from that file instead (connections takes precedence over config).

### Env var support

Given a TOML file with a working `default` connection and a non-working `workbench` connection (`workbench is missing a valid token):

```toml
[default]
account = "duloftf-posit-software-pbc-dev"
user = "chris@posit.co"
authenticator = "SNOWFLAKE_JWT"
private_key_file = "/Users/chris/.snowflake/rsa_key.p8"

[workbench]
account = "duloftf-posit-software-pbc-dev"
authenticator = "oauth"
```

I verified that Publisher offered me the `default` connection but not the `workbench` connection.

Closed Code, set env vars, relaunched code:

```shell
❯ export SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_WORKBENCH_TOKEN="[token from workbench]"
❯ export SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT=foo
❯ code
```

I verified that Publisher now offered me the `workbench` connection (it has a valid token now) but no longer offered me the `default` connection (it has an invalid account name now.) This proves that Publisher is using the env var overrides.

title: Adding the platform selector and refactoring the new credential code
description:
This PR introduces the initial platform selector needed for adding Connect Cloud support into the Publisher plugin. The platform selector is hidden by default behind the `enableConnectCloud` config option and it is not meant to be used yet at all since there are more changes needed before it can be used. If the `enableConnectCloud` configuration option were to be tuned on by a user, they would see the platform selector with two options ("Posit Connect Cloud" & " Posit Connect") but selecting either option would still take them through the Connect flow for adding a new credential, so for now all roads lead to Rome.

The multi-stepper code has been refactored to "jump" steps accordingly with the value of the `serverType` instead of "falling through" the non-applicable steps when adding a new credential. These changes were made to facilitate adding support of new platforms into the plugin such as Connect Cloud.

A new icon has been added for the Posit logo using the `npm run build-font` script to generate the appropriate icon-font and CSS file to make the icon available to the multi-stepper.

## Intent

Resolves [#2685](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2685)

## Type of Change

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [x] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

As of today the Publisher plugin only supports deployments onto a Posit Connect server running on user hosted infrastructure or a Posit Connect server running on Snowflake's SPCS infrastructure. Each of these have different credential needs hence their `serverType` is different but both are supporting the same platform: Posit Connect.

I have introduced a platform selector so new platforms such as Posit Connect Cloud can be supported and differentiated. For all purposes the platform selector will treat a Posit Connect server running on user hosted infrastructure the same as a Posit Connect server running on Snowflake's SPCS infrastructure. In order words those two flavors of Connect will be a single choice in the platform selector: "Posit Connect". However, they will be treated differently when adding a new credential once the server URL has been provided as it is implemented today.

New platforms such as Posit Connect Cloud will have their own entry in the platform selector so all the different multi-stepper steps can be properly handled. Adding the platform selector and refactoring the multi-stepper code to "jump" directly to applicable steps will simplify adding new platforms to the plugin.

## User Impact

These changes will not have any user impact since they are hidden by default behind a configuration option and the E2E tests have been run successfully against this branch.

## Automated Tests

Unit tests have been added for the testable parts of this change. No new E2E tests have been added yet for the platform selector since it is hidden by default behind a configuration option. New E2E tests will be added later on when more bits are working for supporting multiple platforms.

## Directions for Reviewers

Validation of the existing flow for adding a new credential should be tested and it is expected to be working correctly including adding a new credential separately from adding a new deployment or as part of adding a new deployment.

- [x] I have updated [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

title: add support for Snowflake "oauth" authenticator
description:
## Intent

Support "oauth" authenticator connection type.

This works with the connection automatically configured by Posit Workbench when Snowflake session credentials are enabled.

Uses the alternative auth approach mentioned at
https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark-container-services/working-with-services#ingress-authentication. That is, we issue a login request using the oauth token from the configured connection, then retrieve a session token from the response.

Related UI change: the snowflake connection quickpick list always displays, even if there is only one connection. We found in testing that it was confusing that sometimes you get a choice, and sometimes publisher just implicitly picks (and you don't know which connection it picked.)

Fixes posit-dev/connect#31770

## Type of Change


- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->

## Approach

Refactored the existing JWT auth support into a new interface (TokenProvider). Added OAuth implementation. Updated snowflake authenticator to pick the appropriate TokenProvider based on the connection config. Added new fields to connection config parser.

## User Impact

Workbench users who are trying to deploy to Connect in SPCS while using Snowflake session credentials will get a "workbench" connection option.

## Automated Tests

Updated existing tests along with refactor, and added tests of new token provider.

## Directions for Reviewers

If you launch a new VS Code workbench session with snowflake credentials enabled, workbench will automatically generate a `connections.toml`. You can copy that to your local `connections.toml` to test locally (but you will need to refresh it periodically as the token expires.) (`cat $SNOWFLAKE_HOME/connections.toml` from the VS Code terminal.)

Example:

```toml

account = "duloftf-posit-software-pbc-dev"
token = "ver:1-hint:1407662650122246-"
authenticator = "oauth"
```

title: Quote paths to support windows
description:
## Intent

Added functional tests for calling into R from Windows (and particularly when R is installed by rig). Those confirmed the failure. Due to the [way quotes work in windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/archive/blogs/twistylittlepassagesallalike/everyone-quotes-command-line-arguments-the-wrong-way), when the R executable was a `.bat`, we needed to do more + different quoting than we already were for the scripts we shelled out to. This PR changes those to write the script portions out to files and then use `R... -f ...` to run them. This is more robust since we don't have to worry about quoting within the contents of the script.

Resolves #2598

title: snowflake support (MVP)
description:
## Intent

MVP allowing Publisher to deploy to Connect running in Snowflake SPCS.

We cannot use Connect API Keys in this scenario. Instead, the user must have Snowflake connections configured on their host, which the Publisher will then use to authenticate requests to Connect.

The MVP only supports key pair authentication, meaning you must have a connections.toml with a `private_key_file`, `account`, and `user` defined.

Public documentation is not included in this PR as SPCS support is not being publicized yet.

Fixes posit-dev/connect#30701

## Type of Change

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

Modify "new credential" flow:
- "input server URL" sends a test request to the backend; the response now includes "server type"
- if "server type" is "snowflake", the next step is "input snowflake connection"; otherwise existing "input API key" is used
- "input snowflake connection" asks the backend to return available snowflake connections (must be already configured on host)
  - connections are tested against the server URL
  - if only 1 option, pick that option
  - if > 1, present quickpick
  - if 0, error
- server nickname step is unchanged

Modify "new deployment" flow: the optional "add credential" subflow is modified similar to above.

Add "snowflake connection" field to account/credential records. Either API Key or Snowflake Connection must be populated. This means there is now a new Credential version.

Add snowflake server type detection. This also means I needed to modify the deployment schema to accept "snowflake" as a server type.

Add Snowflake authenticator that generates and applies auth headers to HTTP client requests.

Add `/api/snowflake-connections` endpoint to report snowflake connections that work against a given server url.

Add code to load snowflake connection configs.

## User Impact

Most users will not be impacted. The publishing flow will continue to work as before.

Users deploying to Connect in SPCS will now be able to use Publisher. The tool will autodetect when they are deploying to SPCS and do the right thing. Errors will include guidance and links to Snowflake documentation.

## Automated Tests

Updated/added unit tests for new and modified code.

## Directions for Reviewers

Both methods for adding a credential (as a standalone flow, or as part of adding a deployment" have been tested. Chaita and I have tested deployments to dogfood via API key (unchanged) and deployments to https://nagoiaib-duloftf-posit-software-pbc-dev.snowflakecomputing.app/ via key pair auth.

Manual testing notes here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Yy6nAveS3c2Qunaw9hMgh9715IrI0oAp5ugssSCnXTg/edit?tab=t.0

title: Handle workspace trust states
description: ## Intent This PR provides the publisher extension with the functionality to support running within Restricted Mode. When in restricted mode, all publishing functionality is hidden, with only a button made available to manage the trust of the workspace (which is common with other extensions). If and when the workspace is trusted by the user, the extension will commence its initialization. If the workspace is untrusted once again, the publisher returns to its restricted view. Resolves #2611 ## Type of Change - - [ ] Bug Fix - - [x] New Feature - - [ ] Breaking Change - - [ ] Documentation - - [ ] Refactor - - [ ] Tooling ## Approach At activation, the code will check if it is being activated in trusted mode or not. If it is, it proceeds with initialization. If restricted mode is active instead, it registers an event handler for when trust is granted to proceed with initialization. The views and commands configured within `package.json` have been updated to use the context that VSCode API provides (`isWorkspaceTrusted`) When in restricted mode, clicking on the publisher icon will show this view: ## User Impact User should see no difference in functionality for trusted folders. In restricted mode, they will now see an experience much more common to what other extensions do. ## Automated Tests ## Directions for Reviewers Launch VSCode with the extension and open a folder which you have not trusted. If you need to force one to be untrusted, you can use the pallete command of "Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust" and untrust the open workspace. Then confirm that you only see the view described above. Confirm that the button will bring up the trust management page, and click trust. Confirm that the publisher extension initializes and is functional. You can then untrust the workspace and confirm that the extension switches back to the restricted mode. Confirm that you see no difference from before if you open a trusted workspace/folder. ## Checklist - [ ] I have updated [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

title: Support detecting python interpreter requirements from standard files
description:
## Intent

Newer connect versions support a `environment.python.requires` option that tells the server which version of Python can be used to run the content. This constraint is meant to be detected from `.python-version`,`pyproject.toml` and `setup.cfg`. The support was already done in `rsconnect-python` and this PR adds the same capability to the publisher.

## Type of Change

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

The `defaultPythonInspector` will use a newly added `PyProjectPythonRequires` entity to determine if the python project has any constraint over the Python version that should be used to run the project.
If such constraint is detected the `defaultInitialize` will add it to the newly generated project configuration which will then be used to generate the Manifest including that option.

## User Impact

If the user had provided a interpreter version constraint in any of the 3 supported files, the constraint will now be propagated to Connect.

## Automated Tests

- [ ] Added an test for a newly generated manifest out of a project with requirements

## Directions for Reviewers

There is an open question about the fact that currently the information detected from the inspector is mostly ignored and replaced with hardcoded answers from the interpreters API. So that might heavily influence this PR structure as it evolves.

This PR suppresses the Posit Publisher Log panel view until the user has clicked the deployment button from within the publishing extension. Until they do so, it remains hidden as it has no value until a deployment is initiated.

I added an additional context within the view's `when` definition, initialized it to "false" at extension startup, and set it to "true"  when the user initiates the deployment.
