<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The tough part of this implementation was to find a clean way to restore the last selections to reflect the last state, vs the other times which we'll update the selections w/ business logic. So we needed to make sure that the business logic updates to selected configuration (which are made to reflect the last config used to deploy) and the update to credential (which is made to makes sure the account selected matches the deployment URL - either by validating the currently selected one or by switching to the first in the filtered list), are only executed when the deployment choice is changed by the user, rather than programmatically. By doing this, it allows us to set all three select box values to what was last persisted.

So we will restore the settings upon initialization of the Home View WebViewView, and then we record the settings into VSCode storage each time they are changed (either the Home View Deploy button is collapsed or expanded, or any of the select choices are changed - either programmatically or by the user).

We are using workspace storage for these settings, so they are set on a per workspace basis as the name implies. ~~There is no API available to clear them, but I have used this technique to clear all workspace knowledge from VSCode:~~

~~https://stackoverflow.com/a/71178197~~

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

## Directions for Reviewers

<!-- Provide steps for reviewers to validate this change manually. -->

You'll want to have multiple deployments, multiple configurations and multiple credentials with which you can use for validation. On the credentials, you can use the same API key across multiple accounts, so just duplicate up a few to the same server. You'll want to have credentials for two different servers, but also multiple credentials for at least one of them.

As I mentioned in the overview, the last used settings are restored when the Home View is initialized. This allows you to be able to test and reproduce this cycle by using the pallet command: "Developer: Reload Windows" each time you want to test if the values you currently have will be restored.

To start with, you should just verify that after making some changes to the select boxes, you can reload the window and then see that those same values are restored.

After that works, you'll want to verify that the business logic that occurs when a user selects a deployment (and then we automatically select the configuration last used for the deployment or to setup the pre-deployment, along with then making sure the account selected matches the deployment URL - either by validating the currently selected one or by switching to the first in the filtered list), is not being used to initially set the values upon reload. 

To do this:

1. select a different deployment and record which config and credential are selected.
2. Change both of them to something else. 
3. Now reload the extension with the command: "Developer: Reload Windows"
4. Make sure the values persist from your last selection. 
5. Then switch to a different deployment and notice everything possibly changing
6. Then switch back to that previous deployment and confirm that the business logic is in effect and that the last configuration used for deployment and the first matching account or currently matching account is selected.

There are also some edge conditions in which changes of available selection options are taken into account. For example, if a user selects a particular configuration, closes that workspace or VSCode itself, and then removes the configuration file they had selected physically from the filesystem, the initialization process is smart enough to simply fall back to business rules. However, it should be mentioned that we have an outstanding issues which need to handle when there are no longer configurations or when there are no matching credentials available that could be used with a deployment (#1280), so please do not expect that those conditions are handled yet as part of this PR.

There are a good number of combinations here, but by going through these a few times, you can pretty much validate that the implementation matches the intentions.

If you have any question of results, please reach out. For the most part, the validation of this PR is to make sure the values last used is restored ignoring those business rules, and the actual business rule validation is part of a different PR already merged.

title: Force re-render of PSelect when props change
description:
Force re-render of `PSelect` when props change to avoid `vscode-dropdown` the index selection visual bug.

## Intent

Resolves #1349

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

The approach here was after attempts to create our own dropdown detailed in #1349.

What gets this to work is [`:key`](https://vuejs.org/api/built-in-special-attributes.html#key).

> It can also be used to force replacement of an element/component instead of reusing it. This can be useful when you want to:
> - Properly trigger lifecycle hooks of a component
> - Trigger transitions

So when `:key` changes on the `vscode-dropdown` Vue will completely replace it. When props change we change the key causing a full re-render avoiding [the bug causing this](https://github.com/microsoft/fast/issues/5773) entirely.

Iterating from `0` can be done because:

> Children of the same common parent must have unique keys. Duplicate keys will cause render errors.

Meaning as long as the number is unique in `PSelect` we are good.

## Directions for Reviewers

This one is tough to review. I recommend adding the below to `App.vue` when testing this locally:

```vue
 {{ selectedDeployment?.saveName || "Nothing Selected" }}
```

That way you can see the true value of `selectedDeployment` and see if the `PSelect` is showing the right value.

To reproduce the bug that this fixes you can:

1. Have a single Deployment named `quarto`
2. Open the Home View ensuring `quarto` is selected
3. Open the Deployments view and create a `python` deployment

Because `python` is before `quarto` alphabetically the `vscode-dropdown` would visually change the selection (but only visually) to `python`. With this PR it will show the correct value.

Each of the file watchers called the same refresh method, regardless of the type of triggering file.

title: Make homeView `_refreshData` fully async
description:
Holding until Alpha 5 releases.

This PR changes up the `_refreshData` function in the `HomeViewProvider` to be fully async without synchronously calling the API.

## Intent

Part of #1276

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [x] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

There are a few ways to do this, but the one I went with for this code block was using [`Promise.all()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/all). Here are the reasons why:

Promise.all()` waits for each promise to be fulfilled before continuing, but in this case allows all of our API calls to make their requests at once

`Promise.all()` fails with the first rejection
This code block doesn't really care too much about how to handle each failure. They all handle it the same way, the only difference was the code that triggered it. In this case I just changed the string to be more general to this function as opposed to the API call that caused it.

title: Create `PSelect` Vue component for wrapping VSCode dropdown
description:
This PR introduces a Vue component wrapper around [`vscode-dropdown`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-webview-ui-toolkit/tree/main/src/dropdown) and [`vscode-option`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-webview-ui-toolkit/blob/main/src/option) for easy conversion between any possible `v-model` to a string for use by the VSCode Toolkit components.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [x] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

The approach here was to utilize generics in the `PSelect` component to establish two props:
- `options` which contains the array of things to populate all of the `vscode-option`s
- `getKey` a function to get the string for use by the VSCode components

With Vue generics we get checking automatically if `getKey` doesn't work for the `options` provided.

Inside the component we have an inner selection called `_selection` which tracks the string the VSCode components are tracking. When that changes via the `<vscode-dropdown>` a `@change` event is triggered which will update the inner selection, and the `v-model` by finding the appropriate option in `options` which produces the key.

`getKey` must produce a KEY - it must be unique or this will not function.

Example usage:
```typescript
        <PSelect
          v-model="deployment"
          :options="deployments"
          :get-key="(d) => d.saveName"
        />
```

The above is how this component will be used.

title: remove timing issue by making sure selection exists in select values
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Eliminate a race condition, which was temporarily handled with a "fragile" hack.

Resolves #1277 

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [ ] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [x] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

Root cause for the timing issue was the requirement to wait until select values had been updated to include the desired selection (which was a new entry due to the add operations for config or deployment files). The actual message which would update the selection is a result of a file watch (for the new config or deployment file creation) and it's arrival was undeterministic. This is why the hack worked, as it waited a second for the entries to be updated.

Solution to this was to check if the desired selection was a part of the selection list, and if not, then having it temporarily added. This works because we do know that a refresh will be coming in shortly and that the deployment object for the selected deployment will be updated as part of that refresh. (The config has no parallel concept/complications)

Manually refreshing will reset the entry which was temporarily added as part of this fix, but you'd expect that the selected value will be included in the next refresh_data message which comes as part of that refresh.

## Automated Tests

<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

## Directions for Reviewers

<!-- Provide steps for reviewers to validate this change manually. -->

Within the home view:
1. Add a new deployment file and confirm that the deployments select box now has the newly added deployment file selected without any user action required. Confirm that deployment is initiated with the correct values.
2. Add a new configuration file and confirm that the configuration select box now has the newly added configuration file selected without any user action required. Confirm that deployment is initiated with the correct values.
3. Add another new deployment file and this time select a different configuration file within the multi-stepper than is selected within the home view. Upon multi-step completion, both the new deployment and it's configuration file should be selected without additional user actions required. Confirm that deployment is initiated with the correct values.
4. Try the multi-step operations above and make sure that aborting the multi-step prompts (by hitting ESC or clicking away, ahead of completion) do not update the selected values.

This PR saves and restores the choices that the user has made for selections within the Home View. This allows consistency across restarts of VSCode and changes of workspace/folders.

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->

There are four attributes persisted here, within the Workspace folder storage. This means that depending on the folder opened, different values are saved/restored. So you get a persistence for each of your different projects (with our current implementation of one folder, one `.posit` directory.

Attributes persisted:
- is the deployment accordion  expanded or not?
- last selected deployment name
- last selected configuration name
- last selected credential/account name

While these values are initially set, the business rules still apply. So if a choice has been saved but no longer exists or is invalid for the selection, then you'll see a different value selected.

title: Defer creation of file watchers until views are loading data
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

This PR defers creation of the file watchers until the first call to load data (`getChildren` for tree views, `_refreshData` for the home view). This will hopefully address/work around the issue with file watchers on Linux not working if they are registered before the `.posit` directory is created.

Fixes #1216

## Type of Change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- - [x] Bug Fix <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- - [ ] New Feature <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- - [ ] Breaking Change <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
- - [ ] Documentation <!-- User or developer documentation -->
- - [ ] Refactor <!-- Code restructuring -->
- - [ ] Tooling <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach

Pass the extension `context` into the view constructors rather than the `register` method. Views retain the `context` so they can use it when registering the file watchers, and views keep track of the file watcher so they know if it's already been created.

## Automated Tests

No tests in the VSCode extension yet.

## Directions for Reviewers

Run the extension, check that the file watchers work (create, edit, and delete configuration, deployment, and application files and see that the views update). Specifically validate the linked issue.

title: Fix tsconfig to use DOM lib with Vue
description:
We can see in our `web` directory that we should have the `DOM` and `DOM.Iterable` in the webview / Vue TSConfig. We can use Vue's `tsconfig.dom.json` for this so we can access the DOM functions without explicitly typing them. 

We can see the `DOM` and `DOM.Iterable` in the `lib` in the [Vue / Vite template too](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-mtgxmx?file=tsconfig.json&terminal=dev).

However `tsconfig.dom.json` empties the types array

> Set to empty to avoid accidental inclusion of unwanted types

This breaks `acquireVsCodeApi` so we can tell TSConfig that when in Vue components we should have access to it by included its types.

title: Rename error field in pre-deployment API response
description: ## Intent This PR fixes the usage of the `error` field in the deployments API responses. Front-end types and the `isSuccessful` function on deployments have been updated to match. Fixes #1247 ## Type of Change - - [x] Bug Fix - - [ ] New Feature - - [ ] Breaking Change - - [ ] Documentation - - [ ] Refactor - - [ ] Tooling ## Approach There are two error-related fields in the deployment API responses: * `error` is used in an error response, to indicate that the deployment can't be loaded (for example, because it has invalid TOML syntax). There is no deployment record returned. * `deploymentError` is part of the deployment record and is used to indicate that the last deployment attempt ended with an error. The record itself is valid (no `error`). Currently, pre-deployments are putting their "last deployment error" in the `error` field. ## Automated Tests API tests don't cover DTO field naming; they decode into a DTO object and assert field values. So this is not covered by a test. ## Directions for Reviewers The deployments part of the UI should show the correct icon if a deployment file includes an error. For example, if your deployment record contains: ``` [deployment-error] code = 'pythonNotAvailable' message = "Python 3.99 is not available on the server.\nConsider editing your configuration file to request one of the available versions:\n3.8.1, 3.9.7, 3.10.10, 3.11.3." operation = 'publish/checkCapabilities' ``` You should see the "deployment failed" icon not the "invalid file" icon

## Approach

The `configurationName` and `configurationPath` are present in the deployment or pre-deployment returned from the API and from the related `GET` APIs. Frontend API types have been updated to reflect this. There is a difference between a pre-deployment (where those fields are optional) and a full deployment, where they are always present.

If you want to test the API directly, you can call `POST /api/deployments` with `account` and `saveName`, and try also adding `config` (which should be the name of an existing configuration if you want the call to succeed). If you specify `config`, you should get back `configurationName` and `configurationPath` in the response.

This is PR 3 of 3 which will implement the new Home View for the Publisher VSCode Extension.

The code within this PR builds upon the PR #1249 to implement the new "Home" view, which functions as the "simplified user interface" we've been discussing for some time.

description:
Now that most directories handle Prettier formatting well we can move the Prettier formatting to the root of the repo, using Prettier across all of the files.

This removes the `format`, `check-format` Just targets and npm scripts in our individual NPM packages and moves all of that up to the root.

Additionally this PR introduces [`husky`](https://github.com/typicode/husky) and [`lint-staged`](https://github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged) to the root `package.json` to setup a Git commit hook which will automatically run Prettier for you.

To set that up all you have to do is run `npm install` or `just npm-install` at the root dir.

Prettier's VSCode extension is also added to the recommend extensions for the repo.

title: New gitignore
description:
## Intent
This PR intends to solve our the issues with the gitignore module that we used (github.com/iriri/minimal/gitignore). We have matching issues on Windows, subdirectory matching not working, reliance on the current directory, etc. and the existing code structure is simply unmaintainable.

Fixes #1161 
Fixes #420

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [x] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
This is a clean sheet re-implementation of the gitignore rules from the gitignore spec document. The method used is translation of gitignore patterns to regular expressions. Comments in the translation code are direct quotes from the gitignore spec. All path matching is done against absolute paths so there is no dependence on the current directory. Regexes have paths baked into them as needed, based on the location of the ignore file and the gitignore spec.

## Automated Tests
Existing tests were updated since the interface changed slightly. There is also a new, more comprehensive set of tests specifically for gitignore pattern matching.

## Directions for Reviewers
This is a significant change that will require validation of gitignore rules in various scenarios:
* A variety of matching rules
* Rules that are pinned to the top level like `/meta.yaml` or applicable to subdirectories (`meta.yaml`). See the [gitignore docs](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore)
* File and directory wildcards and globstars (`**`)
* Deploying from inside or outside of the project directory.

Prettier [uses the gitignore](https://prettier.io/docs/en/ignore.html):

> By default prettier ignores files in version control systems directories (".git", ".sl", ".svn" and ".hg") and node_modules (unless the [--with-node-modules CLI option](https://prettier.io/docs/en/cli#--with-node-modules) is specified). Prettier will also follow rules specified in the ".gitignore" file if it exists in the same directory from which it is run.

title: Bump black from 21.12b0 to 24.3.0 in /test/sample-content/quarto-proj-py
description:
Bumps [black](https://github.com/psf/black) from 21.12b0 to 24.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from black's releases.

24.3.0

Highlights

This release is a milestone: it fixes Black's first CVE security vulnerability. If you run Black on untrusted input, or if you habitually put thousands of leading tab characters in your docstrings, you are strongly encouraged to upgrade immediately to fix CVE-2024-21503.

This release also fixes a bug in Black's AST safety check that allowed Black to make incorrect changes to certain f-strings that are valid in Python 3.12 and higher.

Stable style

  • Don't move comments along with delimiters, which could cause crashes (#4248)
  • Strengthen AST safety check to catch more unsafe changes to strings. Previous versions of Black would incorrectly format the contents of certain unusual f-strings containing nested strings with the same quote type. Now, Black will crash on such strings until support for the new f-string syntax is implemented. (#4270)
  • Fix a bug where line-ranges exceeding the last code line would not work as expected (#4273)

Performance

  • Fix catastrophic performance on docstrings that contain large numbers of leading tab characters. This fixes CVE-2024-21503. (#4278)

Documentation

  • Note what happens when --check is used with --quiet (#4236)

24.2.0

Stable style

  • Fixed a bug where comments where mistakenly removed along with redundant parentheses (#4218)

Preview style

  • Move the hug_parens_with_braces_and_square_brackets feature to the unstable style due to an outstanding crash and proposed formatting tweaks (#4198)
  • Fixed a bug where base expressions caused inconsistent formatting of ** in tenary expression (#4154)
  • Checking for newline before adding one on docstring that is almost at the line limit (#4185)

title: Fix subdirectory matching for .positignore
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This PR attempts to fix issues with matching file paths in subdirectories via .positignore.

This fix is targeted at a Windows issue, but also the matching algorithm doesn't seem to handle excluded subdirectories correctly. We normally don't notice because we use `Walk`, which doesn't recurse into a subdirectory if it's excluded. The base matching algorithm doesn't seem to do that on its own. 

Fixes #1161

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
* Always slash-normalize paths before attempting to match.
* Add parent directory matching patterns

## Automated Tests
Added a test with Windows paths. Since we always slash-normalize our paths now, unit tests for Windows paths can run under MacOS and Linux.

## Directions for Reviewers
Deploy with .positignore exclusions on Mac/Linux and Windows. Verify different kinds of matching patterns (suggested list below). Check logs to be sure that the correct files are excluded from the bundle when deploying.

Example patterns to match `app.py` in various subdirectories and sub-subdirectories:
```
app.py
*.py
subdir/app.py
subdir/*.py
**/app.py
**/*.py
subdir/**/app.py
subdir/**/*.py
**/subdir/app.py
**/subdir/*.py
```

title: use RelativePath and AbsolutePath
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This draft PR explores the idea of creating new backend types for relative vs. absolute paths, since we've had several bugs caused by confusing them.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [x] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
Created `util.RelativePath` and `util.AbsolutePath`. The existing `Path.Rel` and `Path.Abs` functions return the new types (`Path` remains as a path of unknown absoluteness). Path methods that return a `Path` are implemented in `RelativePath` and `AbsolutePath` to return the matching types; for example `AbsolutePath.Glob` returns an array of `AbsolutePath`s. Much of the agent code now expects `AbsolutePath`, even where it's not strictly required. 

Care is required when creating paths from strings; calling `NewAbsolutePath` with a string that isn't actually an absolute path will return an `AbsolutePath` that isn't. There is a global flag `assertPathType` that can be set to true during debugging; if it's set, paths of the wrong type will panic. (If we want this in production, the path constructors will also have to return an error).

Also the existing `.Path()` method was duplicative of `.String()` and the name was confusing, so it has been removed.

## Automated Tests
Existing tests have been updated. A lot of tests construct paths so there is a lot of change there.

## Directions for Reviewers
Set `assertPathType` to true and run unit, integration, and manual tests.

title: Add scanning and uninitialized welcome views
description:
This PR introduces two new `viewsWelcome`s:
- One for while the asynchronous code is running and the extension is trying to determine if folder is initialized as a Post publishing project
- One for after the asynchronous code is running and a `.posit` or a `.posit/publish` directory are not found 

<details>
  <summary>Preview</summary>

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/61180090-5a0f-4b37-b268-56ad3ed3aee2


https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/3156cb94-b027-4e68-ab5f-cecb5b8d97b5

</details> 

## Intent
Part of #1070 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
The approach here comes from how the Git extension from VSCode works:
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/091987d9431154a3624ba20bc1d6de65d71d6472/extensions/git/src/main.ts#L229
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/091987d9431154a3624ba20bc1d6de65d71d6472/extensions/git/src/model.ts#L285

It uses `git.missing` and `git.state` in tandem to determine if git is either missing entirely, or if the extension is still getting things setup.

I did the same here setting `posit.publish.missing` as quickly as possible, and setting `posit.publish.state == 'initialized'` once `activate()` was finished up.

I also setup a file system watcher to watch both the `.posit` and `.posit/publish` directories which sets `posit.publish.missing = false` when they are gone, or back to `true` when they come back.

## Directions for Reviewers
Try out the `viewWelcome`:
- no folder in the workspace
- more than one folder in the workspace
- when the extension is still activating ("Scanning folder for a Posit project...")
- if the project is uninitialized

To initialize you can use `just run init test/sample-content/fastapi-simple` for example.

You can also test that the file watchers work by removing `.posit` and or `.posit/publish` and bring back up the uninitialized view.

Refactored the `PythonInspector` interface, updated the existing endpoint path, and implemented a new endpoint to get the requirements. So the API is

## Automated Tests
Added tests for the new endpoint.

## Directions for Reviewers
Use the APIs from curl, e.g.
```
curl localhost:9001/api/requirements
```
should return the contents of requirements.txt, or a 404 if it doesn't exist.

```
curl -XPOST localhost:9001/api/requirements -d '{"saveName":"requirements.txt"}'
```
should scan your project and write the dependencies to `requirements.txt`.

* Don't include dashboardUrl in error detailed for a deployment that fails before there is a contentID created.
* As a side note, linting should not check for copyright headers in `node_modules` when running lint locally. In CI this was fine because we don't run `npm install` before linting the agent.

title: Provide `unregister()` closure when registering event callback
description:
This PR introduces a return to the `register` method in the VSCode `events.ts` file. That return is an object that contains an `unregister` function which, when called, will remove the registered callback from the callbacks array associated with the type passed.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
The approach here is to return a method which has the context of the `register` call. So we can access `type` and `callback` still without needing them to be passed to `unregister`.

I tested this on #1054 by unregistering the listener that reset the stages status.

Usage looks like this:

```typescript
const registration = stream.register('publish/start', (_: EventStreamMessage) => {
  this.events = [];
  this.resetStages();
});
registration.unregister();
```

The approach here was to register events for each of the stages and group them in a map that the view understood how to traverse.

This PR adds a status bar facility for the Publisher extension. As shown in this example:

This PR should serve as a model for future usage of this new notification facility.

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

Simple method in `notify.ts` allows for a short string message to be passed in (although nothing stops the caller from passing in a large string)

Notify icon and message are shown for two seconds and then clears without user input.

If notify is called when it is already showing, the old notification is overridden and the new message is shown for a full two seconds and then  clears as expected.

Existing refresh methods in configurations and deployments have been updated to understand if should show the notification or not. File watcher initiated refresh do not show, since manual notifications of delete configuration and forget deployment cause the file watchers to run refresh, and this would have overridden the intended notifications.

The alert method was moved into the new `notify.ts` as it seems more of a notify than a dialog.

Also added a missing `try/catch` for an API call within the `deployments` view.

title: Set target name in CLI before deploying
description:
## Intent
Fixes #920

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
Set the target name before deploying.

The publishing code sets the target when the deployment record is created; this is right after creating the new deployment on Connect (or at that stage if redeploying). On failure, we rewrite the deployment record, adding error information. However, if preflight fails, publishing fails before the point where the deployment record is first written and the target name assigned.

UI flows are not affected, because we are creating pre-deployment records so every deployment action starts with the target name already set.

## Automated Tests
The CLI layer isn't covered by tests yet.

title: Generate a simpler requirements txt
description:
## Intent
This PR simplifies how we generate requirements.txt, and separates that from the `init` process into a separate CLI command (follow on PR will include an API for it).

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [x] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
The old method of using `pip freeze` has multiple issues:
* It captures all of the packages in the environment, whether they are used in the project or not.
* It can include conda-specific packages that can't be pip installed.
* It causes slow environment restores due to the unused packages.

The method in this PR inspects project files to find imports, and resolves those to installable package names by inspecting the site-packages/*.dist-info directories. For this to work, we have to inspect the correct python environment, but pip freeze shares the same constraint.

The resulting requirements.txt file contains only the direct dependencies, and pins them to the version in the local environment. Transitive dependencies are excluded.

## Automated Tests
There are unit tests. We need integration tests inspecting both pip and conda environments.

## Directions for Reviewers
Run init on some projects; observe that requirements.txt is not created.
Run `publisher requirements` (name subject to change!) on some Python/Quarto projects and observe that it captures the python package imports.

title: Formalize backend event payloads
description:
## Intent
This PR changes how the backend generates events for the frontend so that the event payloads are better defined.

Fixes #826 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [x] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
Currently, we use structured logging to generate our events, passing attributes to log calls and using sub-loggers to capture attributes that will span multiple calls. This makes it hard to coordinate with the frontend on event payloads.

This PR introduces an `events.Emitter` interface type and use that to send structured event data. All publishing phase events (`start`, `success`, and `failure` for each operation) use this, and each of those events has a defined payload.

Limitations:
* A new `events.DataEmitter` injects the `local_id` into every publishing event, so that field does not appear in the payload type. This isn't ideal, but we plan to stop using `local_id` in the frontend anyway, and it didn't seem worthwhile to make it explicit in every event payload just to remove it later.
* `log` events are still raised for all logging calls such as `Info`. Since those attributes are ad-hoc, the payloads for `log` events are not explicitly structured.

## Automated Tests
Existing tests have been updated. More unit tests are needed before this is ready to merge.

## Directions for Reviewers
Deploy through the UI and ensure that both progress views (the deployment card and summarized logs) both progress normally. View logs and ensure that there are no "undefined" attributes.

description:
As part of the redesign for Deployment Cards we are moving to relative times like "28 minutes ago" rather than hard dates. 

## Intent

## Type of Change

## Approach
I compared [Day.js](https://day.js.org/) and [date-fns](https://date-fns.org/) and went with `date-fns`. They were about as easy to use, but `date-fns` provides more utilities, doesn't need a plugin system, and has tree shaking to avoid the bundle from getting bigger from what we don't use.

From there I replaced our usage of our own date string formatting function with the `formatDistanceToNow()`

This change replaces the usage of `wait-on` with `net.Socket` management. This allows us to have more information about the server state.

Additionally, methods are added to verify if the server is up or down. Each method is tuned to provide a quick response when the state matches what is requested. title: Add Vite global constant replacement for version
description:
This utilizes Vite's config `define` which does global constant replacements to inject the version into the frontend for use.

## Intent
- Part of #876 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
To inject (or do a replacement more accurately) during dev and build we can use Vite's [`define`](https://vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html#define) feature.

To get the version I used the same `git` command found in our `get-version.bash` script: `git describe --tags`.

This is the same technique used by [Academy](https://github.com/rstudio/academy-ui/blob/main/vite.config.ts).

Once this is ready to be I added it to the `vite-env.d.ts` file so TypeScript doesn't complain as recommended in the docs.

However this caused an issue in `eslint` linting which is specifically called out by the [TypeScript ESLint troubleshooting guide](https://typescript-eslint.io/linting/troubleshooting#i-get-errors-from-the-no-undef-rule-about-global-variables-not-being-defined-even-though-there-are-no-typescript-errors) which suggests disabling `no-undef` entirely for typed files which removes the linting error.

#### References
- https://vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html#define
- https://esbuild.github.io/api/#define
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/no-undef
- https://typescript-eslint.io/linting/troubleshooting#i-get-errors-from-the-no-undef-rule-about-global-variables-not-being-defined-even-though-there-are-no-typescript-errors

## Directions for Reviewers
Add a `console.log` or a constant to use in a template `const version = __VERSION__;` to see the injection at work.

This should work in both dev mode, and in production builds.

title: Handle Deployment fetching and store race condition
description:
This PR addresses the issue where we can attempt to fetch a deployment from the store before the API calls are completed.

## Intent
- Fixes #863 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
To handle this we can use a `computed()` which understands if the deployment store is still initializing (still waiting for API response(s)).

To accomplish sharing the deployment store state an additional `ref()` was added that starts `true` and becomes `false` once the API calls are handled.

The `getDeploymentRef()` was then changed to return a pre-setup `computed()` that handles 404ing if the deployment store is finished fetching, and the deployment still isn't found. Since it is `computed()` this also will work when we get file watching in place and the deployment gets deleted from the store while we are on a page.

---

Once we start using [`<Suspense>`](https://vuejs.org/guide/built-ins/suspense.html) everywhere we can adjust `getDeploymentRef` to being an async function, and have the components `await` its result making it an [Async Component](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/async). I kept this simple with a `boolean` to avoid having to setup `<Suspense>` right away.

title: Support nested links in PCard
description:
This PR makes links clickable, focusable, hoverable, etc inside of the PCard component. **Usage Changes** As mentioned below in more detail this removes the `truncate` on `PCard` so children passed will have to handle their own truncation. This does remove the need for wrap overrides. ## Type of Change * - [ ] Bug Fix * - [x] New Feature * - [ ] Breaking Change * - [ ] Documentation * - [ ] Refactor * - [ ] Tooling ## Approach To make links clickable inside other links we can utilize `z-index` and relative positioning. The card link itself is on `z-index: 1` while the internal links of the card are in `z-index: 2` making the browser prioritize the link on top when hovering and clicking. This doesn't break the specification for anchors since the card anchor is an absolutely positioned element, and no interactive content is actually inside of the anchors. > 12.2.2 Nested links are illegal Links and anchors defined by the [A](https://www.w3.org/TR/html401/struct/links.html#edef-A) element must not be nested; an [A](https://www.w3.org/TR/html401/struct/links.html#edef-A) element must not contain any other [A](https://www.w3.org/TR/html401/struct/links.html#edef-A) elements. To accomplish this I combined both scoped and non-scoped CSS in Vue. The `PCard` styles itself and not children other than the `z-index: 2` adjustment to all internal `a` and `.vscode-router-link` elements. #### Accessibility Changes Focusing was changed. Since focusing was based on `focus-shadow` before, which utilized `:focus-within` it was showing the focus all the time when any link was focused inside the card. This creates confusion on which link is focused while using keyboard navigation. To fix this I changed the focus for the entire card to only show when the `link-fill` was focused using default browser focusing. I had to remove the `PCard` `truncate` class to accomplish this since the `overflow: hidden` was hiding the focus styling. **This leads to a side effect** where all text, child elements used inside `PCard` will have to use `truncate` themselves.
Preview ![CleanShot 2024-01-24 at 11 37 58](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/eae054e1-e24e-4952-8ca4-d38d84a6d760)

description:

## Intent
- Resolves #840 
- Resolves #841 

## Type of Change

## Approach
The blue colors added as CSS variables are from the Posit Brand Guidelines.

To style the `anchors` we needed to independently style them for our light and dark mode which is done by using the body classes `body--light` and `body--dark`. Additionally we need to use VSCode styling when available which can be accomplished with `var()`'s fallback value option.

VSCode introduces hover effects that utilize their CSS variables `--vscode-textLink-foreground` and `--vscode-textLink-activeForeground`. When those aren't utilized we can use our own rather than not providing a `:hover` styling. In both light and dark mode I increased the contrast by going darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode.

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/var

Test the UI and the VSCode Extension independently. Note that #844 is still not merged so you will need to change the dark/light mode to match your VSCode theme when running the extension.

title: Add Quarto project inspection
description:
## Intent
This PR implements project inspection for Quarto python projects.

Fixes #814.
Builds on #831.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
New `QuartoDetector` implements the `ContentTypeInferer` interface, detecting Quarto projects via the .qmd suffix. The "preferred filename" for a Quarto project isn't fixed, since RStudio by default names it $PROJECT.qmd, so we prefer a qmd file whose name matches the directory name.

We run `quarto inspect` on the project directory to discover the quarto version, engines, etc. Quarto must be available on PATH.

## Automated Tests
There are unit tests covering the quarto detector.

## Directions for Reviewers
There is some Quarto example content under `test/sample-content`. These were sourced from the `connect-content` repo.

* run `publisher init` on Quarto content. It can be pure markdown or include Python code blocks. Verify the generated configuration file.
* Projects with R content will generate an error saying the knitr engine is not yet supported.
* Projects with python content will require/create a requirements.txt file and include a `python` section in the configuration file.
* Projects without python content should not create requirements.txt or include the `python` config section.
* Pre-rendered quarto projects (which include a rendered HTML version of the content) deploy as Quarto source and are rendered in Connect. We will need to provide a way to opt out of that. Currently, you need to edit the config file to use the `html` type and remove the `quarto` and `python` config sections.

```
just build && echo && $(just executable-path) init -v && cat .posit/publish/default.toml
$(just executable-path) deploy -a dogfood
```

title: Conditionally use router-link destination in PButton for vscode links
description:
This PR extends the `PButton` component to handle the `to` prop (the location to navigate to using Vue Router) differently depending on whether we are in VSCode or not.

When in VSCode we navigate ourselves and don't render a `<a>` instead using a `<button>` element.

When in the UI we render a `<a>` as normal which behaves as we would expect from a `RouterLink`. 

## Intent
- Part of #759 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
The approach here is to conditionally pass props to `QBtn` which accepts a `to` prop. When in VSCode we don't want to have `QBtn` handle the `to` prop and create a `RouterLink` rendering a `<a>`. Instead we want to use a click and enter listener so VSCode's click listener doesn't intercept the link click and open in a new window.

When we aren't in VSCode however we pass the `to` prop and don't add the listeners at all. 

## Reviewer Instructions
Run the UI and the VSCode extension testing the "New Destination" link. It should navigate in both without issue.

Note this does not fix the breadcrumbs. Those will be addressed in another PR.

title: Create PLink component for handling web and VSCode router links
description:
This PR introduces a new component `PLink` that handles whether to use a normal `RouterLink` or use a custom element when in VSCode. The custom element is a `span` with a click listener and enter key listener (when it is focused) to navigate in much the same way a `a` element works.

The `PLink` component should be ephemeral when running in the web - that is never doing anything but forwarding props and attributes to `RouterLink`. However in VSCode a bit more is done to style and make it behave like a normal link. 

<details>
  <summary>Previews</summary>
  
![CleanShot 2024-01-11 at 18 01 30](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/2670c9c5-b0ab-4d5b-9ac5-45769d9177cc)

![CleanShot 2024-01-11 at 18 01 50](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/5ad9c735-6af4-4a2c-ad39-e1996bf60b22)

![CleanShot 2024-01-11 at 18 02 16](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/bb9afbe8-2d87-4d7f-925d-8f1432548d97)

![CleanShot 2024-01-11 at 18 02 26](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/353e9365-6233-41db-996a-2022d4cf5a6a)

</details> 

## Intent
- Part of #759

This DOES NOT handle buttons or the breadcrumbs. Those are Quasar components that use a `RouterLink` component on their own. They will have to be removed and custom components created to get this to work. Those will come in follow-up PRs to make reviewing this easier.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
To start I created `PLink` and had it only handle `RouterLink` attrs and props making that function the same.

Following that I created a `span` with a click event to see if that worked in VSCode. After confirming it did, I added `tabindex=0` to allow the element to be focusable with keyboard navigation, and added an enter keyup listener so it behaved like an `a` with keyboard link following.

After that I replaced all of the `RouterLink` components we were using with `PLink` and took care of styling issues in both the web and VSCode.

## Directions for Reviewers
To review you will need to run both the UI and the VSCode extension navigating through the UI. Remember that the breadcrumbs and button navigation still will not work as intended (aka it will open in a new window still).

The normal anchors, the cards, and the header logo will navigate as intended.

title: Use HTML5 mode `vue-router` history
description:
This PR switches our `vue-router` history mode from [Web Hash](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/essentials/history-mode.html#Hash-Mode) to [HTML5 mode](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/essentials/history-mode.html#HTML5-Mode). 

## Intent
- Fixes #788 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

## Approach
Without switching to HTML 5 mode the VSCode extension would not load due to a frame-src Content Security Policy. Switching the history mode exposed some other issues.

From the `vue-router` docs:

> Here comes a problem, though: Since our app is a single page client side app, without a proper server configuration, the users will get a 404 error if they access https://example.com/user/id directly in their browser. Now that's ugly.
> Not to worry: To fix the issue, all you need to do is add a simple catch-all fallback route to your server. If the URL doesn't match any static assets, it should serve the same index.html page that your app lives in. Beautiful, again!

I thought this is what was occurring when we were getting 404s but it turns out our `/api` requests were using relative URLs based. When using `WebHistory` we need to use absolute so we are calling `localhost:port/api/...`. With that fixed things are working.

## Directions for Reviewers
This PR needs to be tested both in the web view and as a VSCode extension. Both should work.

description:

Modifies the build process to bundle the binary executable within the VSCode extension package for each target platform.

The extension is modified to resolve the executable binary to the extension's `bin` directory. If the configuration property is set, then it is used instead.

Resolves #737 
Resolves #738 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->

Adds build tooling that places the binary executable at `./extensions/vscode/bin/publisher` and then bundles the binary during packaging. This process is executed via `just vscode` from the project's root or `just` if within the extension's root.

Also, adds a script tied to `just package` that iterates over each platform when `CI=true`. The script calls `just vscode default {{ os }} {{ arch }}` for each platform. This process configures the extension with the correct executable and then packages it.

title: Better TOML errors
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This PR improves the errors returned from the `GET /api/configurations, GET /api/deployments, and GET /api/deployments/{name}` endpoints. 

Fixes #631 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
* - [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
Rather that only returning a string in the `error` field, we now return an `AgentError` which is the same data we feed into the event stream for asynchronous errors.

Every `AgentError` contains a `code` and `msg`. Depending on the `code`, there may be structured data in the `data` field.

This PR introduces structured data for TOML parsing and validation errors (which unfortunately do not have the same shape, based on the data available from the TOML package and jsonschema validator). The front end has been updated to use the `msg` field from the error, but it does not yet consume the structured data for better presentation.

```

      }
    }
  },
  {
    "configurationName": "default",
    "configurationPath": ".posit/publish/default.toml",
    "configuration": {
```

title: Disable deploy buttons if default configuration is invalid
description:
This PR disables the new deploy or re-deploy buttons if the default configuration file has an error.

## Intent
- Resolves #725 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->
* - [ ] Refactor          <!-- Code restructuring -->
* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
Both the Existing Deployment Header and the New Deployment Header have been updated to take in the `ConfigurationError` if one was received from the API. With that the deploy buttons are disabled and a title is used to tell the user why the button is disabled which happens for two reasons currently:

1. A publish is in progress
2. The configuration has an error

Both Headers use a `v-if` to wait for the configuration to be retrieved from the API. Ideally we would use loading states, but we only have one suspend currently and we have discussed having an effort to improve those specifically in the codebase. Rather than implementing that here (since it is a lot more effort) I went with the simple approach that adds the feature.

description:

## Intent
This PR implements some changes to the CLI credential handling as a result of alpha 1 feedback.

Fixes #721 
Fixes #722 
Fixes #735 
Fixes #636 

Added logging to the `deploy` and `redeploy` commands containing important parameter values.

If no account is specified for the CLI deploy command:
* If there are no accounts, it's an error (existing behavior)
* If there is only 1 account, use it (existing behavior)
* If there is an account from `CONNECT_SERVER` and `CONNECT_API_KEY` environment variables, use it.

Implemented a default SaveName for new deployments to avoid using GUIDs.

title: Encode URL params for API requests
description:
Simple PR that calls [`encodeURIComponent`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/encodeURIComponent) for the params we pass to API client methods that are used in the URL we pass to Axios.

This will make API requests to `GET /api/accounts/{name}` and `GET /api/deployments/{name}` work if the names are not URL safe. It will encode them before making the request.

For example:
`http://localhost:9000/api/deployments/a%b@c!` will become `http://localhost:9000/api/deployments/a%25b%40c!`

title: Fix re-deployments from the two deployment pages
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

This PR corrects a number of issues related to creating new deployments vs. updating existing ones. It also resolves an issue in which we do not yet support specifying the content ID for a new destination (by removing it from the interface).

Also included in this PR is the hiding of the publish status summary initially on both the new and update deployment headers, so that users do not see previous publish statuses (and possibly believe a publish has occurred automatically by entering this page).

Closes: #591 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

* - [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->
* - [ ] Documentation     <!-- User or developer documentation -->

* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The single publish API (POST /deployment) has been front-ended now by two different methods (`PublishNew` and 'PublishUpdate') in order to better support the current business logic within the backend API provider.

In addition, both header components keep track of how many times a user has clicked the publish button and it has made it to a successful "enough" deployment, where a contentId has been assigned to it from the server. This allows us to know if a new deployment or an update needs to occur on the add new destination header, as well as when we should be showing the publish status component.

This PR causes the CLI to always log the deployment's dashboard URL, even on failure, if it is known (the only case where it's not known is a new deployment where we didn't get to the create new deployment step).

This is also passed to the UI as an attribute on the publishing failure event.

title: Remove all external links
description:
This PR does two things:
- Removes the direct link to the published content
- Removes ALL `<a>` elements in the UI since they point to external links

### Why are all external links being removed?

VSCode doesn't support `target="_blank"` and actively blocks it. More details can be found in references in #609. The links would still work if you used CMD clicking or middle mouse clicks which defaults to opening in a new tab (new window in VSCode), but if you clicked on them normally:
- a `target="blank"` would be blocked and nothing would happen. A console error would be in the devtools that it was blocked
- an external link would take over the iframe and the only way to navigate back is to use keyboard or mouse shortcuts like a normal browser. VSCode has no interface to back or navigate through history.

Neither of these are ideal for Alpha, and could cause problems. When we find a way to address #609 we can re-add link functionality or a fallback option.

## Intent
- Temporarily deals with #609 
- Resolves #615

Handle the errors (>300) which result in Axios raising promise rejection and exceptions. The intention is to be able to provide helper functions which expose important details from the underlying data and allow the API calling code to handle the errors gracefully. It needs to handle both fatal and recoverable errors, as determined by the API and caller.

Closes #410 

## Type of Change

<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

* - [ ] Tooling           <!-- Build, CI, or release scripts and configuration -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

I've walked through the current go code and identified what possible errors are currently being returned for the APIs which the UX calls. These have been added as comments within the calling code.

I've then created helper functions that help extract important details from the exception return data that Axios provides and placed those within the error utility file.

Each location which calls the agent APIs has been updated with a try/catch around the `await`, and I've used the helper functions to provide special handling for those errors which should receive local treatment from the component. (Actual local treatment will be a follow-on PR, so for now, they are simply throwing an Error.) Fatal errors are routed to the new FatalError page, which displays further helpful information about what has failed. The example below was a result of stopping the agent while the UX was still running and then subsequently trying to navigate to another view within the UX.

3. src/views/new-deployment-destination/NewDestinationHeader.vue - an example of where the API will return an error best handled locally, along with a fatal error.

title: Reduce cli verbosity
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent

This PR replaces the current `--debug` flag with a 2-level `--verbose` flag (you can use `-v` or `-vv`).
* The default log level is `WARN` so most messages are suppressed.
* `-v` maps to log level `INFO`
* `-vv` maps to log level `DEBUG`

Additionally, the `create` and `update` commands show the deployment progress, one step per line, with a success/failure indicator.

Updated the VSCode plugin to run with `-v` so there will be logs.

Fixes #439

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [x] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
There is a new CLI log handler that emits the progress display by monitoring for the Start/Success/Failure messages. There is also a default handler (same as before) that emits structured log messages, conditional on verbosity, but less verbose by default.

## Automated Tests
There are tests for the new CLIHandler.

## Directions for Reviewers
* Create/update deployments using the CLI to see the new display.
* Run with `-v` if you want to see deployment logs.

```
2f82-4ebe-be18-282c13fb00e9.toml: no such file or directory"
```

title: Handle fatal API errors with a new page
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

There are a number of errors returned from our general API queries that we consider as fatal, with no other resolution available other than reloading the application. This PR adds a fatal error page into the routes which helps describe where the issue occurred and what the error encoutered was. It also provides the ability to reload the app to retry from a fresh UX state. This will not solve the issue when the agent must be reloaded, but that is described within this page as a further resolution step.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

- Added new page `src/views/fatal-error/FatalErrorPage.vue`
- Added a new error utility method which routes to the new fatal error page
- Added try/catch blocks around our general API calls and calls the new error utility
- Added logic into event store to indicate current publish process status (error) and updated indicators to allow UX to not show publishing still in progress upon error.

NOTE: This PR does NOT include code to handle expected errors. That will be fixed in #544 

Additional improvements are expected to this code in #548 as well.

NOTE: The error page is not fancy, but it is functional. Here's an example:
![2023-12-12 at 5 14 PM](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/df64828e-1cdb-406e-ac79-4c18f60cc2c8)

## Automated Tests
<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

## Directions for Reviewers
<!-- Provide steps for reviewers to validate this change manually. -->
You can reproduce a fatal error by stopping the agent before attempting navigation within the UX. For the most part, every page attempts a generic API call that is considered fatal if it fails. If you then restart the agent and click on the anchor "here", the app should reload fine.

Examples:
- While on the project page, stop the agent, and then hit refresh within the browser for the page.
- While on the project page, stop the agent, and click on a destination.
- While on the project page, stop the agent, and click on new destination.
- While on the add destination page, stop the agent, and click on Continue to Publishing. (NOTE: this one prompts for you to not exit the page before going to the error page. We should probably fix that.)
- While on the new deployment page, stop the agent, and click on Publish
- While on the update deployment page, stop the agent, and click on Publish

Currently not handled:
- While publishing is in progress, stop the agent (we rely upon the failure of the event stream, which takes a while).

description:
This PR styles the destination and config card grids on the Project Page. It adds some additional functionality to `PCard` (icon and title tooltip), uses CSS to set columns for the grid, and ensures titles truncate.

<details>
  <summary>Before</summary>

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #528 

## Type of Change

- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->

## Approach
Still creating CSS utilities to handle somethings for us. In this PR `truncate` was created to ensure that the cards don't wrap and create imbalanced grids. The max-widths on the cards was kept high to avoid GUIDs from being cut.

The Config Cards presented a bit of a problem for the card view. They have very little information on them, and the error can potentially be quite long. To address this I did two things:
- added the path to the card to help balance it and provide users more context to where the configurations are coming from
  - this presented another problem because the API gives back the bath based on where the `publisher` command ran not relative from the directory passed to the command
- Gave PCard the ability to accept a title tooltip and icon to still show users that their configs are invalid
  - Eventually the Config Card will be clickable to go to a Config Page which can give more context for the error and have the user address them.
  
Other than that I used max-widths and set the number of columns separately for the Config and Destination Cards based on their content. They break at the same point to avoid disjointed adjustments as the window width is adjusted.
