title: Show file exclusions on file hover
description:
This PR uses the custom slot for the `q-tree` to show a tooltip, on hover, when the file has an exclusion.

<details>
  <summary>Preview</summary>
  
![CleanShot 2023-12-11 at 19 18 37](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/83078458-b24f-4b50-b105-855ff7a03c81)

</details> 

## Type of Change
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->

## Approach
Quasar exposes a `default-header` slot in its `q-tree`. Using that we can customize our own label and use `q-tooltip` along side it.

1. At the start I created a `template` that matched the Quasar's `q-tree` exactly with the optional icon and label.
2. After that I removed the `node.disabled` since that removes pointer events which makes it so `q-tooltip` never appears. 
3. I created a custom CSS class to bring back the opacity that disabled used
4. I created a `q-tooltip` with larger text (for accessibility), and custom positioning to go to the right
  - This avoids overlapping with other files when hovering to some degree
  
The exclusion is not styled, but that can be an easy follow-up PR now that the tooltip and `exclusion` object is accessible.

title: Create PCard component and use for Deployment and Config Cards
description:
This PR introduces a generic `PCard` component that is used for `DeploymentCard` and the new `ConfigCard`. This PR also: - Resets `

` margins app-wide - This is similar to the work done in #518 to avoid us having to do this everywhere - Add space-between CSS utilities - This is a duplicate of #518 we will only have one of these once these merge, but I needed them in this PR

Before ![CleanShot 2023-12-11 at 18 36 18](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/d77949dd-2deb-4f74-ae74-90b37261587e)
After ![CleanShot 2023-12-11 at 18 36 08](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/d2d91a35-d07d-479f-b1ea-66a15dd1cf35)
Again the card grid styling has not been written. ## Intent - Resolves #378 ## Type of Change - [x] New Feature ## Approach Rather than duplicating CSS and removing the parts that the new `ConfigCard` doesn't use we can instead make the CSS more generic and throw it in another component. That is what was done here. `PCard` handles whether or not it has a title, a `to` link (takes a Vue Router Location), and if it has slot content or not. It adapts and uses CSS to handle all of them gracefully. For example: If no title is provided the `p.card-title` element isn't rendered and margin was moved to the title to avoid creating unnecessary margin with only a slot used. If no Vue Router Location is supplied the `span.link-fill` isn't rendered, and the whole card no longer has hover styling which may confuse the user. If no slot is provided the `p.card-title` uses `:not(:last-child)` to avoid applying unnecessary margin. This more generic approach puts all the logic (display and functional) into one spot without needing to understand our Deployments or Configurations and those components can take care of how those should work. #### Why the `PCard` name? [Components must be multi-word](https://vuejs.org/style-guide/rules-essential.html#use-multi-word-component-names) to prevent conflicts. With that in mind this is a `Publisher` component or a `P` component for short.

title: Preflight Connect capabilities
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This PR introduces a set of checks, specific to Connect, to validate the configuration will be acceptable to the Connect server before making any Connect API calls that change state. This is a subset of the full checks that Connect does when it receives the API calls we will later send, because we don't have access to all of the information that Connect does. But it can enforce quite a few constraints to help prevent deployments or updates from failing partway through when only part of the change has taken effect.

Fixes #486 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
Hit Connect's server_settings endpoints to gather information about the server capabilities and configuration. Check the configuration settings against those.

## Automated Tests
There are tests for the checked conditions.

## Directions for Reviewers
Create a config file that requests capabilities the Connect server does not have. For example, if your server does not have Kubernetes configured, create a config file with the `[connect.kubernetes]` section populated. Or, try setting `[connect.runtime] max-processes = 100` which is higher than the Connect server's configuration (which defaults to `[scheduler] MaxProcessLimit = 50`).

title: Allow init to complete even if type can't be detected
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This PR improves handling of the case where we cannot automatically detect the content type.

Fixes #484

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
Currently, we return an error (with an outdated message) and don't create the configuration file. With this PR, we create the configuration file with its `type` and `entrypoint` set to `unknown`, and log a warning.

The generated config file will not pass validation. If you try to use it to publish, it will say:
```
 jsonschema: '/type' does not validate with https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json#/properties/type/enum: value must be one of "html", "jupyter-notebook", "jupyter-voila", "python-bokeh", "python-dash", "python-fastapi", "python-flask", "python-shiny", "python-streamlit", "quarto-shiny", "quarto", "r-plumber", "r-shiny", "rmd-shiny", "rmd"
```

## Automated Tests
Existing tests covered this case, and have been updated to expect the new behavior.

## Directions for Reviewers
Try running
```
just run init -c newconfig $(pwd) && cat .posit/publish/newconfig.json
```
in some potential project directories.

Even if the directory is empty, or contains only unrelated files, you should see a config file being created. If there is a requirements.txt file, or if you pass the `--python` argument to `init`, you will also see some Python information in the config file.

title: Support for named deployments
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This PR provides agent support for naming deployment instead of relying on IDs.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
Added a new optional parameter to the `POST /api/deployments` endpoint named `save-name`. Also clarified naming so we use target name where we mean the saved file name, and content ID where we mean the GUID of the deployment.

If you specify:
```
{
 "account": "dogfood",
 "save-name": "staging"
}
```
you will get a new deployment on dogfood, and the file `.posit/publish/deployments/staging.toml` will contain the deployment record.

If you don't specify a save-name, the ID will be used as it is currently (creating a file like `fe97ce15-b3b5-40c4-90ca-27de15c4a8ce.toml`).

If you have an existing deployment, publishing with a save-name will rename the deployment record:
```
{
 "target": "fe97ce15-b3b5-40c4-90ca-27de15c4a8ce",
 "save-name": "staging"
}
```
will read the deployment record in `.posit/publish/deployments/fe97ce15-b3b5-40c4-90ca-27de15c4a8ce.toml`, publish the update, and rename the deployment record to `.posit/publish/deployments/staging.toml`.

There is an equivalent command-line option `-s/--save-name`.

## Automated Tests
Added a test to cover this use of the endpoint.

## Directions for Reviewers

Use the `save-name` option from the API and CLI as described above. Try:
* new deployment without a save-name (creates $GUID.toml)
* new deployment with a save-name (creates $NAME.toml)
* update existing deployment $NAME without a save-name (updates $NAME.toml)
* update existing deployment $NAME with a save-name $NEWNAME (renames $NAME.toml to $NEWNAME.toml)

title: Create general layout CSS for publisher
description:
This PR creates a new CSS utility class called `publisher-layout` that handles the horizontal layout of the content. It does a few things:
- Sets up a max width to avoid the content from being too disjointed in very large windows
- Handles padding-left and padding-right at different responsive sizes so the content is never right against the edge of the window
- Sets margin-auto for the left and right side so the content is centered


<details>
  <summary>Screenshots</summary>
  
![CleanShot 2023-12-05 at 16 03 44@2x](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/8bac7b5e-f6f3-4493-8ff3-f768d95fb926)

![CleanShot 2023-12-05 at 16 03 54@2x](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/92ed9adc-aed8-46d2-9e77-14cb77b7b0a4)

![CleanShot 2023-12-05 at 16 04 01@2x](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/3d9e413e-00fa-4e34-b8bd-378e9e2978b6)

![CleanShot 2023-12-05 at 16 04 08@2x](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/5ab9d29d-184f-47f7-8895-c46db750c66a)

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #466 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
The approach here was to create an easy to use CSS class (or component but didn't go that route) to layout components on the page.

### Why not style `q-page` instead of individual components?

Great question. The `destination-header` look would not have been possible with this approach. To get a fully bordered, background-colored element it needs to either:
- have no margin (which isn't part of the element for border or background-color purposes)
- have a set margin to counter act with a negative margin (to expand the border-box that was reduced by the original margin)

Since we set a max width neither of these options work with `margin-left: auto` and `margin-right: auto`. 

To achieve what we want we have to make each component, element, section, whatever you want to call it handle its own layout.

### Quasar Sizing

Quasar has its own breakpoints, and sizing utilities.

The breakpoints are a bit on the large size (only 2 breaks from 1080px down) so I stuck with using their `xs`, `sm`, and then generalized for `md` and up since the max-width covers those well. I had to set the media queries using pixels rather than the CSS variables for Quasar breakpoints since `var()` isn't supported in media query definitions.

The [sizing utilities in Quasar](https://quasar.dev/style/spacing#flex-addons) are restrictive. Only 5 sizes are available (xs-xl). I kept my pixel sizes for my CSS using those so our spacing in the application feels consistent even though it doesn't match the mock all that well.

### Pixels vs Rem

Originally I wrote this in `rem` sizing to be responsive based on the font size of the browser, but Qausar doesn't use `rem` for any of its sizing so I reverted to using `px` - again for consistency. 

## Directions for Reviewers
Check out the various pages of the Publisher, and try it out on different screen sizes, in VSCode, emulate large and small screens. It should feel responsive in a simple way.

Since a lot of changes are wrapping components with a `div` I recommend using the "Hide whitespace" feature while reviewing this PR.

title: Validate config files
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
This PR validates configuration files and deployment records against their defined schema when loading.

Existing configuration and deployment records don't match the schema (the schema URL itself is wrong among other things), and there were some issues with the schema definitions. They now match, but **all existing configuration and deployment files should be removed since they will no longer load**.

Schemas are now live on the CDN:
* Currently supported subset of [config](https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json) and [deployment record](https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-record-schema-v3.json)
* Draft of full attribute set of [config](https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/draft/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json) and [deployment record](https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/draft/posit-publishing-record-schema-v3.json)

Fixes #416

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [x] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
Use `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v5`, which supports the latest jsonschema standard, to do the validation. 

Schemas are stored in an embed FS in in `internal/schema`, and we register a loader to handle Posit CDN references by loading from that FS.

## Automated Tests
Unit tests validate:
* the schema definitions load (current and draft versions)
* the example files validate against the schemas (current and draft versions)
* everywhere in any test that we load a config or deployment record, validation succeeds

## Directions for Reviewers
Remove old configuration and deployment records that are known to be invalid. Then init to create a new, valid config file. 

If you're editing one of the new config files or deployment records in VSCode with the Even Better TOML extension, the new CDN-hosted schema should be active and providing you with tooltips and validation rules.

Publish. Then re-publish using the saved record, to ensure that the record loads.
```
cd {your project}
rm -rf .posit/
just run init $(pwd)
just run publish -n dogfood $(pwd)
ID=$(ls .posit/publish/deployments | head -n1)
just run publish -u ${ID} $(pwd)
```

If you create a problem in your config file, you should see an error like:
```
 jsonschema: '' does not validate with https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json#/additionalProperties: additionalProperties 'foo' not allowed
```
or
```
 jsonschema: '/validate' does not validate with https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json#/properties/validate/type: expected boolean, but got string
```

description:

## Intent
This PR adds a validation step after deployment, as in https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect-python/pull/511.

Validation is the default but can be disabled by setting `validate = false` in the deployment configuration.

Fixes #437

## Type of Change

## Approach
The Connect client has a new ValidateDeployment method that accesses the deployed content using the user's credentials. This will fail if the app cannot successfully start (for example, it has an import error, or raises an exception in code that runs during import).

This also adds a new event phase `publish/validateDeployment` for the validation step. Since validation takes a couple seconds, this should have its own phase in the progress UI.

Deploy an app and see the validation step in the log:
```
time=2023-12-04T17:45:42.087-05:00 level=INFO msg="Validating deployment" event_op=publish/validateDeployment event_phase=start
time=2023-12-04T17:45:44.315-05:00 level=INFO msg=Done event_op=publish/validateDeployment event_phase=success ok=true

```
time=2023-12-04T17:42:25.406-05:00 level=INFO msg="Validating deployment" event_op=publish/validateDeployment event_phase=start
time=2023-12-04T17:42:27.337-05:00 level=ERROR msg="unexpected response from the server" event_op=publish/validateDeployment event_phase=failure error_code=serverErr URL=https://rsc.radixu.com/content/43485fe8-b037-4f2a-9f7e-e604d5347a1c Method=GET Status=500

title: Show status of asynch publish by using events
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Adds Server-side-events back into the UX and updates the two deployment headers to display a basic progress via received events.

Resolves #435 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The prior support for our eventStream plugin has been brought back into the project, along with the type definition for the events we had defined.

In order to have persistence and multiple-component access to the publishing events, I've created a `pina` store called `events`, which is responsible for opening the connection and subscribing/handling all of the publish events. It also provides a new ref variable which indicates if a publishing operation is in progress or not.

This store also provides a publish method (`initiatePublishProcessWithEvents`), which will reset the publishing in progress  ahead of messages coming in, so that serialization of publish operations can be better controlled. (If we simply relied upon start/completed messages, our logic for supporting only one publish process would have a small pre-initialization window issue.) If this becomes a real issue, we'll implement a semaphore around publishing.

This store receives the incoming messages and then records them within a Map which is keyed by the publishing id (`localId`). For this PR, the messages have been limited to just `publish/start`, `publish/success`, and `publish/failure`. A new structure has been created that records the status of each publishing run (`PublishStatus`).

The two headers (`ExistingDeploymentDestinationHeader` and `NewDestinationHeader`) have been updated to leverage this new functionality. They initiate publishing through the event store, enable/disable their publishing button based on the reference from the events store which indicates if a publish run is in progress (`publishInProgess`) as well as creates a computed string that determines a summary of it's particular publish run's status.

The techniques implemented here are to establish an approach. They will be expanded in an upcoming PR to show the entire lifecycle of the publishing process.

## Automated Tests
<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

## Directions for Reviewers
<!-- Provide steps for reviewers to validate this change manually. -->
Publishing should work for new and re-deployments as before. Please confirm the following:
1. Upon navigating to the deployment page, the "TEMP: Publishing Status" should start out as "unknown" and the Publish button should be enabled.
2. Clicking the publish button should change the status to "in-progress" and the publish button should become disabled. 
3. The publish button stays disabled until the status updates to "completed" showing either success or error.

description:
This PR adds an un-styled component called `ConfigSettings` that displays Configurations and Configuration Errors that we get back from the API.

Because Deployments also have their configurations nested in side of the object we can use a Configuration from the `/api/configurations` API and the deployment from `/api/deployments` to fill this component.

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #377 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
The `ConfigSettings` component will display the error given if it is a `ConfigurationError` type. If not it uses `v-ifs` to determine if it should show each of the sections in the config. Some of these are very straight forward - like title. Others are a bit more complex. The complexity for display is not handled here, but additional components can be added for things like displaying Tags or the Python environment well (rather than a raw object). 

The Existing Deployment Destination Page is very straight forward. We can use the `deployment` we fetch to display the configuration settings.

The New Deployment Destination Page is a bit trickier. Since we are only supporting a default configuration in Alpha I fetch the configurations (we don't have an API to fetch a single configuration) and find the default by name. If it isn't available I present an error that a default configuration will be created. Since we have no way of determining what the configuration will be until it is generated there is nothing to display here prior to publishing.

This isn't a great user experience for new users so perhaps in the future we can generate a dry run configuration, if generating a new one, so we can display a read-only view to the user of what will be used to publish.

title: Add deployment record to the bundle being uploaded
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
To support the Collaboration through Connect use case, the deployed bundle needs to include the deployment record with the target information. Currently, the record is written after the bundle is created and the content item is created (since we the file list from bundle creation and the deployment ID from content item creation).

Fixes #413 

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

This PR changes the deployment sequence to:
* create new deployment with default settings (if not a redeployment)
* pre-scan the file list and write out the deployment record
* create the bundle
* upload the bundle
* actuate new settings (update the content item, and set environment variables). 
* deploy the uploaded bundle

We actuate new settings as late as possible so that changes in Connect are done after bundling and uploading, which could fail. We have to do them before running the deployed code, which requires the updated settings.

## Automated Tests
Existing test was updated to support the new sequence.

## Directions for Reviewers
Start with no deployment records. Deploy content to Connect. Download the bundle from Connect and see that there are deployment records in the bundle tarball, in `.posit/publish/deployments/*/latest.toml`. The history files (`.posit/publish/deployments/*/v*.toml`) are in the default ignore list, so they are not included in the bundle.

Adds lifecycle management to the assistant.

title: Create stub pages for the new config based frontend
description:
This PR does a few things:
- Installs and sets up [`vue-router`](https://router.vuejs.org/)
- Creates stub pages for the 3 pages we need in the UI
  - Project page
  - Deployment Destination page
  - Publish Progress page

## Intent
- Resolves #369

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
I created a new `router` module at `src/router.ts` to encapsulate that construction outside of `main.ts` and used the three new page components in the routes array.

The Deployment Destination page accepts an `:id` in the route to distinguish which destination it is. Currently this just puts it in the header.

Following the [vue-router Getting Started guide](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/) I used the `createWebHashHistory` which you can read about [here](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/essentials/history-mode.html).

You may notice a `#` before the URL this is because of this mode. We can switch in a future PR if we need to but that requires doing some additional work detailed in their documentation.

This also doesn't handle 404s.

## Directions for Reviewers
Ensure you can navigate to the three pages using the URLs in the router:
- [Project page](http://localhost:9000/#/)
- [Progress page](http://localhost:9000/#/progress)
- [Deployment Destination page](http://localhost:9000/#/destination/1)

Take a look at the URLs chosen to see if you agree with them.

## Directions for Reviewers
* Run `connect-client init` to create the default config file (and requirements.txt if needed).
* Deploy new content with `connect-client -n $account publish`, optionally specifying the configuration (`connect-client -n $account -c default`)
* Update existing content with `connect-client publish -u $id`, where id can be found in .posit/deployments (omit the .toml suffix). This implies a configuration name and server URL. The server URL will be looked up in your account list. Currently, it takes the first match, so if you have multiple accounts on the same server, it might pick the "wrong" one.
* Deploy through the UI with `connect-client publish-ui`. The Publish button works, but always selects the default account and configuration until we implement account/target selection.
* Look at the config file and deployment records.

title: Add sub-title for downloading and/or installing python packages
description:
This PR uses the `publish/restorePythonEnv/status` event to fill out a subtitle for the "Restore Python Environment" progress step. You can see a preview of it in action below:

<details>
  <summary>Preview</summary>

https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/22d8734e-3456-4731-9e4b-de7719dfa5b3

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #299 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [X] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
The status event message gives us a few details:
- `status` which can be download, install, or a combination (denoted with `download+install`)
- `name` which is the package name being downloaded and/or installed
- potentially a `version` this can be an empty string, or contain a version

This information is converted into a nicer, human readable string like: **"Downloading and installing package: fastapi (0.103.2)"**

Frequently the version isn't available.

## Directions for Reviewers
Do a new deployment using the UI, and check out the new subtitle being generated. It must be a new deployment - if a python environment is cached then no status events get fired since no packages are being installed or downloaded, they are just used from cache.

To do this frequently I pointed the UI to publish to Yeti and would clear out the python environments that were created after each deployment with `rm -rf /yeti-volume/dev-saml/data/python-environments/pip/3.11.3/mAmALwYH07p1w_JRq4GU3g/` inside the yeti shell (`just shell dev-saml`)

title: Separate progress and status events
description: After a code tour with @mmarchetti we came to the decision that lumping in `Status` log events in the `Progress` event type was confusing. This PR breaks them apart, and creates new typing in the frontend to handle that with the `publish/restorePythonEnv/status` event.

Closes #326 

Adds dynamic port allocation to launch multiple instances on a separate instance.

Additionally, resolves issues with WebView rendering due to incorrect CSP configuration.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->

- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The `vscode.window` API does not provide a callback to obtain terminal output. There is a proposal, but it is still experimental.

Instead, we obtain the port using the `get-port` library. This library returns an open port on localhost.

Additionally, a class `Assistant` is added to maintain the port information between starting the process and rendering the panel.

### Known Issues

It's possible for the port to be used by another process before the server is launched. This is unlikely.

If the WebView renders before the executable finishes launching the server, the WebView panel will be empty. A wait for 3 seconds is added to accommodate for this. A better solution would be to use `wait-for`.

title: Add Nightly Deploy Tests
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

This PR adds deployment tests to run at night against a fuzzbucket instance running Connect. 

Workflows:
* `nightly.yaml`: This runs at 1 AM EST and kicks off all the tests and build workflows that the `pull-request.yaml` runs as well as the `contract-deps`, `contract`, `cleanup`
* `contract-deps.yaml`:  currently this only contains a way to start a fuzzbucket instance running Connect. In the future, we can add ways to run other deployment targets and their dependencies here.
* `contract`: this is where we run the new `test-deploy` target that kicks off deployments from the publish-ui to our new fuzzbucket instance we started in `contract-deps`
* `cleanup`: this stops the fuzzbucket instance we started.

Cypress Tests:
* `contract`: This currently contains only one spec that deploys the content, then checks to ensure the content was deployed properly to our fuzzbucket instance. 
* `ui`: I also split out the existing `home` spec into a `ui` folder.  Tests in the `ui` folder will test the local `publish-ui` without the need to have a running Connect instance for deployments.  

The `pull-request` and `main` workflows will continue to run the `ui` tests but not the `contract` tests since these take longer to run due to fuzzbucket startups. and rely on network connections.

Setup: 
`test/setup/` folder contains scripts to install the latest available dev version of Connect and gets the address using fuzzbucket (`connect_setup.py`) and a script to calculate an api key given a username (`gen_apikey.py`). We then store the Connect address as `CONNECT_SERVER` and the api key as `CONNECT_API_KEY` so we can use the `-n env` flag to publish content.  This may change in the future when we have better ways to add accounts.

Fuzzbucket:
The fuzzbucket instance I created is called `ubuntu22-publishing-client`. It has 3 users (admin, publisher, viewer) and I pre-deployed content to build caches for each of the Connect jumpstart examples so deploys won't take long in the `contract` tests mentioned above.  It currently has Python 3.11.4 and R 4.1.2.

title: Listen for and show publish failure events in progress view
description:
This PR makes each step in the publish process subscribe to its correlated `/failure` server side event. It uses the same `msg.data.message` extraction and places that inside of the logs passed to `PublishStep.vue` which styles `error` logs and the surrounding expandable section.

<details>
  <summary>Preview</summary>
  
![CleanShot 2023-10-26 at 14 15 57](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/c77f8061-daa2-4419-b526-3ae8bfd53d5e)

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #302

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
My approach here was to make the generic component `PublishStep.vue` style itself differently if it received a log message that was an error. If it contains an error message it `hasError = true` which changes the icon, color, and stylizes the error to be semi-bold (medium weight) and red as well.

Some TypeScript changes (types and type predicate functions) were needed to distinguish from a generic string log message and an `AdvancedLog` message which kept the usage of `PublishStep.vue` as simple as possible.

A lot of the changes in the publish step components is the same other than the event they specifically subscribe to.

## Directions for Reviewers
Create an error when publishing to see the error get handled. The easiest example that I used was pointing to a non-existent destination like a stopped `localhost:3939`.

Keep in mind we cannot cancel a publish, and an error message doesn't currently set `publishInProgress = false` to allow the usage of the back button. Of course we can change that in another PR or here based on feedback.

title: Add `PUT /api/deployment/title` endpoint to set title
description:
This PR creates a new endpoint - `PUT /api/deployment/title` - that takes a title, sets the deployment state, and returns the new state.

## Intent
- Part of #305 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
This is very similar to how our files endpoint works, and uses a lot of the same structure.

## Automated Tests
Go unit tests are included for all of the changes.

## Directions for Reviewers
To test fire up the client using something like:
```
just run publish-ui \
test/sample-content/fastapi-simple \
--listen=127.0.0.1:9001 \
--skip-browser-session-auth \
--title=abc
```

Then make an API request to change the title - I use [HTTPIE](https://httpie.io/) for this sort of thing:
```
http PUT :9000/api/deployment/title title=some-title -v
```

In the response you should see that the title for your deployment has changed from "abc" to "some-title". 

Then, even if the UI, hasn't updated you can hit the "Publish" button as see the new title since the UI doesn't actually adjust the deployment state yet.

title: Update Title input field to reference Pinia deployment store
description:
## Intent

The GET `api/deployment` API call returns the initial title value at the object path of `connect.content.title` and stores it within the `deployment` pinia store.

The Title input field should be wired to display the value and update it upon change within the store.

Solves: #275 

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [X] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

Since the deployment object is possibly undefined, we are unable to use Pinia's `storeToRefs` functionality to directly hook up the title to the v-model of the input field. Instead, we need to use a computed wrapper and provide getters/setters to allow the checking against the undefined object path. (Unfortunately, optional chaining will not work with Vue's `v-model`.) 

I also discovered that the types file was incorrect for the `content` object.

## Automated Tests
Unit test was updated with the corrected object spec.

## Directions for Reviewers
By using the `--title` CLI parameter, you can specify an initial value for title. If you do this, the value you pass in should be displayed within the Title field. If you pass in nothing, then the field should be blank. Updating the field should update the pinia store value (confirmable via developer tools as well as observing that the value typed in stays there).

Sample command for specifying a title:
```
./bin/darwin-amd64/connect-client publish-ui \
test/sample-content/fastapi-simple \
--listen=127.0.0.1:9001 \
--open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" \
--skip-browser-session-auth \
--account-name=dogfood \
--title=abc
```

title: Runtime Pallete/Color Adjustments w/ Account Selection
description:
## Intent

The code changes that landed on this branch were initially intended to provide account selection functionality for the UX. Early feedback for the UX design requested styling changes that were not easily provided by the built-in capabilities of our UX component package (Quasar). 

This PR includes both the changes to present account selection within the UX as well as provides a runtime adjustment of styling corresponding to dark vs. light mode.

resolves: #269, resolves: #242


## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

For the Account Selection, a selection list of "cards" is built dynamically from the results of the `accounts` API. These cards provide a radio button interface for selection. It should be noted that selection of the account is not yet "functional". There is an upcoming PR that will provide the API required for the UX to set the selected account/destination.

A sample screenshot is below (in Dark Mode).

![2023-10-11 at 4 42 PM](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/f75d6c41-ab54-4f83-98c1-41a81541a044)

For the ability to set styles and colors dynamically at runtime (in concert with the runtime selection of the `dark` mode), I am using a combination of two approaches. 

1. Where dynamic class definitions are needed, I am using Vue3's `v-bind` in CSS feature. This allows the dynamic updating of attributes within the style sheet attached to the component's DOM tree.  

2. Where a Quasar component supports a color palette prop, I am using their built in ability to accept string values from their defined palette (with a few additions).

To accomplish this, some framework functionality was required:
- `utils/colorValues.ts` was created and defines the Quasar SASS color palette variables in terms that we can use them as both string values as well as convert them to hex. This allows us to use these logical variable names for both Quasar prop values as well as setting hex values within raw CSS style statements.
- A new pinia store was created `stores/color.ts` in which an active palette is maintained for reference through the codebase. The values/colors that this palette assumes are based on the active mode for the Quasar Dark plugin, which are currently statically defined within the store. (This is fully compatible with our future need to support runtime re-definition of these colors.)
- Our Vue components were then updated to use values out of the pinia color store. In some cases, this use was to simply use the string values directly. In other cases, they referenced reactive class definitions which used the store values.
- Initial selection of colors and styles were created for both the dark and light modes. Adjusting these going forward will be a very straightforward exercise thanks to the straightforward association of logical attributes to color values provided for within the store.

**PLEASE NOTE:**
- that the adaption of our components to use these color definitions is a rolling target. The set of changes included in this PR is simply the start of this process.
- The temporary publish events view was not updated with this work. After Jordan's PR lands, we'll be going back and adapting it to use these facilities.

Screenshots of the sections are shown below:

**DARK MODE:**

![2023-10-11 at 4 58 PM](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/6e9494a8-1cea-4bca-9484-916eddd051c0)

description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->

<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Refactors the Cypress tooling to avoid diverging executing paths between localhost and GitHub Actions.

### Known Issues

Cypress still does not work within Docker on GitHub Actions. This is due to "bugs" in Cypress. This is resolved by the in the Cypress Docker image by executing [`chmod 777 /root`](https://hub.docker.com/layers/cypress/included/latest/images/sha256-5132ea1f63d99eb0301349493495735661728af22e4f6233aa3c653fcd30a9b4?context=explore). We don't want to do this in `./build/ci/Dockerfile`, so in the future we can build a downstream image that adds this change.

Additionally, Docker on `macOS` fails due to a vague issue with DBus. The Cypress Docker resolves this by setting [`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=/dev/null`.](https://hub.docker.com/layers/cypress/included/latest/images/sha256-5132ea1f63d99eb0301349493495735661728af22e4f6233aa3c653fcd30a9b4?context=explore) 

```
qemu: uncaught target signal 5 (Trace/breakpoint trap) - core dumped
qemu: uncaught target signal 5 (Trace/breakpoint trap) - core dumped
[263:1010/184153.558083:ERROR:bus.cc(399)] Failed to connect to the bus: Failed to connect to socket /run/dbus/system_bus_socket: No such file or directory
```

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The existing implementation required diverging code paths when executing on localhost versus on GitHub Actions.

This change moves the Cypress files to an isolated directory with a separate Node dependencies cache. This avoids weirdness when building within Docker and executing Cypress tests outside of Docker.

The `start` (`just cy run start`) command is modified to call `just ../../run`, which dynamically resolves to the correct executable.

The E2E GitHub Action is modified to use a Matrix strategy since the execution is no longer different between operating systems.

## Automated Tests
<!-- Describe the automated tests associated with this change. -->
<!-- If automated tests are not included in this change, please state why. -->

title: Add components for displaying progress using event subscriptions
description:
Create the initial frontend components for the Publish Progress view. Utilizes the new event stream plugin to share the EventStream between all of the progress step components.

This PR is a bit bigger than I'd like but the step components are all very similar just subscribing to different events and using different titles / subtitles.

<details>
  <summary>Preview Screenshots</summary>
  
![CleanShot 2023-10-05 at 16 37 28](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/85c5b92c-f818-423a-9770-c62c0ce71399)

</details> 

<details>
  <summary>Video</summary>

https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/c963a816-7877-4445-bb92-a7de916886f6

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #233 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
The approach here was to create a new component for each publish process step that handled its own setup of the generic `PublishStep` component, its events, done state, logs, event subscriptions, unsubscribes, etc. 

`PublishStepper` collects all of those and handles the current open step to show our progress publishing.

### Some Notes

- There is a race condition here since the publish button triggers the api call to publish. However Vue is **quick** and is receiving the events even though it is setting up the components - and therefor the subscriptions to events - after the API call is done. Something to be aware of, but not something we have to tackle right away
- We still need to filter events on the `localID` of events for this particular deployment. That is not being done yet.
- The events are _quick_ in some cases causing the steps to only be open and events visible for a fraction of second.
- The logs are the full events from the backend and aren't displayed any particular way.
- The styling for this is not considered and uses the defaults for Quasar.
- Failures are not handled yet.

There are a lot of improvements to make, but in an effort to work toward smaller PRs and iterative development I've left those out of this PR.

Adds release CI and modifies existing build tooling
description:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title. -->
<!-- Examples: Updates pull request template -->

## Intent
<!-- Describe what problem you are addressing in this pull request. -->
<!-- If this change is associated with an open issue, please link to it here. -->
<!-- Example: "Resolves #24" -->
<!-- See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

Establishes a workflow for creating releases and adds associated tooling. Additionally modifies the existing CI to achieve the following:
- Faster caching in GitHub Actions.
- Use composable workflow calls to minimize redundancy in GitHub Actions workflows.
- Make everything* work in Docker.
- Use varargs to pass arguments from root `Justfile` to nested `Justfile`s

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
<!-- Describe how you solved this problem and any trade-offs you encountered. -->
<!-- Link any additional documentation associated with this change here -->

The [Release Action](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/blob/84b78fcfce467ce1237c6f4f55abb40b6d4afc00/.github/workflows/release.yaml) is triggered once a valid tag is pushed (e.g., `git tag v0.0.0 && git push origin v0.0.0`). An overview of the release lifecycle is documented in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/blob/84b78fcfce467ce1237c6f4f55abb40b6d4afc00/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Also, various parts of the code base have been changed, which are discussed in further detail below.

### Changes to Justfiles

- Refactored `./justfile`  to simplify development in-and-out of Docker.
- Modifies `./web/justfile` to use standard nomenclature.
- Added `./test/bats/justfile` for Bats
- Added `./test/cy/justfile` for Cypress

Previously, commands in `./web/Justfile` which need to be executed within Docker were aliased in `Justfile` as separate commands (e.g., `just web/build -> just build-web`, `just web/test -> just test-web`).  This change removes these commands favoring argument forwarding via `just {target} *args`. (e.g., `just web build`, `just web test`).

_Note that `DOCKER=false just web test` is equivalent to `just web/test`._

#### Commands

`./Justfile`

```
Available recipes:
    all *args       # Executes commands where avaiable. WARNING your mileage may very.
    a *args         # alias for `all`
    bats *args      # Executes commands in ./test/bats/justfile. Equivalent to `just test/bats/`, but inside of Docker (i.e., just _with_docker just test/bats/).
    build           # Compiles the application using Go. Executables are written to `./dist`. If invoked with `env CI=true` then executables for all supported architectures using the Go toolchain.
    b               # alias for `build`
    clean           # Deletes ephemeral project files (i.e., cleans the project).
    c               # alias for `clean`
    cover           # Display the code coverage collected during the last execution of `just test`.
    co              # alias for `cover`
    cy *args        # Executes commands in ./test/cy/justfile. Equivalent to `just test/cy/`, but inside of Docker (i.e., just _with_docker just test/cy/).
    default         # Quick start
    executable-path # Prints the executable path for this operating system. It may not exist yet (see `just build`).
    fix             # Fixes linting errors
    image           # Build the image. Typically does not need to be done very often.
    im              # alias for `image`
    lint            # staticcheck, vet, and format check
    l               # alias for `lint`
    pre-release     # Prints the pre-release status based on the version (see `just version`).
    run *args       # Runs the CLI via `go run`.
    r *args         # alias for `run`
    stub            # Creates a fake './web/dist' directory for when it isn't needed.
    tag             # Prints the Docker image tag.
    test            # Execute unit tests.
    t               # alias for `test`
    version         # Print the version.
    v               # alias for `version`
    web *args       # Executes commands in ./web/Justfile. Equivalent to `just web/dist`, but inside of Docker (i.e., just _with_docker web/dist).
    w *args         # alias for `web`
```

`./web/Justfile`

```
Available recipes:
    build     # Compiles the static assests for the web client. Static assets are written to `./web/dist`.
    b         # alias for `build`
    clean     # Deletes ephemeral project files (i.e., cleans the project).
    c         # alias for `clean`
    default
    dev       # Launch a local web server instance with hot-reloads.
    fix       # Fixes formatting using ESLint
    install   # Installs dependencies
    i         # alias for `install`
    lint      # Checks formatting using ESLint
    l         # alias for `lint`
    preview   # Launch a local web server instance in production mode.
    p         # alias for `preview`
    run *args # Executes commands via `npm`. Equivalent to `npm run`. Provides arbitrary command chaining inside of Docker from project root (i.e., `just web run preview`)
    r *args   # alias for `run`
    test      # Executes unit tests
    t         # alias for `test`
    watch     # Watches unit tests
    w         # alias for `watch`
```

`./test/bats/justfile`

```
Available recipes:
    clean     # Deletes ephemeral project files (i.e., cleans the project).
    c         # alias for `clean`
    default
    install   # Install dependencies
    i         # alias for `install`
    run *args # Executes commands via `npm`. Equivalent to `npm run`. Provides arbitrary command chaining inside of Docker from project root (i.e., `just bats run test`)
    test      # Executes Cypress tests
    t         # alias for `test`
```

`./test/cy/justfile`

```
Available recipes:
    clean     # Deletes ephemeral project files (i.e., cleans the project).
    c         # alias for `clean`
    default
    install   # Install dependencies
    i         # alias for `install`
    run *args # Executes commands via `npm`. Equivalent to `npm run`. Provides arbitrary command chaining inside of Docker from project root (i.e., `just cy run test`)
    test      # Executes Cypress tests
    t         # alias for `test`
```

### Changes to GitHub Actions

This change decomposes the existing workflows into discrete re-useable sections, which are tied together using workflow calls. Additional information on workflow calls is available [here](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/reusing-workflows).

Changes to caching are implemented to use best practices as defined by Docker. See https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha/

### Changes to Dockerfiles

The existing Dockerfile is based on CentOS 7, which is deprecated. Historically, we have continued using CentOS 7 in Connect to catch regressions when linking to different versions of `glibc`. I have verified that this project does not depend on `glibc`, therefore it is safe to build on a newer OS. I have chosen Ubuntu since this is the OS we are using in GitHub Actions.

title: Create and use event stream Vue plugin
description:
Supersedes #254 providing a Vue plugin to setup and give access to a global `EventStream`.

## Intent

title: Add Typescript typing for events and filter for current publishing job id
description:
## Intent

Demonstrate the ability to filter on `local_id` established when the `publish/start` event is received and completed when the `publish/success` event is received.

During the implementation of this feature, it became obvious that we needed to establish better typing for the events. This lead to the large enhancements included within this PR.

Resolves #225 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

1. `EventSubscriptionTarget` enhanced with additional events for SSE added from stream and agent code analysis.
2. Sample SSE event stream added into code comments
3. Added interfaces which specialize an `EventStreamMessage` and provided type guards for them to support proper typing. Also provided type specific event callbacks for each of these interfaces.
4. Created a union type of our base and our extended interfaces
5. Temporarily converted specific failure events into generic failure events within the initial Event Stream processing. This was done ahead of modifying the Agent to send these naturally. Once it does, we can remove this code in a future PR.
6. Update `App.vue` to subscribe to all events using these updated interfaces
7. Update `PublishProcess.vue` to use the event specific interfaces to filter the events it receives to only correspond to the current publishing stream.

## Directions for Reviewers
In order to most easily understand these changes, I suggest you examine the files in this order:
1. web/src/api/types/events.ts
2. web/src/api/resources/EventStream.ts
3. web/src/App.vue
4. web/src/components/publishProcess/PublishProcess.vue

To validate this branch before merging, you would simply need to run it and hit publish, verifying that you see the events displayed on the temporary output.
- Building the agent and Web UX for this branch: `just build-dev`
- Starting the agent with valid cmd line parameters. For example:
```
./bin/darwin-amd64/connect-client publish-ui test/sample-content/fastapi-simple \
--listen=127.0.0.1:9001 \
--open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" \
--skip-browser-session-auth \
--account-name=dogfood
```
- Hit the publish button
- Validate that the server events are displayed
- When they stop and the publish messages indicate the content publishing process was successful, the Back button on the top should be enabled. Clicking it should take you back to the configuration page.

title: Configure vitest with API and Pinia mocking
description:
This PR creates a single test for `FilesToPublish.vue` to setup our patterns for unit testing our frontend with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/), [Vue Test Utils](https://test-utils.vuejs.org/), and [Pinia's testing tooling](https://pinia.vuejs.org/cookbook/testing.html).

**Dependencies added:**
- `@vue/test-utils` for mounting components and easily testing them
- `jsdom` to test in a web environment (and access web APIs) rather than being constrained by a Node testing environment
- `@pinia/testing` to create a Pinia instance specifically for unit testing

**Config changes:**
- Set vitest testing env to `jsdom`
- Unit test files were added to the `include` for the TypeScript config to get the path alias and settings
- Quasar's dark plugin was added
  - This was to fix an error that would occur whenever mounting the component where the dark object properties were attempted to be accessed, but of course that would cause a `undefined` error.
  
**API Type Changes:**
- A property was removed from `DeploymentFile` since our API currently doesn't return it, and our mocked returns need to match our types
- All enums were not exported from our API module, removing `export types` fixed this and allowed us to import the Enums for use in the testing files.

## Intent
Addresses #167

## Approach
This PR doesn't fully test `FilesToPublish.vue` instead it focuses on getting a single test with mocks working for easy expansion. This allows us to review the pattern / methodology used as opposed to a whole suite of tests as well.

Dependencies and configurations were added while establishing a `FilesToPublish.test.ts` file. With each error encountered something was adjusted until a full test was created with the tooling we needed to expand.

Since this is only one test I did not pull out util functions, mock data files, or anything else to reduce the size of the files or create anything to reduce duplication in new tests. That can be done when new tests are actually created.

## Directions for Reviewers
- Take a look at the patterns introduced here and see if you agree with them or have any questions.
- Pull this branch down and run `npm run test:unit` in the `web` directory OR run `just web/test-unit` to run `vitest`
- Ensure your development environment works for Vitest
  - Note for VSCode to run Vitest you will need to open the `web` directory on its own since the Vitest extension doesn't handle the configs being nested well.

title: Receive Server-Side-Events within the UX and display them raw on the Publishing Process view
description:
## Intent
This PR provides the plumbing within the UX to receive the Server-Side-Events being made available from the Agent and updates the Agent code to provide a API endpoint to expose them. The events are displayed on the publish process view after the user hits the publish button on the configuration view.

Resolves #161.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
- A new endpoint has been added to the agent: `/api/events`
- The UX opens a connection to this endpoint on the agent during initialization of the app and closes it before the main app component is unmounted.
- All events received are added to an array hosted by the main component and then passed into the publishing process view as a prop.
- The publishing process component shows the event array as raw output and automatically scrolls the window to keep the last event in view.
- The publishing process component also subscribes to the publish complete event and uses it to enable the back button on its view, once publishing has completed. The button is disabled by default.

## Automated Tests
- A minor unit test was updated for the agent code.
- e2e tests can now wait on the back button being enabled (data-automation tag of "BackToConfiguration").

## Directions for Reviewers
Functionality can be verify by:
- Building the agent and Web UX for this branch: `just build-dev`
- Starting the agent with valid cmd line parameters. For example:
```
./bin/darwin-amd64/connect-client publish-ui test/sample-content/fastapi-simple \
--listen=127.0.0.1:9001 \
--open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" \
--skip-browser-session-auth \
--account-name=dogfood
```
- Hit the publish button
- Validate that the server events are displayed
- When they stop and the publish messages indicate the content publishing process was successful, the Back button on the top should be enabled. Clicking it should take you back to the configuration page.

description:
## Intent

These changes will update `main` with the latest UX base concepts as shown at the Sept 14th, 2023 Sprint Review meeting. These changes were achieved after working with Paul Di Christina and scope to the basic layout and interaction of the App.

It also reorganized the directory structure of the existing code and broke some of the monolithic components into smaller components.

Fixes #218 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

`App.vue` continues to represent the base view of the application, but quickly decomposes to two different views: `ConfigurePublish.vue` and `PublishProcess.vue`. The subcomponents for these views are organized into subfolders as well.

A base menu has been added but has been left empty for now. I've intentionally captured the ideas we had for menu items within commented fields.

The `PublishProcess` component is intentionally blank except for the back button.

NOTE: I recognize that the coordination of the publishing process should move down into a `pinia` store, but did not want to incorporate that in this PR. Because of this, it is possible to initiate another publishing process from the agent while one is already in progress. This PR makes the Publishing API async. It now returns a JSON response containing a unique ID for the deployment, and starts a goroutine to do the actual publishing. This prevents requests from timing out while waiting for the entire deployment process to complete.

Publishing is not cancelable in this implementation, nor is it safe to modify state or publish again while the operation is in progress.

This PR introduces Connect in Fuzzbucket so we can run deploy tests to a real installation of Connect.

* if you want to run the tests locally, you can run `just test/init-connect-and-publish darwin-arm64` which will start Connect in fuzzbucket and run the publishing tests against it (replace darwin-arm64 with whatever architecture you're running, you will need to `just build` first).

* due to some issues accessing environment variables in Windows, I had to add a second target in `web/justfile` and `web/package.json` specifically for Windows.

* the cypress tests added are still under `home.cy.ts`, they don't do much now because I can't yet access the deployment URL to actually test the deployment on Connect.  right now we just make sure we can reach Connect and see that _something_ has been deployed.  i'll likely be adding a different file/folder structure once we're ready to add more tests.

title: Remove Quasar CLI and control our tooling
description:
Forgive me this PR is a long one. It rips out Quasar CLI and sets up the tooling we were using to manage ourselves including:
- Vite
- Pinia
- Cypress
- Vitest
- ESLint
- TypeScript Configs

#### Quasar components

Quasar is still used in the form of its [Vite plugin](https://quasar.dev/start/vite-plugin/) to give us access to components. `@quasar/extras` is included to give us the Roboto font setup and Google Material icons.

#### What wasn't included?

Somethings weren't brought over, but we can easily set them up when we need them like:

- `i18n` which came with Quasar, but we weren't using yet. We can easily setup [`vue-i18n`](https://vue-i18n.intlify.dev/guide/installation.html) or some other tooling
- [Vue Router](https://router.vuejs.org/)

These weren't brought over since there wasn't a way to verify them working. Instead we can add them when necessary with follow-up PRs.

#### What did we get?

A highlight of some of the wins:
- `npm outdated` shows 0 dependencies that need updating. Everything is using the latest version!
- `vue-tsc` is now used to give us TypeScript compilation checking with Vue support as part of our build. If TypeScript doesn't compile we now get a visible error in CI rather than relying on our IDEs.
- Cypress tests are setup to run against dev mode and "production mode" in CI for easier development of Cypress tests locally.
- Reduction of config files that interact with "hidden" Quasar dependencies. `editorconfig`, `nyc`, `postcss`, `quasar`, `quasar.extensions`, `vitest` no longer exist or don't require a config file (in the case of Vitest since it reads the new Vite config).
- Cypress tests and Vitest unit tests are now linted with ESLint.
- One path alias was setup `src` maps to the `web/src` directory.
- The favicon is now the Posit favicon.
- It is much clearer how our dependencies relate to our tooling and code.

## Intent
- Resolves #176 
- Resolves #115 

## Approach
My approach was to create a `web2` directory and setup everything from scratch and bring in our components, utils, modules, and tests one at a time - verifying they work along the way.

Once that was done I removed `web` and renamed `web2 => web` to get a nice git diff. From there I verified the changes, and got to work making the CI work with the changes.

Some of the files moved a bit during this to match the Vite template. Components are now all under the `src/components` directory. `public` no longer has a separate `assets` directory underneath it. I also consolidated `MainLayout` into `App.vue`. These can be separated out again if we need to add Vue Router. They were consolidated to avoid dealing with the `<router-view>` in this PR.

#### ESLint Approach

One of the files with the biggest changes is the ESLint config. What I did here was take what the Vite setup gave us and combined it with the rules from Connect.

This means:
- some of the `parserOptions` and `env` are coming from the Vite setup directly.
- some redundancy was removed using just `plugin:vue/vue3-recommended` rather than the other configs, like essential, that are extended.
- `standard` was removed since it wasn't installed initially
- `import` was removed since we didn't have the plugin setup only the rules. It also conflicts with Vue. (**Perhaps** this should be a follow-up to include those rules again with Vue support).
- Some rules were removed (like `strict: 'error'`) in favor of strict mode, and some were adjusted for easier use with config files or type files.

## Automated Tests
- Vitest is running and passing, but is currently just using a dummy test to show that it is indeed running. This will allow us to expand to actual unit tests in #167 easily.
- Cypress is running with the same tests it had previously and is still integrated into CI.

## Directions for Reviewers
I **highly** recommend going through the commits to understand why certain files were changed or setup a certain way. Until https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/pull/189/commits/49d8f6f095080c47258667ab4b99dd6b4bc9f9c4 you can see how things were setup from scratch.

I also included inline comments to give some highlights of changes that I think are important to note.

A lot of the files that were changed or removed were:
- from Quasar configuration files for itself, extensions, or things it included like i18n, Vue Router, the Store directory, stub tests, etc.
- changes to the build directory `/web/dist/spa => /web/dist`
- using npm scripts and some adjustments to get CI working

title: Add SSE support to the agent
description:
## Intent
This PR adds SSE support to the agent. It supports:
* Forwarding all log messages that appear on stderr (once the UI service starts)
* Providing `*/start` and `*/success` events for the publishing steps
* Annotating Connect server publishing log messages with metadata about the publishing step in progress and the source of the event. Progress/status events have infrastructure support but we don't generate them yet.
* Marshaling error details, when provided, into `*/failure` messages. There is limited support for providing error details at error detection time in this PR.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
We have a new logger type that embeds an `slog.Logger` and adds `Start`, `Status`, `Progress`, `Success`, and `Failure` methods.

Log forwarding is done with a new `MultiHandler` that tees messages to multiple handlers, one of which is a standard handler and the other is a new `SSEHandler` that generates the events.

Errors during publishing can be returned as bare Go errors, or as a more detailed `AgentError` that includes an enumerated error code and optional details. Bare errors will be converted to `AgentError`s by the error handling code in the publishing sequence.

## Automated Tests
There are unit tests.

## Directions for Reviewers
Publish from the CLI as well as the UI.

When publishing from the CLI, we only log to stderr. You should see new messages for start, success, etc.

When publishing from the UI, you should see messages prefixed with `SSE will send:` on stdout.

title: Use slog instead of rslog
description:
This PR changes our structured logging from the `rslog` package to the `slog` package that was introduced into the Go stdlib in go 1.21.0.

## Intent
We intend to extend the logger infrastructure to send logs to the front end as well as to stderr, and also introduce non-log events for the front end to communicate progress, etc.

## Type of Change

title: Upgrade quasar and @quasar/testing-unit-vitest
description:
This PR does a re-install of the Quasar vitest extension and a `quasar upgrade -i` (`quasar upgrade` is a dry-run).

## Intent
- Part of the #167 work

## Approach
Alright this was a bit gross.

`quasar upgrade` did not work right away. I would get an `ERESOLVE` where the dependency  graph could not be resolved. This is because Quasar was attempting to install a new version of `vitest` which didn't match the `package.json` semvar definition that was put there by Quasar in the first place. NPM didn't know what to do - match the dependency for the upgrades or the `package.json` definition so would error.

Additionally `quasar upgrade` wasn't upgrading to the latest version of the `@quasar/testing-unit-vitest` package [^1] but staying in `0.1.x`. According to the Quasar docs to upgrade to a new major version of the extensions you need to remove them, re-add them, overwrite files, and use a git diff to resolve the changes. [^2]

This didn't work either. The re-adding would fail with another `ERESOLVE` because it would attempt to add the new version of the plugin alongside the old `"vitest": "^0.15.0"` in `package.json`.

I had to remove all of the peer dependencies for Quasar's vitest extension manually, do a `rm -rf node_modules && npm install`, then re-add the extension.

Once that was done the resolution using `git diff` was done which was really easy since we are still using the examples. The only change there was the name change for `installQuasarPlugin()`.

After all of that `quasar upgrade -i` finally worked since the dependency resolution could work with the `vitest` version being specified correctly.

**Side Note**: This isn't using the latest `vitest` but instead a version from June 1st since Quasar's extension hasn't upgraded past `0.31.x`.

[^1]: [@quasar/testing-unit-vitest](https://github.com/quasarframework/quasar-testing/tree/dev/packages/unit-vitest)
[^2]: https://testing.quasar.dev/#upgrade-to-a-new-major-version-with-npm

title: Adding simple Logger and ReturnMethod implementations to UX
description:
## Intent
Need a simple way to conditionally log output to the browser console.

Fixes: #160 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

Added a type `ReturnMethod` which follows the pattern used often by Go routines, to include an `ok` as well as `error` if `ok=false`.

Added the ability to suppress `console.debug` messages by default, but enable them by passing in a query string value of `debug`. (Example: `http://127.0.0.1:9000/#/?debug`). This sets us up to liberally use `console.debug` messages throughout the code as verbose logging, but not have them show up for the customer in the default case. Use of `console.error` is not affected. All of the functionality of `console.debug` is maintained with this implementation.

The app startup sequence has been slightly updated in order to start processing only after the app is ready for API calls to be made (`onMounted`). To access the query string values, we also have to wait on the router to be ready. We then are also waiting on the debug state to be established, before we start our first major operation of retrieving the deployment state.

## Automated Tests
None

## Directions for Reviewers
Let me know if you have comments on the implementation or if you have additional ideas. I would like to keep this extremely simple and functional for what is needed.

To verify the debug output:

1. `just build-dev`
2. in one terminal, start `just web/dev`

**Confirm that debug active mode works:**
3. In another terminal, start `./bin/darwin-amd64/connect-client publish-ui /Users/billsager/dev/publishing-client/test/sample-content/fastapi-simple --listen=127.0.0.1:9001 --open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000/#/?debug=true" --skip-browser-session-auth --account-name=dogfood`
4. open the console and confirm that the message `Debug output messages are active!` is shown.

**Confirm that non-debug mode (default) works:**
5. change your URL address in the browser to not have the query string (`http://127.0.0.1:9000/#/`), (possibly reload as the browser doesn't always  pick this up as a navigation change) and confirm that the message `Debug output messages are active!` is NOT shown.
