title: Enforce typescript naming-conventions with ESLint
description:
This PR adds the [`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`](https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/naming-convention/) rule to enforce `camelCase` and `UPPER_CASE` naming.

` selector: ['variableLike', 'classProperty', 'typeProperty'], format: ['camelCase'] },`

Enforces `camelCase` on variables, parameters, functions, class properties, and type properties. `property` wasn't used generally since it affects properties of all kinds including the ESLint rules which don't follow `camelCase` along with several other files. This mainly targets actual TypeScript code and types.

`{ selector: 'variable', modifiers: ['const'], format: ['camelCase', 'UPPER_CASE'] }`

Allows us to use `UPPER_CASE` for more global style constants.

## Intent
- Extension of #153 and #74

## Directions for Reviewers
- Take a look at the rule configuration to see if you agree with it.

title: Use camelCase in the frontend
description:
This PR creates the new [Axios interceptors](https://axios-http.com/docs/interceptors) to convert responses to `camelCase` and requests to `snake_case`. 

A follow-up PR will be created to handle the ESLint changes needed to enforce camelCase naming.

## Intent
- Resolves #74 

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
Two packages were installed to handle this for us. `camelcase-keys` (the same camelCasing package that [Connect uses](https://github.com/rstudio/connect/blob/main/ui/dashboard/package.json)) and the inverse package by the same other `decamelizeKeys`.

The types were updates across the API module and the references updated.

The ESLint ignoring for the `camelcase` rule was ignored since it is no longer relevant. 

Two interceptors were created for Axios as I mentioned above. However this is where we hit a bit of an issue. Our `DeploymentState` contains two object keys that we don't want to be converted to `camelCase`:
- `deployment.manifest.files` contains file pathnames as keys which we want to stay the same
- `deployment.manifest.packages` contains package names as keys which we want to stay the same

To handle this the `camelcaseKeys` function has a parameter called `stopPaths` to prevent the converter from converting along those paths. Rather than having a long array of strings for every path I created a generic solution for this.

`web/src/api/axios.d.ts` was created to extended the TypeScript type for `AxiosRequestConfig` and add an optional key `ignoreCamelCase?: string[]`. When added to the config it is read by the `camelCaseInterceptor` and passed to that `stopPaths` param. Then in API resources like `Deployment` we can add:

```typescript
ignoreCamelCase: ['manifest.files', 'manifest.packages']
```

to the `AxiosRequestConfig`. This allow us to easily set paths we don't want changed for each of our resources if more come up, and have them related as closely as possible to the response types as possible to avoid confusion.

## Automated Tests
No automated tests were added, but it would be a good idea to do as a follow-up to establish or use our testing patterns.

## Directions for Reviewers
- Review the interceptors and ensure they are operating as intended.
- Review the pattern of excluding paths to convert to `camelCase` and see if the pattern is easy to understand and utilize.

title: Add summaries for target and files sections within UX
description:
## Intent
Unexpanded section headers for target and files sections should include summaries.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

Fixes: #140 

Computed summaries were created for each of the sections.

To facilitate the files summary, I needed to calculate the total size of the selected files. The size was included with the `GET /files` API response, so I now created a map, keyed by filePath, which saves off part of the response data. The types were updated to provide both a smaller type for data stored in the map as well as the bigger response type extending the other type, so that types didn't need to be duplicated.

Sample result:

![2023-08-16 at 11 35 AM](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/cf608fe4-90ae-4f02-8371-b4fcabeddf9e)

## Automated Tests
None at this time

## Directions for Reviewers

Start up the UX:
1. `just build-dev`
2. `./bin/darwin-amd64/connect-client publish-ui test/sample-content/fastapi-simple --account-name=dogfood -i`
3. If only have `IPv4` enabled, update the browser window which was opened at the conclusion of step #2, to go to `127.0.0.1` instead of `[::]`
4. Verify that the caption for the Destination section displays your server destination. For example, with an account of `dogfood`:![2023-08-16 at 11 46 AM](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/bce7b5ad-8f07-4755-96e0-079c383b0358)
5. Verify that the summary text for the Files section displays both a file count and summary. NOTE: There is currently a bug that will affect the initial count and sizing. This will be verified after the bug fix is in.
6. Expand the Files section and click on the top-most checkbox to select the entire tree (allowed files only). Verify that the summary is updated and changes with each selection/deselection within the tree. Note that the count is incorrect, but that it is off by the initial count that the header originally indicated for the number of files selected. This will be addressed by issue #138.
7. You can validate the size calculation by examining the sizes returned in the `GET /files` call and make sure I'm both summing only the selected ones plus the total count is converted into a string that can be either bytes, KB or MB. (I used the definition that there are 1024 bytes in a KB and there are 1024 KBs in a MB.) I'm displaying with a 1 decimal precision.

title: Use and update Deployment State with files selected
description:
This PR removes the temporary files Pinia store and instead creates a new Deployment Store to hold onto the Deployment State we get back from `/api/deployment` API calls. It sets up `FilesToPublish.vue` to use that in tandem with the `PUT /api/deployment/files` endpoint to select files to publish.

<details>
  <summary>Preview</summary>

https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/f3f193b5-da6b-4893-8aaf-c8c4602a2f85

</details> 

## Intent
- Resolves #90

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
- The initial Deployment State is loaded in `App.vue` to get the state as quickly as possible in the frontend. When the App component is being setup we fetch the state and put that into our new Pinia store.
- From there `FilesToPublish.vue` can use it to determine what files are ticked in the file tree.
- The Deployment Store contains `deployment` which is the Deployment State in the exact form we receive from the API responses.
- It also contains `files` getters and setters using Vue's `computed` function:
  - The `get` turns the `Deployment.manifest.files` from an object into an array of pathname strings for use to use in `FilesToPublish`
  - The `set` takes that array of pathname strings, sets the state preemptively, and sends it off to `PUT /api/deployment/files`. The response is then used to set the state again to ensure everything is synced.

#### `types` utility functions

This PR creates a new `src/api/utils/index.ts` file that contains two utility types for converting back and forth between `string[]` and `Record<string, ManifestFile>` which are the two forms we need the selected files in. One is for the File Tree `QTree` component and the other is for the Deployment State which holds them in the same form as the Manifest File.

#### `requestOnce` utility function

`requestOnce` is a utility function that is used in the Deployment State, but that I anticipate will be used elsewhere across our stores. It:
- Handles an `AbortController` for us without us having to create one. This will cancel pending API requests to avoid state from being updated with older response data.
- Handles wrapping the passed function with a `debounce()` with the given `wait` millisecond amount to avoid hammering our API with several calls.
- Passes an `AbortSignal` to the function automatically to cancel `Axios` requests.

It allows us to easily setup functions that call the API and their error handling without a ton of boilerplate for debouncing and aborting in progress API requests.

## Directions for Reviewers
The two edge cases to test are:

**Submitting an API request while another hasn't come back:**

This can be tested easily by causing a delay with the `PUT /api/deployment/files` endpoint with:
```typescript
  async setFiles(files: string[], config?: AxiosRequestConfig<DeploymentState>) {
    // wait 1 second
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    return this.client.put<DeploymentState>(
      '/deployment/files',
      { files: files },
      config
    );
  }
```
and reducing the debounce time to `0` to ensure our duplicate requests aren't hitting the debounce.

Then press the checkboxes in the File Tree several times in a second. You should see only one `PUT /api/deployment/files` request in the network and no state flickering.

The next is **debouncing**:

This can be tested by removing the 1 second delay (if you added it) and hitting the File Tree checkboxes several times within `500ms` (the current debounce time).

You should see only one `PUT /api/deployment/files` request after you have finished pressing the checkboxes.

title: Disable checkbox in file tree for excluded files
description:
Nice and simple PR. This one makes files that are `is_excluded: true` not "tickable" in the File Tree.

What that means is:
- they cannot be checked or unchecked - clicking on the checkbox will not change the state of the `ticked` prop
- files can still be in the `filesToPublish` store property and be disabled if we would like different behavior based on what `GET /api/deployment/files` returns we will need to adjust this

<details>
  <summary>Preview</summary>

https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/44838109-37e6-40d2-b3c6-6356151f9e0b

</details> 

## Intent
Resolves #122 

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
This uses `QTree`'s Node's model structure when converting `DeploymentFile`s to `QTreeNode`s and sets `tickable` based on `file.is_excluded`.

There is another option ([discussed here in Slack](https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C05D7NZD52S/p1691697562897719)) called `disabled` that does three things:
- override `tickable`
- prevents the checkbox from being checked
- prevents the collapsing / uncollapsing click action from happening if the file has children

I opted not to use that for the `excluded` for now, but definitely voice your opinions if you believe we should use the other property. We can revisit when dealing with soft and hard exclusions.

## Directions for Reviewers
- Take a look at the logic
- Determine if `tickable` or `disabled` is the right way to go

title: Create Deployment resource with get and setFiles
description:
Adds the Deployment resource in the API library and the associated methods to support the new API endpoints for getting Deployment State and selecting files.

Example Usage:
```
const api = useApi();

const { data: deployment } = api.deployment.get();
api.deployment.setFiles(['some-file.txt']);
```

## Intent
Extension of the work to add `GET /api/deployment` and `PUT /api/deployment/files` and add that functionality to the API library in the frontend.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->

## Approach
I tried two methods here:
- Creating a resource for both endpoints `Deployment` for `/api/deployment` and `DeploymentFiles` for `/api/deployment/files`
- Combining everything under the `Deployment` resource (the one I went with)

I struggled deciding if I wanted the organization to exactly match the endpoints of the API versus being a simple organization and interaction with the API.

`api.deployment.setFiles()` doesn't signify that it is targeting `PUT /api/deployment/files` it doesn't signify that it is using `PUT` necessarily unless you dig into its implementation. However it still communicates the operation and that the list of files you pass will be set for the deployment.

I'm not sure if this is closer to how we want to organize this code so please provide your opinion if you have one 😄

title: Use NODE_KEY const in FilesToPublish
description:
Super small PR that adds a const `NODE_KEY` to `FilesToPublish.vue`. The reason for this is `QTree` takes a [`nodes-key` prop](https://quasar.dev/vue-components/tree#qtree-api) that represents "The property name of each node object that holds a unique node id".

`node-key` is a required Prop, but there is nothing that prevents us from de-syncing what is in the template and what property key we use in our construction of the `QTreeNode`s.

Adding this const gives a stronger connection to the two.

Adds path validation implementation for the **get-files** `pathname` parameter. This implementation should safe guard the host file system from attacks.

The `pathname.IsSafe` method performs three validation actions:
1. Scrubs the `pathname` using [`filepath.Clean`](https://pkg.go.dev/path/filepath#Clean).
2. Verifies that the `pathname` is not a symlink.
3. Verifies that `pathname` resides within the execution directory.

description:
## Intent
This PR is a first implementation of a file selection API, providing `PUT /api/deployment/files` to allow for file selection.

A PUT to the file list replaces the manifest `Files` section with one containing the specified files. Checksums are left empty, to be calculated at deployment time.

Currently this is an incomplete draft. It doesn't validate the provided file paths yet, and there are no unit tests yet.

This endpoint mostly uses the go stdlib, plus a couple of API helper functions. Once we develop a few API endpoints, we will probably want to extract some helpers.

## Automated Tests
To do (must be done before this is ready for review)

## Directions for Reviewers
Run the agent `publish-ui` command.
Open the UI in the browser.
Grab the session cookie from browser devtools to use with curl.
PUT a file list to the endpoint:
```
curl -s -H "$COOKIE_HEADER" http://localhost:59054/api/deployment/files -XPUT -d'{"files": ["app.py", "requirements.txt"]}' | jq
```

title: File exclusion returns the reason for the match
description:
## Intent
This PR adds tracking of the provenance for each file exclusion pattern. The `Match` method returns that metadata instead of just a boolean indicating a match. The List Files API returns the match details as the `exclusion` field, replacing the current `is_excluded` boolean field.

Resolves #42 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
The gitignore `ignoreFile` previous stored only a list of compiled glob patterns. It now stores a list of Match objects that include the glob, as well as the text of the match pattern and a file/line reference to where it originated.

This PR does not add the exclusion info to the File Listing API since that is still in flight.

## Automated Tests
The gitignore package started out externally sourced, and did not include unit tests. This PR adds some tests that provide coverage for most of the gitignore functionality.

## Directions for Reviewers

This is an infrastructure PR that doesn't affect user-visible behavior. Once the Files API integrates this capability it will be externally testable.

## Checklist
- [ ] I have updated [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) to cover notable changes.

title: Setup workspace vscode settings
description:
This PR setups up a `.vscode` workspace setting directory with settings and extension recommendations.

VScode doesn't support multiple `.vscode/settings.json` or `.vscode/extensions.json` config files [^1]. Instead it uses the top level one for the workspace you are in. Rather than requiring the frontend and backend have different workspaces in VSCode we can raise our `.vscode` config directory to the top level.

## Intent
This will assist dev environment setup for those that use VSCode.

## Type of Change
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
<!-- If you check more than one box, you may need to refactor this change into separate pull requests -->

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

This is a tooling setup PR and does not fall under the above 3 change types.

## Approach
I looked at the generated files created from Quasar and included some, but definitely not all of the settings. 

#### Breakdown for `settings.json`

I included:
- `eslint.format.enable": true` to enable ESLint as a formatter, which it isn't by default, since we use it as one
- Setting ESLint as the default formatter for Vue, TypeScript, and Javascript

I didn't include (from the Quasar setup):
- Rules that change affect styling in VSCode (some may not like this):
  - `"editor.bracketPairColorization.enabled": true`
  - `"editor.guides.bracketPairs": true`
- Rules that change onSave actions (which some may not like):
  - `"editor.formatOnSave": true`
  - `"editor.codeActionsOnSave": ["source.fixAll.eslint"]`
-  the `"eslint.validate"` array
   - I believe this is setup by default and uses the `extraFileExtensions` in the `.eslintrc.js` file. This can be checked by reviewers to make sure this isn't specific to my setup.
- `"typescript.tsdk": "node_modules/typescript/lib"` since this gets setup by default

#### Breakdown for `extensions.json`

I included:
- ESLint to support our linting in the frontend
- Volar to add Vue 3 language support
- TypeScript Vue to support TypeScript in `.vue` files

I didn't include (from the Quasar setup):
- `unwantedRecommendations` since that is not supported in VSCode without another extension
- `wayou.vscode-todo-highlight` since we use GitHub Issues and not TODOs as a tracker for tasks
- `ditorconfig.editorconfig` since we have not formalized an Editorconfig for this project or others (can be added later if we like)

## Automated Tests
None - there is no automated testing for development environment configs.

## Directions for Reviewers
Take a look at the VSCode settings and extension recommendations included and see if you agree with them, or if they cause any issues in your local VSCode workspaces.

title: Reorganize justfile recipes and implement parallel CI steps
description:
## Intent

Refactoring main `justfile` and CI steps with improvements suggested in original PR. Also bringing in some of the changes which were in progress prior to closing for PR: https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/pull/37/files.

Resolves #77 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [ ] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [x] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

This includes the renaming of recipes as well as refactoring to limit the logic to one `justfile` if possible. This results in:

1. Recipe names have been changed. For example, `install` and `lint` have been changed to `bootstrap` and `validate`. 
2. Recipe names now use the target as a qualifier within the top level `justfile`. Targets are now `agent` and `web`.
3. The top level `justfile` contains recipes for `agent` as well as convenience recipes for both targets. Docker logic is present only within the top level `justfile`. Web building logic is present within the `web/justfile`. 
 
NOTE: There were too many dependencies within the `agent` recipes to move them out to a separate `justfile`, which was the original intention.

In addition, by renaming the recipes called by the CI workflow steps, this PR also includes the changes necessary to implement parallel CI steps using job dependencies and cached items, setting the stage for optimized CI validation as the codebase and tests grow.

title: Support UX vite dev server functionality while having CLI launch and service API requests
description:
## Intent

This PR adds the ability to utilize the `vite` dev server functionality (error reporting and hot reloading) within a development workflow in which the UX is launched from the CLI (mimicking the actual production execution).

Resolves #66 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach

1. The concept of a "production" build vs. a "development" build has been introduced into the CLI backend. This is set appropriately depending on which build recipe is executed. In this way, CI will produce production code and development workflow _can_ produce development code (or production code). This distinction is used to suppress development functionality from reaching the field.
    - `just build-dev` will build a CLI for the current development platform in "development" mode.
    - `just build` will continue to build CLIs for all of the target platforms in "production" mode. 
3. New CLI flags have been added, which are only acted upon when the CLI backend has been built in production mode. The flags are not listed within the output for `--help`.
    - `--open-browser-at` provides a way in which an interactive mode will be entered, but controls the address which is launched by the browser (rather than the `--interactive` flag which uses the `listen` address).
    - `--skip-browser-session-auth` provides a way to bypass the session token authentication requirement between the UX and the CLI backend.
4. The `quasar` UX environment has been configured to proxy all traffic with the path of `/api` from the `vite` web server over to the internal CLI web server, while still serving up the Web UX from the current code in the repo. Hot reloading and error reporting continue to function w/ this in place.

### Optimized development flow enabled as part of these changes

**NOTE**: The optimized development flow described below will currently only work for `DOCKER="false"` execution dev environments. Since the objective is an optimized flow, that immediately removes the need to support the slower DOCKER execution environment.

#### Steps:

1. Build and start the vite web server, to support error reporting and hot-reloading: `just web/dev` in one terminal. Keep the terminal window open.
    - This will launch the `vite` web server on `http://127.0.0.1:9000`
2. Within a new terminal window, build the development version of the CLI: `just build-dev`. Keep this terminal open, so that you can rebuild as needed.
3. Within a new terminal window, launch the development version of the CLI for the current platform (with these parameters): `./connect-client publish-ui <PROJECT_PATH> --listen=127.0.0.1:9001 --open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" --skip-browser-session-auth`
    - *Where** `<PROJECT_PATH>` above is replaced with a location of a sample project. For example, with a python project at `~/dev/connect-content/bundles/python-flaskapi`, your complete command line would become: `./connect-client publish-ui ~/dev/connect-content/bundles/python-flaskapi --listen=127.0.0.1:9001 --open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" --skip-browser-session-auth`.
    - This launches the CLI and configures it to listen on port `9001`, while launching a browser to the address which is being served by the `vite` web server.

You now should have a Web UX loaded within the browser, which is loading from the `vite` dev server, but has its APIs serviced from the CLI backend.

## Automated Tests
None.

## Directions for Reviewers

### Setup process
1. Review the code
2. Baseline your built environment by executing `just`. This sample recipe will take longer but does generically do all of the build steps required for a consistent build. They are not called out above as it is expected that a normal development flow will have selective use of the recipes to save time.

### To confirm production mode functionality
1. Execute `just web/dev` to launch the `vite` dev server in one terminal window.
2. Within a new terminal window, launch the development version of the CLI for the current platform (with these parameters): `./connect-client publish-ui <PROJECT_PATH> --listen=127.0.0.1:9001 --open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" --skip-browser-session-auth --help`
3. Confirm that the following lines are shown at the beginning of the output
```
<date/time> level=info msg="Production mode" mode=development
<date/time> level=info msg="Production build" productionBuild=false
```
4. Within the same subdirectory/terminal window, launch the Web UI with the command: `./connect-client publish-ui <PROJECT_PATH> --listen=127.0.0.1:9001 --open-browser-at="http://127.0.0.1:9000" --skip-browser-session-auth`
5. Confirm the browser is launched and the UX is displayed.
6. Confirm that the browser is displaying output from port 9001 rather than 9000.

### To confirm development mode functionality
1. Execute the workflow steps specified above within the approach section.
2. Confirm that the output within the terminal where you launched the CLI shows a message: `level=info msg="Loading rsconnect-python accounts from /Users/billsager/Library/Application Support/rsconnect-python/servers.json"`
3. Confirm that the UX text displayed on the Destination summary displays `Colorado, deploying 'Quarterly Report'`.
4. Modify the vue file `web/src/panels/DestinationTarget.vue` on line 172 from:
```
    return `Colorado, deploying 'Quarterly Report'`;
```
to
```
    return `Washington, deploying 'Quarterly Report'`;
```
5. Save the file
6. Confirm that the browser is displaying this change quickly and automatically without doing anything.
    - This will confirm development workflow as working

## Checklist

title: Create a File Diff prototype component
description:
This PR adds a prototype for a potential file diff view, similar to and inspired by `git status`, when redeploying.

Since this is a prototype meant to illicit design feedback and decisions it implements some of the design, but doesn't interact with other components in all of the publishing panels.

<details>
  <summary>Preview (photo and video)</summary>

![CleanShot 2023-07-21 at 11 52 05](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/8cbaf6fd-30dc-4daf-ae4e-0e2040d2dada)

https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/19917631/d281bcb1-bb61-4049-ac26-66636e22772d

</details> 

## Intent
- Prototype for #43 

## Type of Change
This is a prototype of a new feature.

- [ ] Bug Fix           <!-- A change which fixes an existing issue -->
- [x] New Feature       <!-- A change which adds additional functionality -->
- [ ] Breaking Change   <!-- A breaking change which causes existing functionality to change -->

## Approach
- In the original `DirectoryNode` type we had the concept of `deleted` and `new` but we didn't have the concept of `changed` or `modified` so that was added (still open to the naming here both in the UI and in the TypeScript).
- I created some constants in `directoryContents.ts` to play with (flattening and filtering). There are more optimal ways to traverse here, but we will have a better idea of what we will need to do when the GET and POST APIs are constructed.
- I attempted to only use Quasar and use its recommended components for this type of view.
- To make the icon checkboxes different I used the custom icon feature of Quasar and started using Material Icons. We can definitely change these, but Material felt like the best match for the UI Quasar creates, and is there first recommended.
  - This does mean that the inputs are hidden and are using non-standard checkboxes - which is why they look different to the checkboxes in the QTree.

## Directions for Reviewers
To take a look at this prototype:
- Run `just web/dev` to startup the local development UI
- Open the "Files" panel and click "Simulate redeployment view"

title: UX Prototype Split into Components
description:
## Intent

This code migrates the current state of the UX prototype onto the Quasar stack. It also includes refactoring the monolithic component into multiple components which should allow parallelism as we move forward with the prototype.

## Approach

The `layouts/MainLayout.vue` component presents the main view and is responsible for displaying panels. These panels currently correspond with the topics shown within a vertical expander on a 1:1 basis, as well as some of the publishing flow feedback.

![2023-07-18 at 11 44 AM](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/9946151c-777a-4788-963b-a44378c61a7f)

- `web/src/panels/CommonSettings.vue`

The intention here is that multiple developers will be able to work in parallel on the panels, without having to coordinate too much with each other.

title: UX Quasar Tool Stack Updates
description:
## Intent

This PR modifies the project and build chain to use the toolchain selected for the Web UX (as indicated in issue #25). Please note that `pnpm` could not be used due to architectural limitations of `pnpm` when using docker containers of different architectures.

Fixes #32 

The objective of this PR is to simply be able to provide useful justfile recipes to perform the development tasks we anticipate and make these as functional as possible. An actual skeleton has been created for the UX as well as a few sample tests (both unit and e2e). It is anticipated that all of the build chain code included here will change over time. The objective was to simply give us a starting point that we could use as a base moving forward.

## Approach

**NOTE:** This PR includes a lot of code cleanup, which could be very laborious to walk through. The prior project implemented a previous UX stack, which was replaced in place by the new stack and skeleton Web UX project. I would recommend that reviewers mostly ignore the deleted files and perhaps even ignore some of the diffs. It may be more productive to focus review in a practical sense by running the commands or examining the key files related to the build. The skeleton new SPA app will receive further changes shortly in an upcoming PR, as we start applying code that was already written as part of the exploratory UX work.

README.md's have been updated to now include installation instructions for builds.

Justfiles were modified in both the base and the updated `web` subdirectory, with new and modified recipes. These recipes implemented optional docker container execution for the Web UX code from the base `justfile`, while maintaining the ability to execute the optimal development experience from within the `web` directory's `justfile`.

The resulting recipes (with documentation) available from the base project's `justfile` are:
```
Available recipes:
build            -- Args: # Build both the web UX and server for production usage
build-dev        -- Args: # Build the production web UX and the development server
certs            -- Args: # create the security certificates
clean            -- Args: # Clean the server and web UX build artifacts as well as remove all web UX dependency packages.
default          -- Args: # install, lint, build and test server & client (pre-run 'clean' if switching between use of DOCKER cont
go-coverage      -- Args: # Profile the test code coverage of the Go code
image            -- Args: # Build the image. Typically does not need to be done very often.
install          -- Args: # Install any supporting packages (such as web UX javascript/typescript dependencies)
lint             -- Args: # Lint the server and the web UX source code, along with checking for copyrights. See the `post-build-li
lint-fix         -- Args: # Lint and FIX automatically correctable issues. See the `lint` recipe for linting without fixing.
post-build-lint  -- Args: # Lint step which requires the code to be built first. Normally want to lint prior to building.
run              -- Args: *args       # Run the publishing client executable
test             -- Args: # Run all tests (unit and e2e) on the publishing client as well as web UX
test-backend     -- Args: # Run the tests on the publishing client w/ coverage profiling
web              -- Args: # Build the web UX from scratch, lint and test
```

The resulting recipes (with documentation) available from the `web` project's `justfile` are:
```
Available recipes:
build            -- Args: # build the web artifacts for the SPA (into dest/spa)
clean            -- Args: # remove build artifacts and dependencies
default          -- Args: # will run recipes: install, lint, build, and test
dev              -- Args: # start common UX development flow. Runs install recipe ahead of starting the web server which updates a
install          -- Args: # update javascript/typescript dependencies
lint             -- Args: # lint the source files, do not fix the fixable items
lint-fix         -- Args: # lint the source files, fix the fixable items
test             -- Args: # perform unit and e2e tests
test-e2e         -- Args: # run e2e (Cypress) tests
test-unit        -- Args: # run unit tests one time
test-unit-watch  -- Args: # run unit tests in watch mode, re-running as files are changed
```

The setup of the new web project as well as the build steps follow the path established as best practice for a Quasar app. Their CLI was used to generate a skeleton after we provided the CLI with the technology stack choices we were targeting. Several of these are not yet in use within the skeleton, other than setting up, but that will be remedied shortly within upcoming PRs.

## Automated Testing

CI has been modified as part of these changes. If successful, it should pass the checks.

## Manual Testing

NOTE: There is a difference of architectures involved when running in docker mode ($DOCKER not set or set to "true") or when running in native mode (otherwise), particularly within the javascript dependencies compiled as part of the `npm install` process. Switching between modes requires a re-installation of the dependencies to avoid some weird runtime messages. The easiest way to do this is to run the recipe `just clean` at either the top of the project or from within the web subdirectory. Verification of this PR needs to include both environments, so the steps listed below include this.

Steps 1-4 validate the execution of justfile recipes within a docker container.
Steps 5-8 validate the native execution of the recipes.

1. `unset DOCKER`
2. `just image` - build the docker image
3. `just clean` - validate successful cleaning
4. `just` - validate that its sequence is successful and docker containers are used
5. `export DOCKER="false"`
6. `just clean` - validate successful cleaning (required because of change of architectures)
7. `just` - validate that its sequence is successful and docker containers are not used
8. `just web/test-unit-watch` - validate that it runs and waits for changes. Note this is not tested or available within the docker container environment at this time.

* GitHub actions workflow updates to run all platforms (windows-amd64, macos-amd64, linux-amd64, linux-arm64) in GHA on pull requests

Fixes: #27

title: Consolidate FS path handling
description:
PR #12 introduced the use of the `afero.Fs` interface for all filesystem access. This makes it possible to use mocks, in-memory filesystems, etc. for testing. Currently, we pass the path and Fs everywhere they are needed.

This PR introduces a utility struct `util.Path` that contains the Fs and path together. It also proxies the relevant Fs methods so you can directly use, for example, `path.Create()`.

title: Add jupyter notebook extension
description:
The easiest way to install this for now is:

```
git clone https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client.git
cd publishing-client/extensions/jupyter-notebook
pip install .
python -m jupyter nbextension install --sys-prefix --py connect_publishing
python -m jupyter nbextension enable connect_publishing --py --sys-prefix
```

Outstanding questions/TODO:

- [ ] Should the extension spawn the UI?
- [ ] Reading in stdout (implementation partially dependent upon ⏫ )
- [ ] Name of package? Currently `connect_publishing`
- [ ] Should this package include the binary?
- [ ] Should it have a package docs site? Is README enough for now?
- [ ] Should testing be mocking or something including Selenium?

title: Cleanup
description:
This PR cleans up a few things:
* Adds some missing unit tests
* Updates go to 1.20.4
* Cleans up some of the `kong` struct tags

title: State storage
description:
This PR implements an in-memory state store that is the source of truth for what will be deployed. It's populated by optionally loading a saved state from the deployment directory (under `.posit/deployments/{name}`), then is populated with CLI arguments, and applied during publishing.

Current state:
* The server and content IDs are saved in `id.json`, but redeployment is not yet supported (a new content item is always created).
* The Connect create-content API call parameters are saved in `content.json`. They can be provided on the command line (e.g. runtime settings, application title, etc). They are saved and will be applied the next time you publish.
* Parameters that live in the manifest can be provided (e.g. `--python-version 3.10.4`) and they take effect during publishing, but they are not saved/restored yet. We need to think through the relationship between `manifest.json` (if provided) and the saved metadata files.
* The state store doesn't expose an API for the UI to talk to yet.

The new code in this PR needs more tests before merging.

title: App mode detection
description:
This PR adds support for specifying the AppMode and Entrypoint, or having them automatically detected. Along with this are the Python version and package dependencies.

This is a fairly large PR. It includes new and/or updated unit tests for the bulk of the new code.

With this, it should be possible to use the `publish` and `create-bundle` commands like
```
connect-client publish -n myserver ../connect/test/rsconnect-python/bundles-manifest/streamlit
connect-client create-bundle --bundle-file ../bundle1.tar.gz ../connect/test/rsconnect-python/bundles-manifest/streamlit-env
```

You can specify `--python-version` on the command like and provide a requirements.txt to avoid automatic Python version/dependency detection. If you don't, you can specify `--python` to provide a specific python executable to pull version and dependencies from. Otherwise, it runs `python3` from PATH and hopes for the best.

Note that the test example directory above has variants with/without manifests and with/without requirements.txt files.

title: Enable just building
description: Update the justfile to enable a build-only cycle that builds the UI and a platform-native binary. The current `just build` target take a long time since it runs lint and tests.

title: mention exporting DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM
description: For developer quality of life (read: so people don't make the same mistakes as me 😄), I added a small bit to the README to mention exporting the correct Docker platform.

title: Add unit tests
description:
This (large, sorry) PR adds unit tests for much of the codebase. I was working in a prototyping mode previously to start understanding the landscape a bit, and this is a first cut at firming up the code. Significant changes here include:
* Interfaces to help with testability
* Added `testify` mocks
* Introduced the use of `afero.Fs` wherever possible to make the filesystem code more testable.

There's still a fair amount of work to do in testing and commenting. I put off testing in `cmd/` because I expect that to change quite a bit as we introduce a more complete data handling system that enables pure-CLI, UI-based, and hybrid user interactions.

title: Adds GitHub Actions
description: Adds GitHub actions which trigger on pull requests and pushes to main.

title: Adds a simple README file.
description: Adds a barebones README file outlining the essential commands for project development.

title: Moves the 'vendor' module to the project root.
description: Moves the 'vendor' module from the './internal' directory to the project root.

title: Moves the 'cmd' package to the project root.
description: Moves the 'cmd' package from the './internal' directory to the project root. In addition, the 'just build' command has been extrapolated into a 'just _build' command, which allows developers to run builds without the 'just web/build' dependency.

title: Refactors Justfile and adds Docker support
description:
Adds the `{{ _with_runner }}` variable, which conditionally executes the `build` and `test` targets within a Docker container.

I also refactored the `build` command to build all image versions by default. I pulled all available OS/ARCH combinations from the Go documentation but only uncommented the existing builds.

title: Refactors project structure to use "internal" and "web" directories.
description:
The bulk of this change consists of moving Go source from './src/connect-client' to './internal'. 

In addition, this change... 
- Refactors the build process and embed-linking to point directly to compiled assets in `./web/dist/` (via `web/web.go`) instead of copying to `./internal/services/ui/static`.
- Renames local imports from `import connect-client` to `import github.com/rstudio/connect-client`.
- Adds `./web/README.md` with module-specific instructions.
- Adds `vitest` unit testing to `web`.
- Updates `./web/Justfile`.
- Updates `Justfile`.

title: Upgrades web application to Vue 3
description:
This change upgrades Vue from version 2 to version 3. Which, cascades into many more upgrades for various dependencies and tooling:

- `vue v2` -> `vue v3` guide: https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/
- `vue-cli-service` -> `vetify` guide: https://vueschool.io/articles/vuejs-tutorials/how-to-migrate-from-vue-cli-to-vite/
- `vuetify` guide: https://vuetifyjs.com/en/getting-started/upgrade-guide/

I haven't gone through the Vue migration guide in great detail. But, I have made minor changes as necessary based on application logs. The application should still work as expected.

Also, based on the following recommendations, the web application is relocated from `./ui` to `./web` https://github.com/golang-standards/project-layout.

title: fix(mock-connect): Add newly required spec fields to Connect fixtures
description:
## Problem

The `connect-contract-tests / validate-fixtures` job is failing on **every** PR, including PRs that don't touch mock Connect at all.

This is spec drift, not a code bug. `openapi-helpers.ts` fetches the live published spec from `https://docs.posit.co/connect/api/openapi.json` on every run (the 24h `.cache/` is neither committed nor persisted in CI), so CI always validates against whatever the current spec says. The spec recently marked a batch of new fields `required`, and our fixtures predate them.

8 failures — 4 endpoints × 2 test files:

| Endpoint | Fixture |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/content` | `content-create.json` |
| `GET /v1/content/{guid}` | `content-details.json` |
| `POST /v1/content/{guid}/bundles` | `bundle-upload.json` |
| `GET /v1/oauth/integrations` | `integrations.json` |

## Fix

Added every newly-required field to the four fixtures, using plausible values that match the spec's declared types (nullable fields default to `null`; the fixture content is a Python FastAPI app, so `py_environment_management: true`).

- **content** (`content-create.json`, `content-details.json`): `cpu_request`, `cpu_limit`, `memory_request`, `memory_limit`, `amd_gpu_limit`, `nvidia_gpu_limit`, `service_account_name`, `default_image_name`, `default_environment_guid`, `default_r_environment_management`, `default_py_environment_management`, `environment_guid`, `r_environment_management`, `py_environment_management`, `node_version`, `locked_message`, `draft_marker_enabled`, `metrics_collection_enabled`, `notify_on_share`, `otel_enabled`, `public_content_status` (plus `locked` on `content-create.json`, which already existed on `content-details.json`)
- **bundles**: `created_by`, `created_by_name`, `created_by_user`, `environment_guid`, `py_environment_management`, `r_environment_management`
- **integrations**: `id`, `permissions`, `updated_time`

`mock-connect-server.ts` serves these fixtures directly via `loadFixture()` rather than constructing responses separately, so no server changes were needed — fixing the fixtures fixes both `validate-fixtures.test.ts` and `validate-mock-server.test.ts`.

New fields are inserted at logical positions within the existing field ordering to keep the diff readable. `created_by`/`created_by_name` reuse the guid and username from `user.json` so the fixtures stay internally consistent.

## Recommended follow-up: pin the spec

**This PR unblocks CI but does not make the check deterministic.** The next time the published spec adds a required field, this job will break on every open PR again.

Recommended follow-up: commit a snapshot of the spec (e.g. `test/mock-connect/fixtures/openapi.json`), have `openapi-helpers.ts` read the pinned copy by default, and add an explicit refresh path (an `npm run refresh-spec` script, and/or a scheduled workflow that opens a PR when the upstream spec changes). That turns spec drift into a single intentional PR that updates the snapshot and fixtures together, instead of a surprise failure on unrelated work.

That was intentionally left out of scope here to keep this PR small and reviewable as an unblock.

## Testing

```
just validate-fixtures       # 32 passed | 6 skipped  (was 8 failed)
just test-connect-contracts  # 69 passed
just test-extension-contracts # 72 passed
just check-format            # clean
```

`validate-fixtures` was also re-run with `.cache/` deleted, to confirm it passes against a freshly fetched live spec rather than a stale local cache.

## Notes

- Test infra only — no CHANGELOG entry per repo conventions (not user-facing).
- Diff is limited to `test/mock-connect/fixtures/connect-responses/`; no source, CI, or lockfile changes.

title: feat(llm): expose agent deploy tools via vscode.lm and Positron commands
description:
## Summary

Adds tooling so an AI agent (Positron Assistant, GitHub Copilot, and other tool-capable chat clients) can inspect a project, confirm a deployment plan with the user, and deploy it to Posit Connect / Connect Cloud end-to-end — secrets never enter tool arguments or model context.

- **`planDeployment`** (read-only) — inspects a project directory: content-type/entrypoint candidates, interpreter defaults, existing configs/records, and available credentials (redacted — name/url/serverType only).
- **`deployContent`** (write + deploy) — creates a config + deployment record if none exist, runs the real deploy, and returns a structured status (`success | needs-credential | needs-content-type | failed`).
- **`addCredential`** (initiate-only) — opens the interactive New Credential UI so the user enters the API key / completes OAuth themselves; optionally accepts a `serverUrl` to pre-fill the URL field (not a secret).

Each tool is exposed **two ways** for host compatibility:
1. As `vscode.lm` `LanguageModelTool`s (tagged `positron-assistant`) — works today in any host that forwards these.
2. As agent-compatible VSCode commands (`posit.publisher.agent.*`) declared via `contributes.commands[].agent`, landing in Positron's `positron.ai` allow-list. Both upstream blockers for this path (`posit-dev/positron#15077`, `posit-dev/assistant#1810`) have since merged.

**Enabling refactor:** `runDeployWithProgress` and `HomeViewProvider.initiateDeployment` now return a structured `DeployOutcome` (`success | failed | canceled`) instead of `void`, so the deploy tool can report real status back to the agent. A new `deployProject()` selects the target in the sidebar before deploying so the user watches progress on it.

Tracking issue: posit-dev/publisher#4305

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] ESLint clean on all changed source
- [x] Unit tests: `planDeploymentTool`, `deployContentTool`, `addCredentialTool`, `deployProgress`, `homeViewSelectDeployment` — all passing
- [x] `just test-extension-contracts` — 81/81 passing (registration + positional-arg → `run()` mapping for both exposure paths)
- [x] Rebased onto latest `main` (picks up the OAuth authentication work, #4314); resolved conflicts preserving both the new `DeployOutcome` return type and the OAuth re-auth retry path
- [ ] Manual end-to-end verification in a chat client that forwards Publisher's `positron-assistant`-tagged tools (plan → confirm → deploy; needs-credential → addCredential path)

title: chore(deps): bump the test-data-dependencies group across 1 directory with 3 updates
description:
Bumps the test-data-dependencies group with 3 updates in the /test/e2e/content-workspace/examples-shiny-python directory: [shiny](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny), [pandas](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas) and [scipy](https://github.com/scipy/scipy). Updates `shiny` from 1.6.3 to 1.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from shiny's releases.

shiny 1.7.0

New features

  • Added test mode, enabled via the SHINY_TESTMODE=1 environment variable or the App(test_mode=) argument (which defaults to that env var). The pytest app-launch fixtures (local_app, create_app_fixture) now run apps in test mode. (#2269)

  • When test mode is enabled, each session serves a JSON snapshot of its input, output, and export values at /session/{id}/dataobj/shinytest (URL available via session.get_test_snapshot_url()). App authors can surface internal reactive values with shiny.testmode.export_test_values(). The endpoint honors query params input/output/export to select specific blocks (=1 for a whole block, or a comma-separated list of keys); unlike R, requesting no blocks returns all three rather than a 400. (#2269)

  • input.set_snapshot_preprocess(id, fn) (or shiny.testmode.snapshot_preprocess_input()) and my_output.snapshot_preprocess(fn) preprocess test-mode snapshot values before they are written, e.g. to scrub timestamps or temp paths. Handlers may be synchronous or asynchronous. File inputs automatically scrub each file's datapath to its basename, matching Shiny for R. export_test_values() moved from shiny.session to the new shiny.testmode module. (#2282)

  • shiny.playwright.controller.AppTestValues reads a session's test-mode snapshot (input/output/export) in end-to-end tests. Its expect methods accept predicates: pass any callable (e.g. app_values.expect_input("n", is_integer)) in place of an expected value, and the expectation retries until the predicate returns a truthy value. (#2269, #2357)

  • offcanvas() creates sliding Bootstrap Offcanvas panels that appear from a viewport edge. Panels can be triggered by a UI element, revealed programmatically with show_offcanvas(), or controlled by id with hide_offcanvas() and toggle_offcanvas(). (#2279)

  • @render.download_button and @render.download_link pair 1:1 with ui.download_button() and ui.download_link(). (#2364)

  • The shiny package now ships bundled Agent Skills under shiny/.agents/skills/ (the library-skills convention): a single shiny-for-python skill whose SKILL.md is a grouped index that routes coding agents to a per-topic reference file for each of shiny's public APIs. (#2339, #2344, #2345, #2356, #2365, #2366)

    • Foundations: reactivity (the reactive graph — reactive.value/calc/effect/event, req, isolate, poll), express (Express mode), modules-core / modules-express (reusable namespaced components), and session-lifecycle (on_ended/on_flush, request info, dynamic routes).
    • Layout and navigation: layouts (pages, cards, sidebars, columns, value boxes), navigation (navsets and page_navbar), dynamic-ui (@render.ui, update_*, insert_ui, panel_conditional), and theming (ui.Theme, presets, dark mode).
    • Outputs and rendering: plots (render.plot/render.image and interactions), data-frames (render.data_frame), and files (upload/download).
    • Feedback and interactivity: feedback (notifications, modals, progress, busy indicators), extended-tasks (non-blocking long-running work), and bookmarking (save/restore app state with bookmark_store= and session.bookmark hooks).
    • Generative AI: chat (ui.Chat) and markdown-streaming (ui.MarkdownStream).
    • Extending shiny: custom-renderers (authoring a Renderer subclass) and custom-components (custom JavaScript input/output bindings).
    • Testing and observability: testing (end-to-end tests with pytest and Playwright), debugging (inspect running apps via test mode), and otel (OpenTelemetry observability).

  • shiny skills list shows each bundled skill's name and description, and shiny skills path <name> prints the skill's directory, so its SKILL.md and supporting files (references/, scripts/) can be read from the installed package. To install the skills into a coding agent, the README and the shiny skills CLI help now point at library-skills (uvx library-skills --claude). (#2340, #2367)

Improvements

  • The shiny[otel] optional dependency group now includes opentelemetry-distro[otlp], so OpenTelemetry zero-code auto-instrumentation works out of the box: opentelemetry-instrument shiny run app.py. This is now the documented standard way to enable OpenTelemetry — the docs and the examples/open-telemetry/ example no longer configure providers inside the app (in-code set_tracer_provider() setup is silently ignored when a provider is already installed, e.g. under opentelemetry-instrument). The OTLP exporters are also included, making it easy to switch between gRPC and HTTP export via standard OTEL_* environment variables. Note that opentelemetry-distro pins opentelemetry-sdk to a matching minor version, so if you combine shiny[otel] with other packages that pin the OpenTelemetry SDK (e.g. logfire), the resolver may need matching versions. (#2349)

  • The Playwright controllers DownloadButton and DownloadLink now share a common base class and gain expect_label(), and DownloadLink gains the width expectations previously available only on DownloadButton. (#2093)

  • OutputDataFrame.set_filter() now supports multi-column filters. (#2093)

Deprecations

Release notes

Sourced from scipy's releases.

SciPy 1.18.0 Release Notes

SciPy 1.18.0 is the culmination of 6 months of hard work. It contains many new features, numerous bug-fixes, improved test coverage and better documentation. There have been a number of deprecations and API changes in this release, which are documented below. All users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, as there are a large number of bug-fixes and optimizations. Before upgrading, we recommend that users check that their own code does not use deprecated SciPy functionality (to do so, run your code with python -Wd and check for DeprecationWarning s). Our development attention will now shift to bug-fix releases on the 1.18.x branch, and on adding new features on the main branch.

This release requires Python 3.12-3.14 and NumPy 2.0.0 or greater.

Highlights of this release

  • SciPy now supports three different build modes for BLAS and LAPACK LP64/ILP64 support, and machinery is provided for downstream cython_lapack consumers to gracefully handle LP64/ILP64 backend builds. ILP64 support has been substantially improved across the SciPy library.
  • Remaining Fortran to C translations have been completed---an experimental Fortran-free build option is now available to developers for testing purposes. Developer feedback is welcome on Fortran-free builds.
  • scipy.signal.whittaker_henderson now provides access to Whittaker-Henderson smoothing of a discrete signal.
  • A large number of scipy.stats functions now support lazy arrays and JAX JIT. Array API support has been improved substantially in SciPy, with at least 21 functions gaining new support in this release. 16 scipy.stats functions have also gained support for MArray input.

New features

scipy.fft improvements

  • SciPy's internal FFT backend has switched from pocketfft to its successor package ducc0.fft, which features several incremental improvements. The most significant of those from SciPy's perspective is probably that storage requirements for internally cached plans have been significantly reduced for most long 1D transforms. Plans that require more storage than 1MB will no longer be cached; this mainly affects huge 1D transforms of prime and near-prime sizes.

scipy.interpolate improvements

    • Extending shiny: custom-renderers (authoring a Renderer subclass) and custom-components (custom JavaScript input/output bindings).
    • Testing and observability: testing (end-to-end tests with pytest and Playwright), debugging (inspect running apps via test mode), and otel (OpenTelemetry observability).

  • shiny skills list shows each bundled skill's name and description, and shiny skills path <name> prints the skill's directory, so its SKILL.md and supporting files (references/, scripts/) can be read from the installed package. To install the skills into a coding agent, the README and the shiny skills CLI help now point at library-skills (uvx library-skills --claude). (#2340, #2367)

Improvements

  • The shiny[otel] optional dependency group now includes opentelemetry-distro[otlp], so OpenTelemetry zero-code auto-instrumentation works out of the box: opentelemetry-instrument shiny run app.py. This is now the documented standard way to enable OpenTelemetry — the docs and the examples/open-telemetry/ example no longer configure providers inside the app (in-code set_tracer_provider() setup is silently ignored when a provider is already installed, e.g. under opentelemetry-instrument). The OTLP exporters are also included, making it easy to switch between gRPC and HTTP export via standard OTEL_* environment variables. Note that opentelemetry-distro pins opentelemetry-sdk to a matching minor version, so if you combine shiny[otel] with other packages that pin the OpenTelemetry SDK (e.g. logfire), the resolver may need matching versions. (#2349)

  • The Playwright controllers DownloadButton and DownloadLink now share a common base class and gain expect_label(), and DownloadLink gains the width expectations previously available only on DownloadButton. (#2093)

  • OutputDataFrame.set_filter() now supports multi-column filters. (#2093)

Deprecations

  • @render.download is deprecated; use @render.download_button (or @render.download_link) instead. (#2364)

Bug fixes

  • Fixed rare tabset ID collisions in pages with many navsets. Randomly generated data-tabsetid values were drawn from a pool of ~1 million, so a page with dozens of tabsets could occasionally produce two navsets with the same ID (a birthday collision), resulting in duplicate DOM ids and broken tab switching. IDs are now drawn from a pool of 9 trillion. (#2296)

  • shiny run --launch-browser now opens the browser even when Uvicorn's INFO-level startup logs are unavailable, e.g. when logs are disabled or --log-level=warning is used. (#569)

  • InputSlider.set() and InputSliderRange.set() now compute the target value's position from the slider's step configuration and drag the handle directly to it, verifying the landing position against the widget's state (finishing with arrow-key presses when the slider has more steps than the track has pixels). Previously the handle was swept one pixel at a time while polling the label, which was slow and could intermittently miss the target when the browser coalesced or dropped mouse-move events (a recurring webkit CI flake). InputSliderRange.set() orders the two handle moves so neither is clamped by its sibling, instead of parking both handles at their extremes first. Setting a value the slider cannot produce now raises an error listing the slider's actual values. (#2311, #2326)

  • ui.output_data_frame() now consistently orders the filtered columns in ascending column order (#2093), and resetting a numeric range filter resets both values (#2093).

  • value_box()'s id docstring now documents input.<id>_full_screen() for observing the value box's full screen state, matching card(). It previously documented the wrong reactive-value syntax, input.<id>()["full_screen"]. (#2324)

SciPy 1.18.0 Release Notes

SciPy 1.18.0 is the culmination of 6 months of hard work. It contains many new features, numerous bug-fixes, improved test coverage and better documentation. There have been a number of deprecations and API changes in this release, which are documented below. All users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, as there are a large number of bug-fixes and optimizations. Before upgrading, we recommend that users check that their own code does not use deprecated SciPy functionality (to do so, run your code with python -Wd and check for DeprecationWarning s). Our development attention will now shift to bug-fix releases on the 1.18.x branch, and on adding new features on the main branch.

This release requires Python 3.12-3.14 and NumPy 2.0.0 or greater.

Highlights of this release

  • SciPy now supports three different build modes for BLAS and LAPACK LP64/ILP64 support, and machinery is provided for downstream cython_lapack consumers to gracefully handle LP64/ILP64 backend builds. ILP64 support has been substantially improved across the SciPy library.
  • Remaining Fortran to C translations have been completed---an experimental Fortran-free build option is now available to developers for testing purposes. Developer feedback is welcome on Fortran-free builds.
  • scipy.signal.whittaker_henderson now provides access to Whittaker-Henderson smoothing of a discrete signal.
  • A large number of scipy.stats functions now support lazy arrays and JAX JIT. Array API support has been improved substantially in SciPy, with at least 21 functions gaining new support in this release. 16 scipy.stats functions have also gained support for MArray input.

New features

scipy.fft improvements

  • SciPy's internal FFT backend has switched from pocketfft to its successor package ducc0.fft, which features several incremental improvements. The most significant of those from SciPy's perspective is probably that storage requirements for internally cached plans have been significantly reduced for most long 1D transforms. Plans that require more storage than 1MB will no longer be cached; this mainly affects huge 1D transforms of prime and near-prime sizes.

Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.3.0

Minor Changes

  • #1825 16b3f74 - It is now possible to run multiple tasks in parallel for a single glob by configuring it with an array of tasks (which run sequentially), and then placing another array inside it (where the tasks will run in parallel). The following demonstrates the order tasks will start in:

    {
  "*.ts": ["first", "second", ["third", "third"], "fourth"]
}

    As a concrete example, lint-staged's own configuration is:

    /** @type {import('./lib/index.js').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*": [
    [
      "oxfmt --check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern",
      "oxlint --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern",
    ],
  ],
  "*.ts": () => "tsc",
};

    which means:

    1. for all staged files, run the two commands in parallel with staged filenames appended, for example:
      • oxfmt --check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern lib/index.js
      • oxlint --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern lib/index.js
    2. additionally, if any *.ts files are staged, run tsc without appending any arguments
    3. The two sets of commands also run in parallel

Patch Changes

  • #1829 15f7e53 - During an in-progress merge, files that are unchanged from the branch being merged are now skipped. Technically, files are only included if there are staged changes against both HEAD and MERGE_HEAD.

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.19.0 - July 22, 2026

This release raises the form-data security floor, adds configuration and type-system capabilities, and fixes NO_PROXY matching, interceptor errors, progress reporting, and serialization edge cases.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Multipart Form Data: Raised the form-data dependency floor to ^4.0.6, preventing fresh installations from resolving versions affected by the CRLF injection vulnerability GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx). (#11028)

🚀 New Features

  • Configuration Extensibility: Preserved own-enumerable symbol-keyed fields through mergeConfig and added a generic params type across public TypeScript declarations, responses, errors, adapters, and serializers. (#11043, #11081)
  • Header Parameter Parsing: Added the opt-in AxiosHeaders.parseParameters() parser for quote-aware, RFC-style HTTP parameter parsing while preserving legacy parsing behavior. (#11051)
  • HTTP Status Codes: Added the missing Cloudflare 520 WebServerReturnsAnUnknownError status and matching ESM/CJS declarations. (#11067)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Form Data Conversion: Limited formDataToJSON path splitting to dot and bracket notation, preserving literal punctuation in keys, and removed browser-facing Buffer.from usage from toFormData to avoid unnecessary polyfills. (#11006, #11018)
  • Proxy Bypass: Canonicalized IPv4 shorthand, octal, and hexadecimal forms during NO_PROXY matching and honored * entries within comma- or space-separated bypass lists. (#11029, #11053)
  • Cancellation: Propagated already-aborted input signals immediately when composing abort signals. (#11035)
  • Header Handling: Preserved empty first values for duplicate singleton headers and made AxiosHeaders#getSetCookie() consistently return arrays for present values. (#11036, #11037)
  • URL Handling: Included normalized, safely redacted offending URLs in malformed-protocol errors and removed repeated trailing slashes when combining base URLs. (#11024, #11038)
  • Progress Events: Clamped malformed negative progress values to zero and ensured final Node.js download progress events are delivered before streamed responses close. (#11039, #11040)
  • Error and JSON Serialization: Serialized Set values as arrays in JSON-compatible snapshots and synthesized useful AxiosError messages from otherwise-empty AggregateError instances. (#11044, #11059)
  • Content-Length Enforcement: Corrected base64 data: URL size estimation so maxContentLength is enforced consistently by the HTTP and Fetch adapters. (#11061)
  • Synchronous Interceptors: Prevented requests from being dispatched after synchronous request interceptors fail unless their paired rejection handler resolves successfully. (#11071)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Dependencies: Updated development and test tooling, the docs fixture's Axios version, and GitHub Actions integrations including Checkout, Setup Node, Setup Deno, and Zizmor. (#11031, #11055, #11056, #11058, #11079, #11080, #11088, #11089, #11090)
  • Build Outputs: Limited sourcemap generation to published minified bundles, removing broken map references from non-minified builds. (#11054)
  • Form Data Internals: Centralized FormData header handling and made the Node.js adapter tolerate getHeaders() returning undefined under the content-only policy. (#11062)
  • Developer Experience: Ignored common local AI-tooling directories and fixed a constant-reassignment crash when the development sandbox serves its root path. (#11032, #11073)
  • Documentation: Updated sponsor information, clarified that baseURL is not a path-security boundary, scoped provenance claims to attested releases, and corrected the configuration-defaults documentation. (#11041, #11068, #11076, #11078)
  • Publishing: Simplified v1 publishing to use the npm version bundled with Node.js 26 and updated package metadata for the 1.19.0 release. (#11083, #11095)
